# LightX2V 昨日提交分析（9fd3d98）

## 1. 主要更新类型
- **功能新增（feature）**：为 InfiniteTalk 视频生成功能新增了一种面向特定硬件的推理变体，属于模型配置/部署能力的扩展，无涉及 Bug 修复或文档更新。

## 2. 关键变更点及与项目整体方向的关系
- **变更核心**：新增 "4090D SLA0.6 BF16 SP" 变体，即针对 NVIDIA RTX 4090D 显卡，在 SLA 0.6（服务等级目标约 0.6 的延迟/吞吐指标）约束下，采用 BF16 混合精度与 SP（单进程/单卡轻量部署）策略的 InfiniteTalk 推理配置。
- **契合项目定位**：LightX2V 的核心目标是"轻量级视频生成推理"，该提交正是将这一目标落地——通过针对消费级/准专业级显卡（4090D）的专门优化配置，降低硬件门槛并保证明确的时延承诺（SLA），与框架追求的高性价比、易部署方向完全一致。
- **扩展覆盖场景**：InfiniteTalk 是框架内的重要长视频/对话驱动生成能力，为其补充新变体意味着扩大该能力在实际生产环境中的可用硬件矩阵。

## 3. 对项目的影响和潜在意义
- **用户价值**：使 4090D 用户（尤其国内市场常见的合规降频版本）可以直接选用经过验证的配置，无需自行调试精度与进程模式，开箱即得满足 SLA 0.6 的推理表现。
- **生态意义**：体现项目正在从"能跑"走向"可承诺性能指标"的工程化成熟阶段，SLA 化的变体命名有利于企业用户评估选型。
- **潜在风险**：变体数量增加会带来配置维护成本，后续需关注该变体与模型更新的兼容性同步。

## 4. 值得关注的技术点
- **BF16 精度选择**：在 4090D 上用 BF16 替代 FP16/FP32，兼顾吞吐与数值稳定，是推理优化的典型做法。
- **SLA 量化指标**：将性能目标写入变体命名，说明团队建立了可复现的基准测试流程，这是推理框架走向标准化的重要信号。
- **硬件特化调优**：针对 4090D（相对 4090 的显存/功耗差异）单独出配置，反映框架具备细粒度硬件适配能力，而非笼统的通用配置。

## 5. 基于 README 背景对项目发展的影响
- README 显示 LightX2V 定位为轻量视频生成推理框架，配套完整中英文文档与 Apache 2.0 开源协议，已具备面向广泛用户群的产品化雏形。本提交通过新增硬件特化变体，直接强化了"轻量"这一品牌主张在具体显卡上的可验证性，使文档中的性能承诺有配置支撑。
- 这类持续累积的变体提交，有助于项目构建覆盖主流 GPU 的预置配置库，降低新用户上手成本，从而推动社区采用与生态扩张，与其国际化文档布局相辅相成，共同支撑项目从研究型框架向生产级推理基础设施演进的长期路线。

## AI分析总结

# FlashInfer 昨日提交综合分析

## 一、主要更新
本日工作以**性能优化为绝对主体**，辅以训练 API 命名规范化、新硬件适配、健壮性修复与工程基建。性能方面横跨 Cake 系列内核：FMHA、分组/FP8/NVFP4 GEMM、MegaMoE、RMSNorm-SiLU-Gate、DSA indexer、KDA prefill、VSA 稀疏注意力、DSv4 稀疏 MLA、GDN、causal conv1d、MLA value gate、ExpCast 注意力、MSA 索引器等持续提速；硬件覆盖 sm_100a（B200）、sm_103a（GB300）、sm_107a（VR200/Rubin）、sm_120 与 RTX 5090，并新增 Rubin CuTe DSL prefill 后端、Kimi K3 MegaMoE 后端、SM100/103 HyperConnection sum-state 后端、sm_90a 融合 GEMM+all-reduce 与 batch-invariant MXFP8 GEMM。

## 二、关键变更
**API 规范化（#8928 系列）**：训练入口统一为 `flashinfer.cake_<op>_<det|nondet>_train`，删除 `deterministic=` 关键字与旧名别名，后端迁入 `experimental/cake/`，配套迁移表文档与 `_LAZY_EXPORTS` 懒导出机制，`import flashinfer` 不再加载后端，并以 `sys.modules` 反射检测、containment 测试与 CI 防线保障包独立性。

**性能策略**：以 AOT 程序替代 JIT，按硬件与形状精确路由——FMHA 新增 45 个 runtime-size 程序族，KDA prefill 借 TMEM 双槽预载把 kernel 由 5 个减至 2 个、延迟约降 2 倍；加载与计算重叠（K_scale 提前一 tile、UE8M0 每 4 个 K block 预取）、host 端调度表逐架构调参、radix-select 扫描融合、PDL 与 8 行 tile 配合、L2 显式 EVICT 控制。

**修复与精度**：修复 MegaMoE 异步代理竞争（`fence.proxy.async.global`）、GDN 确定性训练非法内存访问、KDA GLM 门梯度 TF32 舍入、Mamba FP8 scale 越界、MoE EP 空批次崩溃、CUDA 13.0 量化回退与 Windows arm64 构建问题；RMSNorm 确定性反向引入 Kahan 补偿，误差从 1.10 倍容差降至 0.79 倍。

## 三、项目影响
破坏性变更集中于训练 API 重命名，下游（如 vLLM）需按迁移表升级，换来明确确定性边界与长期稳定契约。性能收益显著且大多位级一致：B200 上 FMHA 比 JIT 快 1.05–3.2x、比 trtllm-gen 至 4.4x；SM107a 重布局 GEMM 至 1.77x；KDA forward 2.1x；DSA top-k 1.43x；Kimi K3 EP8 提速 1.218x；HC sum-state 几何均值 1.394x。主机路由类改动收益 1%–14% 且零回归风险，项目如实报告 host-bound 天花板与 sm_90a 融合内核略低于基线（0.944x）的取舍，体现诚实的性能文化。batch-invariant GEMM 与确定性双轨制（det/nondet）为可复现训练提供硬指标。

## 四、值得关注的技术点
TMEM 双槽预载与任务状态槽去重；零同步设备侧 scale（编译缓存仅含 scale 种类）；`448/amax` FP8 溢出根因推导；sha256 封闭内核包 fail-closed 分发；ExpCast 用 E4M3 编码 log 域 softmax 省去指数运算；lead-prefetch 表、TMA 越界零填充、共享内存缓存 score key 加 warp radix 直方图；按 heads/page/batch/context 的路由目录机制；严谨基准方法学（A/A 校验、CUDA graph 热重放、L2 flush、CUPTI、Mann-Whitney U 检验、`cuobjdump -sass` 逐指令比对）；务实的优化哲学——主动放弃共享 SM 回退风险的微小收益。

## 五、总体意义
FlashInfer 沿"推理+训练、确定性+非确定性"双轨演进，优化粒度已推进到逐架构、逐形状、逐程序的层面，并通过懒导出、containment 测试与 CI 加固守护工程质量。硬件覆盖面从 B200 扩展至 Rubin 全系，负载面从推理延伸到确定性训练，生态上与 vLLM、SGLang、TRT-LLM、Kimi K3 紧密协同，标志项目进入规范化与精细化并重的成熟阶段，持续巩固其作为多代 NVIDIA 硬件上可信赖生产级内核库的地位。

## 详细提交记录

### [ab63ff3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ab63ff3afd8bbb74fe69ace64de706c4addb54c7)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T23:58:52Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_mhc): name the mHC training modules by their mode: cake_mhc_det_train, cake_mhc_nondet_train, cake_mhc_head_det_train (#8928) (#8907)

Part of #8928. This PR now implements #8928's mHC rows and replaces its
earlier `deterministic=False` scope. The mHC training kernels now share
one naming scheme across three public modules:
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train`, `flashinfer.cake_mhc_nondet_train` and
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_head_det_train`. Each one is a stable top-level
facade over a backend package under `flashinfer/experimental/cake/`. The
module and function names carry the mode, so no entry point takes a
`deterministic` keyword. Former names are removed without aliases, so
downstream code must update its imports (see Migration).

## Modules

- **`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train`**
- Backend: `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_det_train`, moved from
`flashinfer/cake_mhc_det_train_backend`.
- `CakeMHCDetTrain{Prepare,Finish}Function` is renamed to
`CakeMHCDet{Prepare,Finish}Function`.
  - `route_key` is renamed to `cake_mhc_det_train_route_key`.
  - All other function names are unchanged.
- **`flashinfer.cake_mhc_nondet_train`** (new top-level module)
- Backend: `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_nondet_train`, moved
from `flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_mhc_train_backend`.
- Replaces the experimental selector
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train` and its `deterministic=`
keyword.
- Entries: `cake_mhc_nondet_train_{forward_prepare, forward_stats,
forward_finish, backward_prepare, backward_finish, prepare, finish,
forward_workspace_bytes, backward_workspace_bytes, forward_workspace,
backward_workspace, reset_workspace, route_key}`,
`is_cake_mhc_nondet_train_supported`,
`CakeMHCNondet{Prepare,Finish}Function`, `ARCHES`,
`SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES`.
- Uses the same stable API decorator as the deterministic module. It
emits no `ExperimentalWarning`.
- **`flashinfer.cake_mhc_head_det_train`** (split out of the
deterministic module)
- Backend: `flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_head_det_train`, moved
from `flashinfer/cake_mhc_det_train_head_backend`.
- Entries: `cake_mhc_head_det`, `CakeMHCHeadDetFunction`,
`cake_mhc_head_det_train_{forward,backward}`,
`is_cake_mhc_head_det_train_supported`.
- `flashinfer.cake_mhc_head_nondet_train` is reserved for a planned
version. It does not exist yet.
- The top-level `flashinfer` namespace re-exports the deterministic and
head entry points (`cake_mhc_det_train_*`, `cake_mhc_head_det`,
`cake_mhc_head_det_train_{forward,backward}`), and
`CakeMHCDet{Prepare,Finish}Function` and `CakeMHCHeadDetFunction`
resolve lazily at the top level through the lazy-export table added in
#8932.

## Behavior

- No entry point takes a `deterministic` keyword. Passing one raises
`TypeError`.
- Former names have no alias. Importing a former module path raises
`ImportError`, and former attributes are gone. #8900 already removed the
deterministic package's names that lacked "det".
- Each facade imports its backend package on first use. `import
flashinfer` does not import `flashinfer.experimental.cake`.
- Torch deterministic mode with the non-deterministic module:
- Under `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`,
`cake_mhc_nondet_train_backward_finish` and the backward of a prepare
node raise PyTorch's alert (`RuntimeError`) right before the
order-varying `dfn` reduction.
- With `warn_only=True`, they emit a `UserWarning` and run the
non-deterministic kernels.
  - There is no fallback to the deterministic module.
- The other calls (`forward_prepare`, `forward_stats`, `forward_finish`,
`backward_prepare`, the workspace helpers and the support query) give
bitwise-identical results from run to run and do not alert.
- Each finish accepts only a handle from its own module's prepare. A
handle from another module raises `TypeError`, and the message names the
matching finish.

## Unchanged

- Kernels, JIT library names, routing tables and the numerics of both
modes.
- CUDA sources. The files moved with their package, and their contents
are unchanged.
- A deterministic backward workspace still serves the non-deterministic
backward.
- Records (`stats`, `grad_stats`) work with either module.
- Coverage: hidden 4096, 5120 and 7168 on sm_100a and sm_103a, and
hidden 4096 on sm_107a. mHC has no KCP variant.
- This PR changes no kernel, launch or routing table.

`flashinfer/cake_mhc_det_train_head_backend/` |
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_mhc_head_det_train/` | det |
| `flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_mhc_train_backend/` |
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_mhc_nondet_train/` | nondet |

The 0.7.3 directory `flashinfer/cake_mhc_train_backend/` held the
deterministic package, so it maps to `cake_mhc_det_train`.
- `docs/api/mhc.rst` has one section per module and includes the
migration table above. `flashinfer/experimental/cake/__init__.py`
describes the backend packages as #8928 specifies.
- The non-deterministic tests are renamed to
`tests/experimental/test_cake_mhc_nondet_train*.py`. The head test is
renamed to `tests/mhc/test_cake_mhc_head_det_train.py`.
- New CPU tests
`tests/cpu/mhc/test_cake_mhc_{det,head_det,nondet}_train_names.py` check
three things:
  - every public name carries its mode word;
- no entry point, including autograd `Function.forward`, accepts a
`deterministic` keyword;
  - every former name fails at import.

### [acd2bd7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/acd2bd7a1141fe2b011c7e26d6bf2ca31e9e7dd5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T23:46:02Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate): route the deterministic forward by rows per SM (#9007)

The Cake SiLU-gated RMSNorm training kernel has two Cake variants: a
deterministic package and an opt-in non-deterministic package. This PR
changes the deterministic package,
`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_det_train` (BF16, head dim 128). The
baseline is the previous Cake deterministic version. It runs one plain
forward for every row count. With this PR, the forward uses rows per SM
to select a fixed-order forward program. The tiers are short, mid, and
long or extra-long, and the set of tiers depends on the architecture.
Between the short and mid tiers, the plain forward stays in use. All
routes are fixed-order, so each run gives the same bits as the last. The
backward does not change, so the checkpointed-layer gain comes from its
two forwards only.

Over all measured shapes on the new routes, the forward ratio is 1.092
to 1.300 on B200, 1.048 to 1.155 on GB300 and 1.112 to 1.299 on VR200.
The checkpointed-layer ratio is 1.036 to 1.208, 1.029 to 1.163 and 1.049
to 1.137. The tables below show selected shapes. A ratio above 1 means
the new version is faster.

The other Cake variant of this kernel is the opt-in non-deterministic
package `flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_silu_gate_nondet_train`, which uses the
same forward programs and a one-kernel backward with an order-varying
FP64 weight-gradient sum; both packages ship BF16, head dim 128, `[T, H,
128]` and `[T * H, 128]` layouts on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [7d091ce](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7d091ceb4b91903b2d634270fbf15a4fc4748637)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T23:42:44Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): walk key tiles in descending order in the sampling-off sm_103a wide programs (#9019)

Cake ships two variants of its deterministic DSA indexer top-k training
kernel (`cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`) in FlashInfer: the default
BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form. Each form has a
sampled-threshold mode and a sampling-off mode, and the family ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR changes only the BF16 `wide` scan
program on sm_103a. On sampling-off calls, the program now walks key
tiles in descending order. It does this through eight new `wide_desc`
programs, which a host plan field selects. Calls with sampling run the
same programs as main. Output ids and scores are bit-identical.

The baseline is the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main `d52713ec`.
Speedup is main time divided by this PR time, so values above 1 mean
faster. Four prepared calls with sampling off get faster. Z1k4096 goes
from 18.0118 to 12.7670 ms (1.411x), S6sink from 244.2289 to 194.6145 ms
(1.255x), Z1 from 13.3952 to 11.1354 ms (1.203x) and Z1k256 from 11.0596
to 10.5200 ms (1.051x). All four were timed with 12 processes. The other
sampling-off calls that switch to `wide_desc` are S5, S6, S7, V2, S8 and
the 12 sweep rows. They range from 0.997x (G16384x128k_s1,
G16384x128k_s4) to 1.003x (V2, G1024x128k_s8).

| GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs, CUDA 13.4) | min | max |
|---|---|---|
| prepared calls, sampling off, `wide -> wide_desc` (9 rows) | 0.998x
(S5) | 1.411x (Z1k4096) |
| prepared calls, sampling off, program unchanged (24 rows) | 0.997x
(V1) | 1.010x (A2) |
| prepared calls, sampling on, program unchanged (32 rows) | 0.991x
(Z1k4096) | 1.015x (Z1k256) |
| sweep rows, sampling off, `wide -> wide_desc` (12 rows) | 0.997x
(G16384x128k_s1, G16384x128k_s4) | 1.003x (G1024x128k_s8) |
| sweep rows, sampling on, program unchanged (12 rows) | 0.996x
(W8192_128k) | 1.009x (G16384x128k_s1, G16384x128k_s2) |
| eager entry, program unchanged (8 rows) | 0.995x (A1) | 1.000x (S1,
S2, C1, Z2cp, A3) |

### [38ca032](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/38ca0322c0395bf630cf9a48b164d392efb0c688)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T23:29:40Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_kda_det)!: name the det single-rank KDA entries by mode and move its backend under experimental/cake (#8928) (#9008)

## Summary

Part of #8928. #8928 adds the mode word (`det` / `nondet`) to every Cake
training name and removes the `deterministic=` keyword. This PR applies
that scheme to one family only: deterministic single-rank KDA (Kimi
Delta Attention) chunked training. The facade
`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train` keeps its path, but its entries are
renamed. They are now stable, so they no longer emit
`ExperimentalWarning`. The backend package moves under
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/`. Old names and the old package path are
removed with no alias.

## Depends on / order

- #8908 (merged): removed the names from before the det rename
(`flashinfer.kda_train`, `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train`,
`chunk_kda*`, `Kda*`).
- Merge order: this PR, then #8801, then the KDA family PR.

## Migration

Old names fail to import (`ImportError` / `AttributeError`). The
`flashinfer` top level gains no KDA names.

**Facade `flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train`** (former names as in
v0.7.4rc1)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `chunk_kda_det_fwd` | `cake_kda_det_train_forward` |
| `chunk_kda_det_bwd` | `cake_kda_det_train_backward` |
| `chunk_kda_det` | `cake_kda_det` |
| `kda_det_train_arena` | `cake_kda_det_train_arena` |
| `kda_det_train_workspace` | `cake_kda_det_train_workspace` |
| `kda_det_train_workspace_bytes` | `cake_kda_det_train_workspace_bytes`
|
| `kda_det_train_saved_bytes` | `cake_kda_det_train_saved_bytes` |
| `is_kda_det_train_supported` | `is_cake_kda_det_train_supported` |

`__all__` is now exactly: `DEFAULT_SCALE`, `cake_kda_det`,
`cake_kda_det_train_arena`, `cake_kda_det_train_backward`,
`cake_kda_det_train_forward`, `cake_kda_det_train_saved_bytes`,
`cake_kda_det_train_workspace`, `cake_kda_det_train_workspace_bytes`,
`is_cake_kda_det_train_supported`. The module no longer defines
`_FEATURE`.

**Backend package and its `cake_backend` module**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `ChunkKDADetFunction` | `CakeKDADetFunction` |
| `KdaDetWorkspace` | `CakeKDADetWorkspace` |
| `KdaDetChunkSaved` | `CakeKDADetChunkSaved` |
| `KdaDetArena` | `CakeKDADetArena` |
| `chunk_kda_det_fwd` | `cake_kda_det_train_forward` |
| `chunk_kda_det_bwd` | `cake_kda_det_train_backward` |
| `chunk_kda_det` | `cake_kda_det` |

**Package path**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_det_train/` |
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_kda_det_train/` |
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_det_train` |
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_det_train` |

The package `__init__` exports `ARCHES`, `ARCH_BY_CAPABILITY`,
`SAVE_MODES`, `SAVED_VERSION`, `SAVED_VERSION_TAPE`, `SCALE`,
`SEG_SAVE_MIN_TOKENS_PER_SEG`, `CakeKDADetArena`,
`CakeKDADetChunkSaved`, `CakeKDADetFunction`, `CakeKDADetWorkspace`,
`cake_kda_det`, `cake_kda_det_train_backward` and
`cake_kda_det_train_forward`. It no longer re-exports the internal
host-plan helpers `Plan`, `plan`, `is_supported`, `workspace_bytes`,
`saved_bytes`, `output_bytes`, `memory_report` and `seg_states_saved`.
They are still available from
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_kda_det_train.cake_backend`.

The package moves as a whole directory. Its `build.json` names the new
package. Its build files (`build.json`, `cake_build.py`,
`csrc/cake_ffi_checks.h`) stay inside the package directory, so it still
builds and imports on its own.
`tests/cpu/test_cake_packages_standalone.py` checks this by importing
every `PACKAGES` entry with `flashinfer` blocked. The `PACKAGES` row in
`tests/test_helpers/cake_package.py` is now `"cake.cake_kda_det_train"`.
`.github/labeler.yml`, the `pyproject.toml` package-data key and the row
in `scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py` now use the new path. So do
the two GDN KCP build tests that read the det KDA backend's shared
loader bytes.

## Scope

The follow-up KDA family PR renames three packages that are out of scope
here:

- the det context-parallel package (`flashinfer.cake_kda_det_train_kcp`
/ `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_det_train_kcp`)
- the nondet single-rank `flashinfer.cake_kda_train`, which still has
its `deterministic=` keyword
- the nondet KCP package

This PR only changes the lines in those files that import or name the
moved det single-rank package, so they keep working. No KCP or nondet
name changes, and no behaviour changes. Because the det single-rank
facade no longer exports `_FEATURE`, the det KCP facade now defines its
own experimental-feature string with the same text. The det KCP package
still imports the single-rank package across directories, so it stays in
the standalone test's `ALLOWLIST` until the family PR.

## Unchanged

Kernels, numerics, the program/library names
(`cake_kda_det_train_<digest>`) and csrc are unchanged.

### [8cfcf6a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8cfcf6ae1441eb9a9aefa03c21df4bd60544a83d)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T23:09:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_fmha): BF16 paged-context runtime-size programs for the non-causal, LSE and sink forms (#9016)

Cake's BF16 paged-context attention (head dim 128, BF16 Q, K, V and
output) already ships AOT programs for the plain causal form (causal, no
LSE output, no sinks). These are exact-shape programs and runtime-size
RUNTIME_PACK<p> programs at GQA packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16.

Five other forms had no AOT program and ran the JIT-compiled module:
- non-causal (NC)
- causal with LSE (LSE)
- causal with sink (SINK)
- non-causal with LSE (NC_LSE)
- non-causal with sink (NC_SINK)

This PR adds 45 runtime-size programs, RUNTIME_PACK<p>_<FORM>, for these
five forms at GQA packs 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12 and 16. Each program is
built for sm_100a and sm_103a. A call takes the program of its form at
the pack and page size the JIT module would use. Calls with both LSE and
sinks keep the JIT module. So do calls past per-target key-length bounds
where the program was not faster than the JIT module. On B200 this
covers 4 of the timed shapes (1 x 8192 x 8192 with pack 8, SINK and
LSE).

Outputs (O and the LSE) are bitwise equal to the JIT module of the same
form. The baseline is the previous Cake path for these calls, which is
the JIT module. trtllm-gen is shown as a second column. On B200, 143 of
147 shapes run a program. On those shapes this PR is 1.047x-3.227x
faster than the JIT module and 1.062x-4.400x faster than trtllm-gen. On
GB300, all 147 shapes run a program, and this PR is 1.065x-5.673x faster
than the JIT module and 1.012x-4.095x faster than trtllm-gen.

**B200 (sm_100a), CUDA 13.4 (13.4.2 toolkit).** GPU time with cold L2,
100 ms warm-up and 1000 ms per measurement (CUPTI).
- Unmarked rows: median of 3 rounds on one seeded memory layout, with
the arms rotated each round.
- Rows marked † were re-measured with this PR's kernels: median over 10
seeded memory layouts x 2 rounds.
- Unmarked SINK and LSE rows were measured with the previous build of
these kernels. This PR's build adds a branch these programs never take;
paired runs measured it 0-2.0 % slower.
- Shape is batch x query tokens x key/value tokens per request; heads
are query/KV heads; page is the KV page size in tokens.
- Ratios are of the shown medians. "JIT (bound; program measured X)"
rows keep the JIT module; X is the program's time.

- Shape is batch x query tokens x key/value tokens per request; heads
are query/KV heads; page is the KV page size in tokens.
- Ratios are of the shown medians.

Cake's paged-context attention also ships FP8 e4m3 programs (the plain
causal form and the same five forms), runtime-size programs with an
NVFP4 KV cache, and head-dim-256 FP16 and FP8 variants; the BF16
programs in this PR ship on sm_100a and sm_103a.

* **New Features**
* Added runtime-sized BF16 context-attention support for causal calls

within supported limits; other calls continue to use JIT execution.

operations, with clearer errors for invalid inputs and CUDA failures.

### [f0c8ee8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f0c8ee8afa2340e07519afe0b32e07e24c50c314)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T22:54:54Z
- **提交信息**: test(cake_kcp): always-on CPU parity of the KCP partition and base context across the four packages (#8928) (#9011)

## Summary

The deterministic and non-deterministic KDA and GDN KCP packages each
keep their own copy of the KCP partition and of the context builder, so
that each package still vendors on its own (#8928). This PR adds
`tests/cpu/test_cake_kcp_partition_parity.py`, which pins the behaviour
the four copies share:

- **Partition:** `to_dict()`, the fragments, each rank's local
`cu_seqlens`, the crossing counts and the document chains. It covers the
`contiguous`, `zigzag` and `zigzag_per_document` layouts (default and
random cut points) and explicit fragment tables (per-rank and flat),
with 16 seeded cases each.
- **Base context of every rank:** crossing slots, chains, chunk geometry
and tables, local `cu_seqlens`, halo plan and tables, fragment table,
`conv_kernel_size`, the `sm_count` default, and `seg_chunk_start`.
- **Errors:** the error type and message of 20 invalid partition inputs
and 5 invalid context inputs, and the process-group check (with
`torch.distributed` stubbed).

The segment plan, P rule, wave rule, head plan, byte queries and arena
layouts are not compared, because they differ by design.

The existing cross-package checks in the GDN KCP suites run only when
`GDN_ROWS_DIR` is set. This test needs no environment variable, GPU or
process group, and runs in the unit-test run over `tests/` (128 tests,
about 3.5 s of test time on one CPU node).

The test finds its packages and entries by rule, so the #8928 family
renames can land in any order without changing it:

- **Packages:** the one `PACKAGES` row per family whose import path ends
in `cake_<op>_<mode>_train_kcp`, or `cake_<op>_train_kcp` for the
non-deterministic package before the rename.
- **Entries:** the plan module's one public function named with
`partition` (or `build_context`) and `kcp`. This matches
`partition_det_kcp` as well as `cake_kda_det_train_kcp_partition`.

A package that the rule does not find, or that does not import, fails
the test; nothing is skipped.

## Validation

CPU only, CUDA hidden:

- This branch: 128 passed; `pytest --collect-only tests/` collects all
128.
- Negative controls, each failing as expected:
  - one package's `near_equal` changed (partition);
  - one package's `seq_order` tie rule changed (context only);
  - the GDN det row removed from `PACKAGES`.
- A tree where the deterministic KDA KCP package carries its #8928 names
under `flashinfer.experimental.cake`: 128 passed.

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8928

Co-authored-by: Yingyi Huang <averyh@nvidia.com>

### [b419089](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b419089c0f646345e6cd07be4a031cab600662ec)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T22:44:48Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): preload the next task's entering state into tensor memory in a new work-bin build of BF16 KDA prefill (sm_103a) (#9012)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
The BF16-input fused module with FP32 state has work-binned builds,
which place several (sequence, head) tasks in each CTA's bin. This PR
changes one of them: the bounded binned build that prefetches the next
task's state. In that build, the compute warps load each task's 64 KiB
FP32 entering state from global memory. This PR adds a new version of
that build for sm_103a (GB300). In the new build, the prep stage that
prepares a task's last chunk also loads the next task's entering state
into one of two TMEM slots. The compute warps then copy the state from
that slot and skip the global load. A task skips the preload when it
shares its state slot and head with one of the six tasks before it in
its bin. As a result, every task reads the same FP32 state words that it
reads without the preload. On GB300, a launch uses the new build when
four conditions hold: its work bins come from the strict bin test, it
has an initial state, every sequence has 64 to 256 tokens, and it has
more tasks than SMs. Every other launch keeps its build, including
launches whose bins come from the bounded rule. Outputs, final states
and checkpoints are bitwise identical to FlashInfer main. The tables
compare this PR with FlashInfer main on GB300 and report the latency per
call in microseconds. We measured against FlashInfer main before #8994
merged. #8994 changed only sm_100a, and the sm_103a programs that
current main renders are byte-identical to the measured baseline, so the
baseline still holds. Each table has 56 rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate
lower bound or -5, and 14 sequence-length shapes. One table covers the
plan-cache fast path, and the other covers the serving pattern. TIE
means no difference beyond the measurement band. In each table, two rows
are faster. Both have 16 heads and gate lower bound -5. With shape BS16
x T64, the latency goes from 23.58 to 22.30 us (1.06x) on the fast path
and from 23.36 to 22.27 us (1.05x) in the serving pattern. With shape
BS64 x T64, it goes from 62.98 to 60.83 us (1.04x) on the fast path and
from 63.20 to 60.67 us (1.04x) in the serving pattern. Every other row
is TIE, and none is slower. On the fast path, the speedup is 1.00x to
1.06x over 56 rows. In the serving pattern, it is 1.00x to 1.05x over 56
rows. We also ran two sweeps of launch shapes on two GB300 nodes. In a
60-shape sweep, all 60 shapes are faster on both nodes, with a latency
ratio (this PR / main) of 0.9332 to 0.9905. In a fresh 80-shape sweep,
44 shapes are faster on one node and 45 on the other, the rest are TIE,
and none is slower. The tables have GB300 columns only because sm_100a
(B200) does not change: there is no new sm_100a program, the sm_100a
preload table is empty, and every sm_100a program is SASS-identical to
FlashInfer main. The other Cake variants (the TF32-input modules, the
split forms and every other program) are unchanged on both sm_100a and
sm_103a.

GB300: NVIDIA GB300, sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03. CUDA 13.4
(nvcc), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add `backend="cute-dsl-rubin"` to
`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, exposing SM107 prefill through
the existing `plan`/`run` API. It accepts E4M3 Q/K/V with
`head_dim_qk=192`, `head_dim_vo=128`, and BF16 output.

- Equal-head attention uses ragged FMHA; grouped-query ratios 2, 4, and
8 use a persistent GQA kernel with positive, uniform query and KV
lengths.
- Backend planning validates hardware and input support, prepares lazy
CuTe DSL compilation, and binds buffers for eager execution or CUDA
graph replay.
- Run supports Q/K/V scales and optional FP32 LSE, with validation and
tests for masked rows, graph replanning, output storage, scale limits,
and grouped launch limits.

The backend requires explicit selection. Existing `cute-dsl`, `auto`,
and decode dispatch remain unchanged.

the #8928 CAKE training renames. It covers the #8928 checklist item "One
release note with the full migration table" and item 3 of
issuecomment-6680200530, which asks for the old -> new backend directory
map for vendoring builds. This PR changes only docs: it adds a Markdown
file outside the Sphinx build, which builds only `.rst` files, and
changes no code.

The note contains:
- The target modules after the renames (28 shipped modules and 4
reserved names), with the PR for each family.
- The calls that took `deterministic=`. The default or `True` maps to
the det module, and `False` maps to the nondet module. New entry points
raise `TypeError` on `deterministic=`. Old names fail at import because
there are no aliases.

`flashinfer/cake_rmsnorm_train_backend` was det in 0.7.3 and has been
nondet since #8208.
- The backend directory map, with the mode of each old path in 0.7.3 and
0.7.4rc1.
- A public name table for each family, listing the old name, the
releases that shipped it, the new name and the PR.

The PR column names the PR that renames each family (GDN: #8959, MoE
grouped GEMM: #8963, KDA det single rank: #9008), without its
open/merged state, so the tables do not go stale as the renames merge. A
row names a PR only when that PR's branch has the new name. The KDA det
KCP and KDA nondet modules have no rename PR yet, so those rows list the
#8928 target names as planned.

The rows were checked against the 0.7.3 and 0.7.4rc1 tags, main and each
family PR head. Where the contents of one old path went to different new
paths by release, the tables give one row per release; default calls and
`deterministic=False` calls get separate rows; KCP names carry their
module.

merges. One writer maintains the file; family owners send corrections to

### [d9da13b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d9da13b94456054d8132d7381f3a1b301dc28493)

- **作者**: Enwei Zhu
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T22:33:01Z
- **提交信息**: feat: support token-strided QKV in CuTe KDA prefill (#8613)

## 📌 Description

Packed projection or convolution outputs produce token-strided Q/K/V
views. This PR lets CuTe KDA prefill consume these views directly,
eliminating the three packing copies required previously.

- Support aligned token strides in `cute-dsl` and `cute-dsl-persistent`,
including both SM120 variants.
- Use runtime 64-bit token strides and construct input/output TMA
layouts independently.
- Make SM120 descriptor caching and alias checks stride-aware.
- Extend existing numerical and CUDA graph tests with strided inputs.

### Performance

NVIDIA GB200 (SM100), one sequence, 96 heads, head dimension 128, BF16
Q/K/V and FP32 state. Inputs are views of `[1, T, 3, 96, 128]` packed
storage.

Numbers are median summed GPU kernel durations from 21 warmed eager
calls measured with Nsight Systems, flushing L2 between calls. Before
includes Q/K/V `.contiguous()` copies; after passes the views directly.

| Tokens | CuTe before (µs) | CuTe after (µs) | Persistent before (µs) |
Persistent after (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 53.92 | 25.89 | 51.94 | 24.83 |
| 8,192 | 1,065.70 | 442.24 | 999.23 | 375.84 |
| 16,384 | 2,109.15 | 872.00 | 1,973.95 | 737.22 |

Kernel counts decrease from 5 to 2 for ordinary CuTe and from 4 to 1 for
persistent CuTe. Contiguous-input controls remain within 1%.

## Summary

This PR is the causal conv1d det family's part of #8928. #8928 renames
the Cake training kernels so every name states its mode. After the
rename:

- The public module is `flashinfer.cake_<op>_<mode>_train[_kcp]`.
- The backend package sits at `flashinfer/experimental/cake/<module>/`.
- No entry takes `deterministic=`.
- Old names have no aliases, so they fail at import.

This PR covers the det single-rank and det KCP entries. The nondet
conv1d entries were renamed in #8906 (merged). This PR builds on #8932
(merged), which added the `_LAZY_EXPORTS` table.

The kernel math is unchanged. The csrc tree is byte-identical between
the old and new backend directories (86 files, tree hash `c3ba7e6f…`).
`build.json` differs only in its `"package"` field. Library stems,
program names and csrc names are unchanged.

The facades `flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train` and
`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_kcp` keep their module names,
but they no longer import the backend at module level.
`CakeCausalConv1dDetFunction`,
`cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_forward_workspace_bytes` and
`cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_backward_workspace_bytes` are now served
at top level through `_LAZY_EXPORTS` rows. As a result, `import
flashinfer` loads no backend.

Other changed files:
- Call sites of the det names in the nondet conv1d KCP facade, its tests
and its bench.
- `docs/api/mamba.rst`.
- The det-conv lines in the KDA det/nondet KCP README and in the
dist/upload tests. The KDA owners reviewed these lines.
- One row each in the shared files: `tests/test_helpers/cake_package.py`
`PACKAGES`, pyproject package-data,
`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py`, and the
`.pre-commit-config.yaml` exclude.

New tests:
- A names test. It checks the mode word per token and confirms that
`inspect.signature(obj).bind_partial(deterministic=False)` raises
`TypeError`, including on autograd `Function.forward`.
- A test that det entries never raise PyTorch's deterministic-algorithms
alert.

## 📌 Description

Native Windows cannot import `fcntl`, which prevents several cache and
test-runner paths from loading. Add a lightweight descriptor-lock
adapter and migrate ten existing callers. Unix continues to use
`fcntl.flock`; Windows uses Portalocker's `Win32Locker` for native
shared/exclusive and blocking/nonblocking locks. Preserve the original
Unix caller control flow, retries, file modes and cleanup, with
conditional Windows setup where required.

Package the standalone adapter, declare its Windows backend and the
already-used `filelock` dependency, and update the Frost exporter and
manifest together. Skip only Quack-dependent attention cases on native
Windows pending upstream support; keep Quack-free coverage eligible and
preserve errors from installed-but-broken Quack on other platforms.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- [NVBug 6954295](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/6954295): VSA
dependency and native Windows import failures.
- [Quack PR #216](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/quack/pull/216): upstream
portability work, still open/unmerged.
- [NVBug 7010251](https://nvbugspro.nvidia.com/bug/7010251): overlapping
B12x imports; upstream #8300 now includes its separate Windows
directory-sync guard.

### [d20e164](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d20e164d936d17129f6a7ee72f6ab7727252ac22)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T22:21:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): split SM107 FP8 64-head decode calls of few query rows (#8984)

Cake's DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA attention for FlashInfer (`cake_dsv4`) on
FlashInfer main routes 32 call forms to 28 distinct programs on each of
sm_100a and sm_103a. These programs cover BF16 and FP8 KV caches and 8
to 128 query heads. It also has 9 FP8 programs for sm_107a. This PR adds
no program and changes no kernel. It changes only the host routing in
`flashinfer/mla/cake_dsv4.py` for sm_107a decode calls that meet all of
these conditions:

- FP8 KV cache
- 64 query heads
- PDL on
- sparse widths of four to nine 128-key tiles (385 to 1152 sparse keys
per query)
- few query rows

The baseline is the previous Cake version on main (commit `7b93789d`,
which contains #8950 and #8978). There, each of these calls runs as one
launch of the route's program. With this PR, they run the split-KV
producer and merge kernel that #8950 added for 128 heads, which are the
same two programs. The table's c128 rows give the pieces per row at the
first and last row count of every band. The following calls keep main's
route: calls with more query rows, widths of three tiles or fewer, calls
without PDL, other head counts and other architectures. The 128-head
rule is unchanged.

The results below are from NVIDIA R200 and NVIDIA VR200 (both sm_107a).
On each GPU, the 184 routed full-width cells cover both layers, q_len 1
and 4, and row counts across every band, including both of its edges. On
these cells this PR is 1.03x to 1.57x faster than main on R200 (median
1.19x) and 1.03x to 1.63x faster on VR200 (median 1.17x). When each of
the 8 back-to-back calls has its own input set, it is 1.09x to 1.66x
faster on R200 (median 1.26x) and 1.07x to 1.67x faster on VR200 (median
1.24x). Partial widths, where the last 128-key tile is not full (for
example 388 and 516 keys), behave the same, at 1.00x to 1.68x across
every band on both GPUs. Only one cell is below 1.00x: 388 keys (three
full tiles plus 4 keys), 2 rows, c128 layer, on R200 with one input set.
It goes from 6.668 us on main to 6.682 us with this PR (0.998x), which
is within run-to-run noise. The same cell is 1.10x on R200 when each
call has its own input set, and 1.08x on VR200. In mixed batches, every
other request attends all keys of the width and the others attend few
keys. These batches are 1.05x to 1.58x faster on R200, saving 0.38 to
3.69 us per call, and 1.03x to 1.62x faster on VR200, saving 0.23 to
3.91 us per call.

One case is slower. When every request in the call attends few keys,
each row fits in one piece, but the split still runs the merge kernel.
On R200 these calls run at 0.79x to 0.90x, which is 0.56 to 1.50 us
slower per call (main 4.84 to 6.49 us, this PR 5.44 to 7.83 us). On
VR200 they run at 0.79x to 0.97x, which is 0.17 to 1.49 us slower per
call (main 4.97 to 6.69 us, this PR 5.46 to 8.15 us). The host cannot
detect this case because request lengths live on the GPU, the same
reason as in #8950 and #8978. 128-head calls behave the same way under
the existing rule.

The table below lists times per call in microseconds on NVIDIA R200
(sm_107a, 216 SMs) and NVIDIA VR200 (sm_107a, 212 SMs), both with the
CUDA 13.4 runtime. Each call is one of 8 back-to-back calls with PDL,
captured in one CUDA graph. L2 is flushed before each replay, and all
calls use one input set. Each value is the median over 8 rounds, with
main and this PR alternating in the same process. Speedup = main latency
/ this PR's latency.

Column definitions:

- **c4 (W)** and **c128 (W):** the DeepSeek-V4 c4 and c128 layers with
sparse width W per query, which is 128 sliding-window keys plus the
layer's selected/compressed keys.
- **q_len:** query tokens per request.
- **rows T:** query rows in the call.
- **pieces per row:** the split pieces this PR runs. Main runs 1 launch
with no split.

In every row, every query attends all W keys and PDL is on.

### [f3f2dc2](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/f3f2dc2a5820f848018d1418c2bec421ee8a4165)

- **作者**: Andrii Skliar
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T21:30:21Z
- **提交信息**: fix(mamba): bound FP8 ReplaySSM checkpoint scales (#8968)

## 📌 Description

Prevent invalid scales when shared FP8 ReplaySSM checkpoints contain
very small row magnitudes.

The flush encoder computes `encode = 448 / amax` and stores `decode = 1
/ encode`. Tiny rows can overflow the reciprocal or produce a subnormal
decode scale. The native recurrence uses fast math, which can flush
subnormal values to zero.

The overflow corrupts state. When `amax` is below about `2^-119`, `448 /
amax` overflows to infinity. Exact zeros in that row then encode `0 *
inf` as an E4M3 NaN, which `satfinite` conversion preserves. The stored
decode scale becomes `1 / inf = 0`, and the next replay propagates the
NaN. INT8 conversion maps NaN to zero, so INT8 rows lose only negligible
magnitude.

For FP8 E4M3 only, bound the denominator by `448 * 2^-117`. The smallest
nonzero E4M3 value is `2^-9`, so the resulting decode scale keeps
nonzero decoded values at or above the smallest normal FP32 value,
`2^-126`.

Zero rows retain scale 1. INT8 encoding and ordinary-range FP8 encoding
retain their existing behavior. There is no API or checkpoint-layout
change.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Companion prefill encoder change: [vLLM
#52962](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52962), now included
in [commit
`d199e17b0c`](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/commit/d199e17b0c7a0c691e10e9aceb255009fe5dd27f).
[Commit
`cf22b7d658`](https://github.com/askliar/vllm/commit/cf22b7d658e4e88c70ccea69a4d191fa346a865a)
in that PR rejects shared FP8 checkpoints on FlashInfer releases without
this change.
Its minimum version, 0.7.5, assumes this change ships after 0.7.4rc1. It
must be updated to the first release containing this PR.

The open checkpoint-runtime and Nemotron-test PRs do not implement this
scale bound. This change is limited to the existing FP8 flush encoder.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit`.
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files`.

All applicable hooks passed for the two changed files, including
clang-format and Ruff. The complete repository was not checked.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing on this exact branch. The new CUDA
regression requires GPU execution.
- [ ] This PR requires **full-scope** CI, not targeted tests.
      Reason: the change is limited to one checkpoint encoder.

Suggested CI test target: `tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py`.

Both new tests force a checkpoint flush through `checkpointing_ssu`,
using a recurrence that changes nothing. Each runs with nearest rounding
and SR5, and SR5 follows the existing hardware-support guard.

- `test_checkpointing_ssu_fp8_flush_keeps_valid_scales` checks zero,
tiny, threshold, and ordinary rows. The decoded state must be preserved
exactly.
- `test_checkpointing_ssu_fp8_flush_tiny_row_with_zeros_stays_finite`
flushes a `2^-122` row whose alternate elements are exactly zero. The
stored state must contain no NaN, every scale must equal `2^-117`, and
the decoded state must be preserved exactly. The unbounded encoder
writes NaN for this row.

Local checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  include/flashinfer/mamba/kernel_checkpointing_ssu_8bit.cuh \
  tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py
```

GPU regression command:

```bash
pytest -v \
  tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py::test_checkpointing_ssu_fp8_flush_keeps_valid_scales \
  tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py::test_checkpointing_ssu_fp8_flush_tiny_row_with_zeros_stays_finite
```

Prior GPU evidence used this encoder change in FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 on
GB300, with Torch 2.14.0+cu130:
- The component run completed 72 paired native checkpoint calls with
nearest rounding, SR5, and SR10.
- The matching vLLM prefill bound corrected a captured row with
`amax=1.4438979376402915e-41`, whose original stored scale was zero.
- With both encoder changes, Super120B NVFP4 scored 1201/1319 (91.05%)
and 1187/1319 (89.99%) on two consecutive GSM8K passes. The run used
shared FP8, SR5, eager STP, replay window 8, batch limit 256, and a
fixed 120 GiB KV budget. Invalid answers, corruption, and preemptions
were zero.

These earlier runs do not validate the complete current upstream tree or
isolate the accuracy effect of this change. Neither new regression test
has run on a GPU in this publication checkout. A CPU PyTorch check of
the second test's row confirms the arithmetic: the unbounded formula
produces NaN, and the bounded formula round-trips the row exactly. No
throughput improvement is claimed.

The floor applies only to FP8 E4M3. The comparison-based bound retains
the existing handling of a NaN denominator.

The vLLM prefill encoder must use the same bound. The tested FlashInfer
0.7.2.post1 package required this patch.

this description. OpenAI Codex and Claude Code assisted.

### [dc0ed2e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/dc0ed2e6e9f866c4d6c3c5a323cf4c10e9bcb505)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T21:27:42Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_vsa_sm120): merge a two-part row with one partial read in vsa_sm120_blk64 (#9002)

`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="vsa_sm120_blk64")` on SM120 /
SM121 has 4 Cake variants: the BF16 and FP16 builds of two persistent
kernels, `vsa_sm120_blk64` (two 128-thread CTAs per SM) and
`vsa_sm120_blk64_pair` (one CTA of two 4-warp groups per SM). Both
kernels run one host plan, and the host planner picks the kernel per
shape. The kernels cover head dim 128, 64 x 64 blocks, GQA and optional
LSE. This PR changes only the BF16 and FP16 builds of `vsa_sm120_blk64`;
the `vsa_sm120_blk64_pair` kernels, the host planner, the API and the
numerics contract are unchanged. When the planner splits a query row
into parts, the last part to finish merges the partial states (O, m, d)
of all parts. For a row of exactly two parts, that last part now keeps
its own state in registers and reads only the other part's state from
the workspace, so the merge issues 68 instead of 136 global loads per
thread. It folds the two states in part order with the same operations
as before, and rows of more than two parts merge as before. Outputs are
bitwise equal to main on all 100 measured shapes with both CUDA
versions, and LSE is bitwise equal on the 2 shapes that return it. The
baseline is FlashInfer main at `cf89246b`, the base of this PR, which
runs the previous Cake version of these kernels and planner (from #8799,
#8829, #8898, #8940 and #8973). Over all 100 shapes, the geomean speedup
is 1.005 with nvcc 13.0 (64 of 100 at or above 1.0, slowest 0.991) and
1.003 with nvcc 13.4 (60 of 100 at or above 1.0, slowest 0.964). The
geomean is 1.006 (nvcc 13.0) and 1.007 (nvcc 13.4) on the 22 delivery
shapes, and 1.007 with both on the 66 shapes that run `vsa_sm120_blk64`.
The 40 of these 66 shapes whose plans merge two-part rows run the
changed code and reach 1.011 (nvcc 13.0) and 1.012 (nvcc 13.4). The gain
is largest where the merge is a large share of the time: the 11 of these
40 that take at most 65 µs on main reach 1.023 with both, and the
largest value is 1.047 with nvcc 13.0 and 1.055 with nvcc 13.4, both on
`std_s1024_d50`.

Measured on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, 188
SMs, driver 595.84.01), with the kernels JIT-built by CUDA 13.0 and by
CUDA 13.4. `wrapper.run` latency is timed with CUPTI and a cold L2. Each
value is the median over 5 interleaved rounds x 3 input placements.
Speedup is main / this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster.
The Kernel column names the kernel that this PR's planner picks for each
shape ("blk64" or "pair", with "+ packed" when the plan packs short KV
lists).

above 1.0, slowest `h16_n8192_k36` 0.964).

row: geomean 1.000 (nvcc 13.0) and 0.999 (nvcc 13.4), range 0.991-1.014
and 0.987-1.005. The 34 shapes that run `vsa_sm120_blk64_pair` run the
same kernel code and the same plan in main and in this PR: geomean 1.000
(nvcc 13.0) and 0.997 (nvcc 13.4), range 0.994-1.019 and 0.964-1.005.

value under nvcc 13.4 (0.964, `h16_n8192_k36`) is one of these pair
shapes. The slowest under nvcc 13.0 (0.991, `mb24_s32`) is one of the 26
shapes without a two-part merge.

Cake also ships VSA block-sparse attention for Hopper (sm_90a) and for
SM100 / SM103 Blackwell (sm_100a, sm_103a); this SM120 family ships for
sm_120a and sm_121a.

### [cc2320e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cc2320ea7e5ec10e531ed9b43b590c0f16eea330)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T21:16:25Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_mega_moe_v3): fence the in-launch global hand-offs before async-proxy reads (#9001)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline in a single kernel launch. It has single-rank routed-FP4,
single-rank routed-FP8 and grouped-GEMM-routes variants, plus a TP/EP
rank variant. The rank variant has 32 programs, covering TP4 EP1, TP8
EP1, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 at 1 to 4096 tokens.

This PR fixes a correctness gap in all 32 rank programs. These programs
use TMA and bulk copies (`cp.async.bulk`) to read data that ordinary
stores wrote earlier in the same launch. TMA and bulk copies read
through the async proxy, and there was no proxy fence between those
writes and the reads, so the reads were not guaranteed to see the
writes. Each program now issues `fence.proxy.async.global` on the
reading side before these reads. Outputs are bitwise identical to the
previous version. The fence costs time: up to +1.000 % per call, and no
program got faster beyond its noise band.

This PR does not change the 13 programs of the other variants
(single-rank and grouped), and they do not get the fence here.

*Rank-variant latency on NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs), driver
580.159.03, CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Replicates a and b
ran on different GB300 nodes. All values are per call in us and come
from CUDA graphs of 20 calls.*

*Previous version vs this PR: "previous" is FlashInfer main before this
PR. Each run has 6 rounds, and each round runs the previous version,
this PR, and the previous version again (the A/A check), each in a fresh
process. Each process does 21 graph replays. Each value is the median
over the 6 rounds. Speedup = previous / this PR, computed from unrounded
latencies. Each row has its own noise band: the larger of its A/A
difference and its maximum in-process A/A spread. Bands range from 0.024
% to 0.974 % per row. No row is faster than the previous version beyond
its band in either replicate. 11 rows (a) and 13 rows (b) are slower
beyond their band. The worst slowdown is TP8 EP1 at 1024 tokens: 196.39
-> 198.35 us (+1.000 %) in a and 196.66 -> 198.52 us (+0.949 %) in b.*

*Baseline vs this PR: the baseline is the issue's autotuned
`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, pinned to the tactics from its
original autotune run. In each replicate, two baseline graphs and two
graphs of this PR ran in two processes for 21 interleaved rounds, and
each value is the median per graph. To keep the comparison conservative,
each "TRT baseline" value is the fastest of the two in-run baseline
graphs and the issue's recorded baseline median. Each "this PR" value is
the slower of this PR's two graphs. Speedup = TRT baseline / this PR.
The band is the largest of the two in-run A/A spreads and a
per-configuration cross-process A/A allowance (1.0 % for TP4 EP4 and TP8
EP8). Every row is faster than the baseline beyond its band in both
replicates. The tightest row is TP8 EP8 at 4 tokens: 1.009 % faster in a
and 1.050 % faster in b, against a 1.000 % band. Both margins are
computed from unrounded medians.*

### [2d134f9](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2d134f98d88351c499e09259d32cf3b9b82a34b4)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T21:13:16Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): early-PV sm_107a FP8 low-head prefill for launches up to 64 query tokens (#8991)

Cake's DSv4 sparse MLA kernel (`trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(...,
backend="cake")`) has 53 BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128
query heads with this PR (52 before it), plus an NVFP4-KV decode family.
With this PR it ships ten FP8 programs on sm_107a. Five are for 128
heads: three persistent prefill programs, a split-KV producer and its
merge. Three are 64-head M64 prefill programs. Two are low-head prefill
programs for 8, 16, 32 and 64 heads: the existing `fp8_lowhead_prefill`
and the new `fp8_lowhead_prefill_overlap`, which this PR adds. Routing
is unchanged. On sm_107a FlashInfer sends a call to the low-head prefill
route when four conditions hold: its KV is the 128-token sliding window
only (no compressed KV), it has 8, 16, 32 or 64 query heads, `max_q_len
< 257`, and 2 × query tokens ≤ SM count. Within that route, launches
with at most 64 query tokens on a 216-SM part now run the new program.
The ceiling scales down with the SM count on parts with fewer SMs (62 at
212 SMs, 61 at 208 SMs), and larger launches keep the existing program.
The host selects the program per launch (`_overlap_variant`). The new
program has the same arguments, grid, launch configuration and output
bits as the existing one. It issues the P × V MMAs as soon as the
softmax has written the low half of P, instead of waiting for all of P.
Its epilogue drains the output of the first V block while the MMA of the
second V block runs. Outputs are bitwise identical to the existing
program's. The existing program, sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged. To
retire the new program, point its `VARIANTS` entry back at the existing
program. Speedups are measured against the previous Cake program, which
is the shipped low-head prefill program timed in the same build with the
new program disabled. On rows with at most 64 query tokens the speedup
is 1.006x-1.033x with a cold L2 and 1.008x-1.039x in CUDA graphs. Rows
above 64 query tokens run the same program on both sides and are
unchanged (0.998x-1.001x).

NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs), CUDA 13.4. The cold L2 columns give
kernel time (CUPTI) with a cold L2 and back-to-back launches: the median
of each round, then the median of 6 paired rounds. The CUDA graph
columns time one CUDA graph of 8 calls with PDL behind a predecessor
kernel. The per-call time is the median over 100 replays of (graph minus
predecessor graph) / 8, then the median of 6 rounds. Speedup is the
median of the 6 per-round previous / this PR ratios, so it can differ
slightly from the ratio of the two printed medians. The CUPTI timer step
is 32 ns per launch, so a 1-step change is about 0.4-0.6 % on these
rows. T is the total number of query tokens. Every row uses the
128-token sliding window with sparse top-k 128 and attention sinks. Rows
with T > 64 run the existing program on both sides and are shown as
controls.

Full windows, no unused slots. The cache column gives request 0's SWA
cache length, and each later request's cache is longer by the stated
step.

separate SM120 DSv4 programs (NVFP4 and DSv4.1 mixed-cache sparse MLA)
ship on sm_120a.

### [ea66b20](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ea66b20462519fce84e7780911df8e735e6fb5c2)

- **作者**: Anerudhan Gopal
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T20:52:17Z
- **提交信息**: feat(moe_ep): add isolated Kimi K3-family MegaMoE backend (#8934)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Add Kimi K3-family MegaMoE to `flashinfer.moe_ep` through the explicit
`sm100_kimi_k3_megamoe` selector and `Sm100_KimiK3_MegaMoeConfig`. Kimi
K3 and K3.1 Pro share the routed E896/H3584/I3072/top-16 contract, with
EP1/8/16, NVFP4 or MXFP4/MXFP8, and BF16 or MXFP8 combine. Both use the
same API with their own checkpoint config and weights. Use
`routed_expert_hidden_size=3584`; routing, latent projections, post-MoE
RMSNorm, and shared experts remain in the framework.

The adapter lives in `backends/mega/kernel/sm100/kimi_k3`; its runtime
and source live in `kernel_src/sm100/kimi-k3-megamoe`. It owns its
quantizers, route staging, symmetric buffers, compiled kernels, and
reducer, while sharing the generic API and workspace lifecycle. The
current MegaMoE providers and automatic selection are unchanged. This
includes a pinned 44-file source export, hash checks, package-data
loading, tests, a benchmark, and API documentation.

B300 EP8, 8192 tokens/rank, NVFP4/BF16 warm graph forward:

| Provider | Median time |
| --- | ---: |
| Current standard provider | 2.560 ms |
| Kimi K3 | 2.105 ms |

Median paired speedup across three runs: **1.218x**. Both use sparse
weights, supplied routes, the same calibration, and fast SiTU disabled.
The current provider uses tile `(256, 128, 256)` because its default
tile fails admission at this size. Each timing uses 30 samples of 10
replays, taking the slowest rank per sample.

GB300 EP16 at 8192 tokens/rank: NVFP4 measured 2.102 ms with BF16
combine and 1.627 ms with MXFP8 combine; MXFP4/MXFP8 measured 2.743 and
2.614 ms. All 12 EP16 cases completed. Full tables and commands are in
`docs/api/moe_ep_kimi_k3.rst`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

No linked issue. Source: [Kimi K3
MegaMoE](https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/bchislett/kimi-k3-megamoe),
pinned at `6e8cfe94e9d6c92b184fb46700c72e9f66ccb884`.

### [26d91ec](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/26d91ec57e8af68134023da57ba2d831630c07cf)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T20:45:07Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda): enable the three 128-token turnover builds of BF16 KDA prefill on sm_100a (#8994)

The Cake chunked KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) prefill behind
`flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` has modules with BF16
inputs and modules with TF32 inputs. Both come in fused and split forms.
The BF16-input fused module with FP32 state has three 128-token turnover
builds for launches where every sequence has exactly 128 tokens. #8823
added these builds on sm_103a (GB300), and #8874 changed two of them. In
all three builds, the compute warps load the first state. In the two
builds from #8874, every warp role also computes its bin bounds and task
ids with round-robin arithmetic. Also, a CTA whose bin is shorter than
the longest bin waits 3.8 us before it starts. Until now, these builds
ran only on GB300. This PR enables the same three builds, with the same
kernel code, on sm_100a (B200). On B200, launches now use these builds
when every sequence has exactly 128 tokens and the launch goes to a
bounded turnover build. Every other launch keeps its build. Outputs are
bitwise identical to FlashInfer main. The tables compare this PR with
FlashInfer main on B200. FlashInfer main already includes #8874. The
tables report the latency per call in microseconds. Each table has 56
rows: 12 or 16 heads, no gate lower bound or -5, and 14 sequence-length
shapes. One table covers the plan-cache fast path, and the other covers
the serving pattern. TIE means no difference beyond the measurement
band. In each table, two rows are faster. Both use shape BS16 x T128
with gate lower bound -5: one row has 12 heads and the other has 16
heads. With 12 heads, the latency goes from 32.51 to 29.50 us (1.10x) on
the fast path and from 32.74 to 29.47 us (1.11x) in the serving pattern.
With 16 heads, it goes from 33.73 to 31.46 us (1.07x) on the fast path
and from 33.76 to 31.46 us (1.07x) in the serving pattern. Every other
row is TIE, and none is slower. On the fast path, the speedup is 0.99x
to 1.10x over 56 rows. In the serving pattern, it is 0.99x to 1.11x over
56 rows. Three TIE rows read 0.99x and their launches keep the same
build. In both tables, one is the row with 12 heads, no gate lower bound
and shape 8x(1024+64). In the serving pattern, the third is the row with
16 heads, gate lower bound -5 and shape 16384. We also swept 114 launch
shapes that are not in the tables and that this PR moves to these builds
on B200. We ran this sweep on two B200 nodes. All 114 shapes are faster
on both nodes, with a latency ratio (this PR / main) of 0.8839 to
0.9872. GB300 is unchanged because no sm_103a build or route changes, so
the tables have B200 columns only. The other Cake variants (the
TF32-input modules, the split forms and every other program) are
unchanged on both sm_100a and sm_103a.

B200: NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs, driver 580.82.07. CUDA 13.4 (nvcc),
PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

### [0ff7d4f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0ff7d4fb42d262521961c30eab9e1a4616f1d6db)

- **作者**: Jonathan Dierksen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T20:14:00Z
- **提交信息**: ci(docker): install rsync in the CI images (#8990)

## 📌 Description

Adds `rsync` to the apt packages in `docker/Dockerfile.ci`, next to
`jq`.

NVIDIA's internal unit-test CI keeps a persistent per-host cache and
publishes it with `rsync`. The CI images don't include `rsync`. On the
DGX Spark lane, containers run as the job user, without root or sudo, so
before every publication the job downloads the `rsync` and `libpopt0`
packages and unpacks them into a temporary directory. With `rsync` in
the image, that workaround can be removed.

Merging this starts the Release CI Docker workflow. Its
`update-docker-tags` job moves #6266 to the new image tag, so one tag
bump brings both `jq` (added in #6814) and `rsync`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- #6266: Docker CI tag bump
- #6814: added `jq` to the image

### [878fd51](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/878fd51c7b9116e7e12796a054b73e25a8c6fc39)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T19:56:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): take the wide unit from 5.5 rounds per CTA on sm_100a (#8989)

Cake ships two variants of its deterministic DSA indexer top-k training
kernel (`dsa_indexer_det_topk`) in FlashInfer: the default BF16 form and
the opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form. Each form has a sampled-threshold mode and a
sampling-off mode, and the family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.
This PR changes one BF16 dispatch rule on sm_100a. The eight-query wide
unit is now used from 5.5 wide rounds per CTA instead of 6, so calls in
the 5.5-6 round band move from the narrow unit to the wide unit. Output
ids and scores are bit-identical.

Only BF16 sm_100a plans change: 40 of 722 checked plan geometries on 148
SMs and 40 of 722 on 152 SMs. The FP8 plans and the sm_103a and sm_107a
plans are unchanged.

The baseline is the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main
`568731206e30`. Speedup is main time divided by this PR time, so values
above 1 mean faster. With sampling, W7040_64k goes from 2.8787 to 2.4940
ms (1.154x) on GB200 and from 3.2010 to 2.6840 ms (1.193x) on B200. With
sampling off, W7040_256k goes from 13.4798 to 12.2085 ms (1.104x) on
GB200 and from 15.2040 to 13.2028 ms (1.152x) on B200. Calls whose plan
does not change launch the same program on both sides.

| speedup range | GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs, CUDA 13.4) | B200 (sm_100a,
148 SMs, CUDA 13.4) |
|---|---|---|
| band rows whose plan changes, sampling on | 1.124x (W7040_40k) to
1.154x (W7040_64k), 5 rows | 1.167x (G3520x64k_s2) to 1.193x
(W7040_64k), 6 rows |
| band rows whose plan changes, sampling off | 1.054x (G3520x64k_s2) to
1.104x (W7040_256k), 5 rows | 1.095x (W7040_64k) to 1.152x (W7040_256k),
6 rows |
| prepared calls, sampling on (32 rows, plan unchanged) | 0.985x (A2) to
1.022x (Z1k256) | 0.982x (P1_peaked) to 1.040x (P3) |
| prepared calls, sampling off (32 rows, plan unchanged) | 0.986x
(Z1k4096) to 1.008x (A2) | 0.986x (Z1) to 1.012x (C3) |
| eager entry (8 rows, plan unchanged) | 0.992x (A1) to 1.000x (A3) |
0.993x (A2) to 1.006x (S2) |

### [90276bd](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/90276bdb15fb696d38d62bb1a87ddf04191ad45b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T19:40:07Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): stream macro batch 0's unaliased minibatches ahead of macro batch 1's combine in the sm_107a MXFP8 forward (#7821) (#8988)

FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel family covers
forward, full-forward checkpoint recompute and backward. It has four
variants: BF16 or MXFP8 routed experts, each with plain or clamped
SwiGLU. This PR speeds up the MXFP8 forward kernel on sm_107a, for both
plain and clamped SwiGLU, when a rank's padded schedule holds exactly
two macro batches of 262144 rows (for #7821).

Previously, the communication CTAs streamed macro batch 1 first. They
then blocked in its combine's `y_ready` wait until the shared-expert
phase and macro batch 1's down tiles finished, which delayed macro batch
0's dispatch. This PR adds a new sm_107a build,
`forward_mxfp8[_clamped]_multimacro`, which works in three parts. Macro
batch 0 computes its minibatches in rotated order, beginning with the
ones that macro batch 1 does not alias. The communication CTAs stream
those rows right after macro batch 1's rows and before macro batch 1's
combine. Macro batch 0's combine walks its tiles in the same rotated
order. Every task still writes the same bytes once.

Each rank picks the build per launch from the same lagged, asynchronous
observation of its padded schedule row count (`num_tokens`) that the
communication-SM split already uses. It uses the multimacro build
exactly when that count fills two macro batches. In every other case the
default build runs: no observation yet, one macro batch, three or more,
schedule capacity of at most one macro batch, or a GPU other than
sm_107a. Both builds produce bitwise identical outputs, saved context
and gradients for any schedule. Ranks can therefore run different builds
in one step, and a stale choice only costs time. During CUDA Graph
capture the current choice is kept, and `comm_split_log=True` prints
each change of the choice. The default sm_107a build, all sm_100a and
sm_103a kernels, and the backward and recompute kernels are unchanged,
and no workspace is added.

At T=27116 with uniform routing, each rank has one macro batch. At hot
2x, the hot rank needs three macro batches and runs the default build.
Both of those rows are expected to stay at parity. At T=32768 uniform
and at hot 1.25x, the relevant ranks have two macro batches.

macro batch 262144 rows. "Before" is FlashInfer main at e7ec0e68 and
"after" is the same main plus this change. These numbers were measured
before #8919 (MXFP8 backward speedup) landed. This branch is based on a
newer main that includes #8919. The forward kernels and the host
selection code are byte-identical to the ones measured. The backward
kernel is the one from #8919, and this PR does not change it. Each value
is the mean of 4 runs per side in recompute mode, in the order before,
after, after, before, after, before, before, after. In forward replay
mode, each value is the mean of 2 runs per side, in the order before,
after, after, before. Runs were interleaved on the same two nodes, and
SM clocks agree within 5 MHz. The backward kernel SASS is identical on
both sides, even though backward differs at T=32768 (0.991x in recompute
mode, 0.983x in forward replay). The microbatch and training-update
times include these backward differences. Peak memory per rank is
identical in every workload. Outputs, input gradients, routing-score
gradients and weight gradients are bitwise identical to before on all 8
ranks, with FP32 weight-gradient accumulators seeded identically.*

The family also ships the BF16 routed-expert variants and the MXFP8
backward and recompute kernels, and every variant runs on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a; the multimacro forward build is sm_107a only.

### [b1cc4f3](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b1cc4f35a5e30bdf378ccb5f6c398ce154375774)

- **作者**: Yuxian Qiu
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T19:32:26Z
- **提交信息**: feat(prims-ts): support independently inferred device global scales (#8093)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Dynamic per-input FP8 attention, including TRT-LLM VisualGen, computes
current-input descales on the GPU. Its effective QK multiplier is
attention_scale * q_descale * k_descale and its output multiplier
includes v_descale. Converting those values to Python floats requires
device-to-host synchronization; caching them once would use stale
scales, and captured floats cannot observe later GPU updates. Add
independent host-float or scalar-shaped or one-element CUDA FP32 global
scales throughout PrimTS while retaining runtime scalar values and
existing quantization/layout gates.

`plan()` infers each argument kind from its scale defaults. `run()`
inherits omitted defaults or binds same-kind overrides. Callers can
independently select float/float, float/tensor, tensor/float, or
tensor/tensor without a separate mode flag. Softmax scales use
natural-exponential units for either type. Tensor values are read inside
the GPU kernel; type and metadata checks never read their contents.

Coverage includes contiguous/paged context, standard and prepared
decode, QToken sparse attention, dense/sparse MLA, and contiguous/paged
block-sparse attention. Sparse MLA also supports a device
`kv_cache_scale` for its FP8-primary format. Block-sparse attention
gains an optional global `output_scale` multiplier. Existing Sage/VC
block/channel scale tensors and generated output-quantization scale
buffers keep their separate roles.

Compilation and persistent-cache identities include only the
independently inferred scale kinds, never values or tensor addresses.
Global softmax conversion uses FP32 arithmetic: float operands convert
in compiled host launchers, and tensor operands load/convert in device
kernels; the standalone decode reducer drops unused scale arguments.
Trace schemas and examples represent device inputs without scalar
readback.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- #6925 introduced the current host-runtime global-scale ABI.
- #8021 covers paged decode with a paired device-scale flag. This PR
includes that behavior through independent type inference and covers the
other PrimTS entry points.
- NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#21354 preserves live FP8 context scales in its
upstream refresh compatibility patch.

### Host-float regression check

On the same B300 allocation, two ABBA blocks (eight fresh processes,
four per revision) compare main `17481d293` with review-fix revision
`3e75b4499`. Each process uses deterministic inputs, preallocated
outputs, 20 warmup calls, and 31 samples. CPU submission uses batches of
eight eager `validate=False` calls with synchronization outside the
timed segment; GPU timing uses CUDA events around a 32-call graph. All
independent reference checks pass before and after timing. Numbers below
are medians of the four process medians.

| Host-float case | CPU submission, main → revised | Change | Graph GPU,
main → revised |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Context BF16 B1 H32/Hkv32 D128 Q/K2048 | 5.740 → 5.874 us | +2.34% |
36.920 → 36.919 us |
| Decode BF16 B4 H8/Hkv2 D128 KV4096 | 17.067 → 16.618 us | -2.63% |
6.695 → 6.695 us |

At that revision, these three representative host-float cases did not
show the reported 10–16% submission regression; they do not establish
performance across all shapes or a model-throughput improvement.
Measurements are scoped to prepared-wrapper calls and use the same test
fixtures and dependency stack on both revisions.

### Ordering and cache corrections

- Omitted runtime scales reuse normalized plan operands through
`resolve_scale`; both context wrappers use that helper directly. Context
passes original operands to `FmhaTs.__call__()` and uses FP32 for both
conversion paths. Its input-bound check protects the later launcher
conversion without inspecting tensor values. Mixed internal operands are
named `softmax_scale_operand`; `scale_softmax_log2` identifies resolved
base-2 scalars.
- Device scale loads in persistent decode occur after the existing
deferred dependency acquire and split pruning, immediately before task
execution, preserving prologue overlap.
- The nonpersistent decode acquire precedes producer-owned packed-Q
offsets used for tile pruning.
- The 2CTA MLA producer now waits before reading producer-owned inputs.
This fixes a pre-existing PDL race and also affects host-float
execution. The new producer wait follows the existing nonpersistent
split-KV launch condition. Producer/reducer PDL otherwise retains the
existing scheduling conditions.
- The standalone reducer's persistent identity canonicalizes scale kinds
because its ABI does not contain scale operands.
- All eight affected trace dispatchers publish canonical tensor-scale
variants for Trace Apply. Bound scale defaults and zero-dimensional
views reach replacement solutions; 36 real routing cases and eight
registry checks cover this integration. The shared resolver reuses
runtime validation for host values and CUDA device placement, while
preserving CPU/meta schema-only tracing and omitted defaults. Invalid
host values and malformed or misplaced tensors fall back to the original
API instead of reaching a replacement solution. Existing
dynamic-template fallback for plan-specific decode/MLA wrappers is
preserved.

### [e9735b0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/e9735b0239f834fa2f46a633e7ab76be49a2cc06)

- **作者**: akshaver
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T19:13:36Z
- **提交信息**: feat(trace_apply): dynamic loading of verified kernel packages (#8866)

## 📌 Description

Dynamic loading of verified kernel packages for Trace Apply, plus an
optional per-solution setup step.

- **Sealed kernel packages** (`flashinfer/trace_apply/packages.py`): a
Solution shipped as a directory named by the sha256 of its manifest.
Every byte is verified before import, the code runs in a digest-private
namespace, and the entry point registers as *preloaded* through a small
`apply.py` seam, so sealed sources never touch the on-disk solution
cache. Loaded at `import flashinfer` from `FLASHINFER_KERNEL_PACKAGES` /
`FLASHINFER_KERNEL_PACKAGE_ROOT` (kill switch
`FLASHINFER_KERNEL_PLUGINS_DISABLE`), best effort and never breaking the
import; refusals are `RuntimeError`, never `ImportError`.
- **Setup step** (`flashinfer/trace_apply/setup.py`): optional
`setup_entry_point` / `teardown_entry_point` / `setup_inputs` /
`setup_state_param` on `BuildSpec` let a Solution prepare weights once
per weight set (its own layout, say) outside the timed path and outside
CUDA-graph capture. State is keyed on the identity of the declared
tensors and passed to `run` by keyword. The fields are hashed only when
set, so existing Solution hashes are unchanged.

Docs: `docs/trace_apply.rst`.

## 🧭 How to use it

A complete example is preserved at
`tests/cpu/trace_apply/data/kernel_package/48812d76b7d3073a961dc996d6968e09998bae895ff83f3a175fe7f98cb26280/`
and served end to end by the tests.

1. Write the kernel; if it wants its own weight layout, add a setup
step:

   ```python
# prepare.py: once per weight set, eager, never under CUDA-graph capture
   def setup(context):
       weight = context["setup_inputs"]["weight"]
       return {"weight_f32": weight.float().contiguous()}

   def teardown(state):
       state.clear()

# kernel.py: Definition inputs by keyword, the state, the output buffer
   def run(hidden_states, weight, state, output):
       ...
   ```

2. Declare it in `solution.json`:

   ```json
"spec": {"language": "python", "entry_point": "kernel.py::run",
"destination_passing_style": true,
"setup_entry_point": "prepare.py::setup", "teardown_entry_point":
"prepare.py::teardown",
"setup_inputs": ["weight"], "setup_state_param": "state",
"target_hardware": ["sm100"]}
   ```

3. Seal it: put the files under `bundle/`, write `manifest.json` =
`{"schema_version": 1, "files": {<path>: <sha256>}, "bundle_sha256":
<sha256 of the sorted "name\0digest\n" listing>, "sealed_files":
{<sidecar>: <sha256>}}`, and name the directory `sha256(manifest.json)`.

4. Load it: `FLASHINFER_KERNEL_PACKAGE_ROOT=<root>
FLASHINFER_KERNEL_PACKAGES=<digest>` before `import flashinfer`, or
`flashinfer.trace_apply.load_packages(root, [digest])`.
`flashinfer.trace_apply.setup_stats()` reports `runs` and `weight_sets`
per Definition.

### [2eb2e8c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2eb2e8cb1c46b324567df66385c25326e7067089)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T19:04:05Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): sm_107a FP8 runs an l6 snake program on short single-document calls (#8986)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`
is the deterministic DSA indexer top-k. It has two Cake variants: the
default BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 form (`float8_e4m3fn` q / k with a
per-key FP32 `k_scale`). This PR changes only the FP8 form, and only on
sm_107a. Earlier FP8 PRs: #8749 added the FP8 form and #8781 improved
it. #8841 / #8895 / #8933 added an FP8 wide program on sm_103a / sm_100a
/ sm_107a, #8954 picks the FP8 wide unit by wave count on sm_100a, and
#8976 made the sm_100a FP8 l6 programs load K_scale one tile ahead. Here
sm_107a gains an FP8 l6 scan program (the 6-query unit) in snake unit
order. It is the FP8 counterpart of the BF16 form's existing sm_107a l6
snake program. The FP8 dispatch runs it only on single-document calls
that meet two conditions. The dispatch decision must mark the call snake
(on sm_107a: at least half a query per key and at least 32 mean unit
tiles), and the call must need at most 40 waves of the l6 persistent
grid, with waves = ceil(ceil(T / 6) / grid). The baseline is the FP8
dispatch before this PR. Every other call keeps its previous program,
and ids and scores are bit-identical to the previous dispatch on every
measured row.

**sm_107a (212 SMs), CUDA 13.4 (13.4.92), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.**

Each time is the CUPTI GPU interval over every kernel of the call.
Settings: cold L2, eager launch, 3 warm-up iterations, 20 repetitions.
Cake arms time a prepared runner (scan, merge, finalize) into
caller-owned outputs and workspace. Each run's value is the median over
three arm orders (A then B, B then A, interleaved). The table gives the
median over runs. Runs are separate processes on separate GPUs of one
node. There are 2 runs per row for the owner shapes and for the 32768 /
36864 / 40960 / 49152 rows, and 4 runs for the 8192 / 16384 rows of the
second table. "Previous Cake FP8" is the FP8 dispatch before this PR,
which runs the plain l6 program on the rows this PR moves. "This PR" is
the l6 snake program that this PR's dispatch selects on those rows,
timed in the same process. Rows the dispatch does not move run the same
program before and after this PR. For them, "This PR" is an A/A twin of
the previous arm, so their ratio is parity by construction. "vs
previous" is previous time / this PR time (above 1 = faster). An A/A
twin bounds the noise: a row counts as a speedup only when every run and
every order exceeds 1 + the row's A/A band. On s3_cold16k the A/A band
is 0.0007 and the per-order ratios are 1.023 to 1.028. P1's A/A band is
0.0107. All rows use top-k 2048, key ratio 1 and causal masking (each
segment's queries are its last positions). P1 is a recorded packed
training call with 8 segments. s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries over
18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352 keys.

| Shape | Queries T | Keys Tkv | Segments | Program after this PR |
Previous Cake FP8 (ms) | This PR (ms) | vs previous | DeepGEMM +
FlashInfer top-k (ms) | vs DeepGEMM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| P1 | 16231 | 268757 | 8 | l6 (unchanged) | 2.1679 | 2.1500 | 1.008x
(parity) | n/a (device-side assert) | n/a |
| glm2k_16k | 2048 | 16384 | 1 | l6 (unchanged) | 0.1751 | 0.1749 |
1.001x (parity) | n/a (device-side assert) | n/a |
| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | wide (unchanged) | 1.8161 | 1.8210 |
0.997x (parity) | n/a (device-side assert) | n/a |
| s2_4x2k_packed | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | l6 (unchanged) | 1.7314 | 1.7322
| 1.000x (parity) | n/a (device-side assert) | n/a |
| s3_cold16k | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | l6 snake (13 waves) | 0.7047 | 0.6875
| 1.025x | n/a (device-side assert) | n/a |

Other single-document calls that the dispatch moves to the snake
program:

| Queries T | Keys Tkv | l6 waves | Previous Cake FP8 (ms) | This PR
(ms) | vs previous |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 | 8192 | 7 | 0.2475 | 0.2333 | 1.061x |
| 8192 | 16384 | 7 | 0.4952 | 0.4900 | 1.011x |
| 16384 | 16384 | 13 | 0.7085 | 0.6873 | 1.031x |
| 16384 | 20480 | 13 | 0.9396 | 0.9274 | 1.013x |
| 32768 | 32768 | 26 | 2.2620 | 2.2471 | 1.007x |
| 36864 | 36864 | 29 | 2.7845 | 2.7616 | 1.008x |
| 40960 | 40960 | 33 | 3.3407 | 3.3204 | 1.006x |
| 49152 | 49152 | 39 | 4.6335 | 4.6144 | 1.004x |

Forcing the snake program measured 0.970x-0.982x on packed equal
documents (2 x 16384 up to 4 x 32768 queries), parity at 65536 and
262144 queries and 0.993x-0.995x at 131072, 524288 and 1048576 queries,
so the dispatch keeps those calls on the plain l6 program.

The default BF16 form is unchanged. Both Cake forms ship on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a, and the FP8 form has a wide program on all three
and, after this PR, an l6 snake program on sm_107a.
