### [cf89246](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/cf89246b2ea8c5e960f10f45131fe89a7a189a27)

- **作者**: NVJiangShao
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T18:55:34Z
- **提交信息**: feat(experimental): add SM100/SM103 HC sum-state backend (#8944)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds a standalone SM100/SM103 low-rank HyperConnection backend that
carries FP32 per-branch square sums between layers. It folds and packs
Down+Inject weights, fuses the small-T projection epilogues and
Apply+statistics, and provides the large-T path, explicit workspaces and
state/context APIs. It builds on SGLang's original HC implementation and
ports the subsequent optimization work from sgl-project/sglang#40552;
source provenance is recorded in
`flashinfer/experimental/hc_sum_sm100/SOURCES.md`.

The new carried-state API enters the experimental track while its
integration contract and hardware coverage are established. The backend
runs independently of SGLang. Its API, numerical contract and supported
layouts are documented in
`flashinfer/experimental/hc_sum_sm100/README.md`.

**Measured HC kernel performance**

Matched GB300/SM103 measurements, BF16, C=4, H=2560, lowrank=320,
default atomic mode. Baseline: SGLang main
`8884b4b42137c9447328f84127e220e6dc239d8a`. The metric is the sum of NCU
`gpu__time_duration.sum` for mix+apply within each invocation, then the
median of 24 invocations per implementation/T. Application replay,
cache-control none, clock-control none; all collected kernels used a
single replay pass. Weight preparation, allocation, bootstrap, core
computation, compilation and host overhead are excluded.

| T | SGLang main (us) | FlashInfer (us) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 13.712 | 10.880 | 1.260× |
| 2 | 15.808 | 10.912 | 1.449× |
| 4 | 16.032 | 10.944 | 1.465× |
| 8 | 16.432 | 11.392 | 1.442× |
| 16 | 19.744 | 12.592 | 1.568× |
| 24 | 23.344 | 15.088 | 1.547× |
| 25 | 24.960 | 17.120 | 1.458× |
| 64 | 25.280 | 17.856 | 1.416× |
| 256 | 31.200 | 23.472 | 1.329× |
| 2048 | 92.624 | 71.584 | 1.294× |
| 8192 | 302.288 | 259.152 | 1.166× |

Across these 11 T values, this backend achieves a **1.394×
geometric-mean speedup**, with a peak of **1.568× at T=16**. Speedup is
`baseline_time / FI_time`.

Within this same measurement, the small-T path (T ≤ 24, six cases) has a
geometric-mean speedup of **1.452×**; the large-T path (T > 24, five
cases) has **1.329×**. Both groups remain in the full table and overall
aggregate. Kernel-duration sums do not represent service throughput or
an elapsed window with overlapping kernels.

A separate matched comparison with the already-optimized SGLang
implementation `9cdd6624fe115979b0a0e6c588d9de5ddfeaafe2` gave a
geometric-mean speedup of **0.999587× (approximately 1.000×)**, with
per-T speedups from 0.984× to 1.013×, measured as `optimized_SGLang_time
/ FI_time`. This checks performance preservation during the port. The
two comparisons were separate runs; their absolute times should not be
mixed.

The runnable FI-side profiling harness is
`benchmarks/experimental/bench_hc_sum_sm100.py`, with NCU invocation
instructions in its module docstring.

## Reviewer Notes

The carried state contains FP32 square sums of the update before the
BF16/FP16 storage cast; consumers must use the documented state
contract. Folding RMS weights changes rounding relative to an unfused
checkpoint computation. References and tolerances model these stages
explicitly.

GPU validation is on GB300/SM103. Physical SM100 hardware, MIG and
green-context partitions have not been validated. The small path
requires non-portable 16-CTA cluster launch support. This backend is
JIT-only and needs the experimental CUDA sources shipped with the
installation. Tracking issue, maintenance owner and graduation target
remain to be assigned with maintainers.

### [79c568d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/79c568d2a8036bfd5c7a8b51517cc08253e43593)

- **作者**: S.J. Lee
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T18:17:47Z
- **提交信息**: fix(moe_ep): handle empty local batches in two-sided combine (#8821)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`NVLinkTwoSidedAlltoAll.combine` reshapes the returned top-k slots with
an inferred last dimension. When a rank has no local tokens the tensor
has no elements, so PyTorch can't infer that dimension and raises:

```
RuntimeError: cannot reshape tensor of 0 elements into shape [0, 2, -1] because the unspecified dimension size -1 can be any value and is ambiguous
```

A rank can legitimately have no local tokens in a step while still
serving tokens from other ranks, so it has to keep taking part in both
collectives. This passes the hidden size explicitly instead of `-1`, so
an empty rank runs the return collective as before and gets a `[0,
hidden]` result. For non-empty batches the explicit size is the one
PyTorch inferred before.

The host-side two-sided test now also dispatches and combines an empty
local batch, once without an `output` buffer and once with the 3D
`expert_output` form and an empty `output` buffer. It checks the `[0,
hidden]` shape, that the supplied buffer is returned, and that the
return all-to-all is still called. The existing non-empty case keeps
checking the top-k reduction.

### [5dbf6b8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/5dbf6b8a6c203d9849084f1ddeee4f4a44ac30ae)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T17:44:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8): two early-setup sm_107a programs for the N=4096 K=7168 and N=7168 K=2048 bands (#8981)

`cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8` is Cake's FP8 masked batched GEMM (NT layout,
float32 block scales, DeepGEMM masked API). It has one route chain per
architecture: sm_100a (148 SMs), sm_103a (152 SMs) and sm_107a (216
SMs). FlashInfer main ships 68 programs, 12 of them on sm_107a. With
this PR it ships 70, with 14 on sm_107a, and sm_100a and sm_103a are
unchanged. This PR adds two sm_107a programs that use early setup:
masked_m is read once per CTA and prefetched, setup is split, and tensor
memory is freed early. The first is
`cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8_40c9c1d3f7d59ad4b451` (BLOCK_N 96, 7 stages, K
tile 128). The second is `cake_batch_deepgemm_fp8_c6484b37ae389e3495bf`
(BLOCK_N 128, 5 stages, K tile 128). On sm_107a, a key that took the
N=4096 K=7168 BLOCK_N 144 band or the N=7168 K=2048 BLOCK_N 112 band now
goes to the narrowest new program whose worst-case tile count, B *
min(ceil(M/128), ceil(expected_m/128)+1) * ceil(N/BLOCK_N), fits in one
wave of 216. BLOCK_N 128 is used only for N=4096. Cells, all other keys
and the N=4096 K=7168 BLOCK_N 112 band keep their programs. Compared
with main, only these keys move: 452 points for N=4096 K=7168 and 867
for N=7168 K=2048. The baseline is the previous Cake programs that main
routes for the same keys: BLOCK_N 144, 3 stages, K tile 256
(`fa7c913fa26439d68c52`), and BLOCK_N 112, 6 stages, K tile 128
(`2dba8870634863384b03`). The new programs' outputs are bitwise equal to
the previous ones on every measured row.

Measured on NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs) with CUDA 13.4.2. Latency is
CUPTI kernel time, with L2 flushed before each timed launch and 10
warmup launches. The previous and new arms ran in ABBA order x 3 blocks
under one GPU hold, with operand seeds 50, 51 and 52. Times are the mean
over the 3 seeds. Speedup is 1 / (geometric mean over the 3 seeds of the
paired new/previous ratio); above 1 is faster. The per-seed column gives
the range of the paired new/previous ratio across seeds. Each row's
verdict uses a rule fixed before measurement: FASTER if every seed's
new/previous < 1 - max(noise, 0.005). The A/A control gave max |A/A - 1|
= 0.0023. The table covers every measured shape of the moved keys. These
are the moved rows of the representative set, plus two shapes for each
row of the new route: a worst-case shape (every group's masked_m at the
bound) and a typical DeepGEMM-mask shape. All 28 rows are faster, by
1.0208x-1.1631x. B=1 M=640 N=4096 K=7168 (DeepGEMM mask, expected_m=504)
was measured twice with the same inputs, and both rows are listed.

### [b53d496](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/b53d49643110aea20bf9b0f418c6514b29e600d9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T17:21:20Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_lm_head_det_train): rename the deterministic LM head training entries and drop the deterministic routing (#8925)

## Description

On main, `flashinfer.chunked_lm_head_*` runs the deterministic LM head
package by default. It also falls back to that package when torch's
deterministic mode is on. With this PR, that routing no longer exists.
The deterministic LM head entries now live in a new stable top-level
module, `flashinfer.cake_lm_head_det_train`, and their names state the
mode.

This PR covers the deterministic LM head family under #8928. Under that
issue, Cake training kernel names state their mode, and there is no
`deterministic=` keyword and no alias. The non-deterministic side
(`flashinfer.cake_lm_head_nondet_train`) comes in a separate PR from its
owner. That PR merges right after this one.

`flashinfer.cake_lm_head_det_train` exports
`cake_lm_head_det_train_{loss,logprob,preload,support_logprob,support_kl}`
in `__all__`. These entries use `@flashinfer_api` instead of the
experimental decorator, so they emit no `ExperimentalWarning`. The
module imports the backend lazily.

No entry, forwarded backend entry or autograd `Function.forward` accepts
`deterministic`. Passing it raises `TypeError`. Old names fail at import
because there are no aliases.

The five non-deterministic `chunked_lm_head_*` dispatchers stay in
`flashinfer.chunked_lm_head` until the non-deterministic rename PR
replaces that module. If they are called without `deterministic=False`,
they raise `ValueError` and the message names the deterministic entry to
use. They never route to the deterministic package.

Kernels, programs and numerics are unchanged.

### Migration

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| `flashinfer.chunked_lm_head` (det entries) |
`flashinfer.cake_lm_head_det_train` |
| `chunked_lm_head_det_loss` | `cake_lm_head_det_train_loss` |
| `chunked_lm_head_det_logprob` | `cake_lm_head_det_train_logprob` |
| `chunked_lm_head_det_preload` | `cake_lm_head_det_train_preload` |
| `chunked_lm_head_det_support_logprob` |
`cake_lm_head_det_train_support_logprob` |
| `chunked_lm_head_det_support_kl` | `cake_lm_head_det_train_support_kl`
|
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_lm_head_det_loss` |
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_det_train` (same submodules:
`cake_backend`, `cake_backend_opt_in`, `cake_support`, `cake_jit`,
`cake_build`) |
| backend
`chunked_lm_head_det_{loss,logprob,logprob_temperature,logprob_keep}` |
`cake_lm_head_det_train_{loss,logprob,logprob_temperature,logprob_keep}`
|
| opt-in `preload` | `cake_lm_head_det_train_preload` |
| `cake_support` `chunked_lm_head_det_support_{logprob,kl}` |
`cake_lm_head_det_train_support_{logprob,kl}` |
| `ChunkedLmHeadDetLossFunction` | `CakeLMHeadDetLossFunction` |
| `ChunkedLmHeadDetLogprobFunction` | `CakeLMHeadDetLogprobFunction` |
| `ChunkedLmHeadDetLogprobTemperatureFunction` |
`CakeLMHeadDetLogprobTemperatureFunction` |
| `ChunkedLmHeadDetLogprobKeepFunction` |
`CakeLMHeadDetLogprobKeepFunction` |
| `SupportDetLogprobFunction` | `CakeLMHeadDetSupportFunction` (one
class serves both support entries) |
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_lm_head_loss` (alias package) | removed,
no replacement |
| the 12 pre-det names the det modules still defined | removed |
| `chunked_lm_head_*` without `deterministic=False` | `ValueError`
naming the det entry |

### Unchanged

The private module `flashinfer/_cake_lm_head_train_knobs.py` now holds
the shared env-var parsing. The code moved there unchanged. The
`FLASHINFER_CAKE_LM_HEAD_LOSS_*` variable names and their behaviour are
the same, and both modes read them.

These build identities and internal helpers keep their old names. In
`build.json`, only `"package"` changes.

| Kept | Items |
| --- | --- |
| Program/library stems | `cake_lm_head_det_loss_<20 hex>[_<arch>]` |
| Source directory | `csrc/cake_lm_head_det_loss/` |
| Kernel symbols | unchanged |
| `cake_jit` registry keys and loader |
`cake_lm_head_det_loss_sm_10{0,3,7}a`,
`load_cake_lm_head_det_loss_module` |
| Internal helpers (not forwarded by the facade) |
`prepare_lm_head_det_loss`, `validate_lm_head_det_inputs`,
`lm_head_det_loss_workspace_size`, `LmHeadDetLossRunner` |

### Other edits

| Area | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Tests and bench | Renamed to
`test_cake_lm_head_det_train{,_api,_host_state,_standalone,_support}.py`
and `bench_cake_lm_head_det_train.py` |
| New `tests/experimental/test_cake_lm_head_det_train_names.py` | Checks
the mode word by token. Checks that `bind_partial(deterministic=False)`
raises `TypeError` on 5 facade entries, 18 forwarded backend entries and
8 autograd forwards. Checks that old modules and names fail to import. |
| Non-deterministic package tests, bench and messages | Only the
deterministic names are substituted |
| `flashinfer/experimental/cake/__init__.py` | Namespace docstring now
covers both modes' backends |
| Docs and config | LM head sections of
`docs/training_backend_names.md`, env table rows in `CLAUDE.md`, the det
README, det paths in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` |

## Related Issues

- Part of #8928. This PR covers the LM head det family.
- Answers review
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8907#pullrequestreview-5796227300.
- The rules text is in #8930.
- The non-deterministic rename (`flashinfer.cake_lm_head_nondet_train`)
follows in a separate PR.

## Tests

Latest-head manual [CI run

at `d4f2513765ad017a1bd7b7574a69b183959dbded` passed: targeted H100

### [22092e0](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/22092e01fad031073e5865622d0adda6bdd0f1f1)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T17:09:21Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): sm_100a FP8 l6 programs load K_scale one tile ahead (#8976)

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train.cake_dsa_indexer_det_train_topk`
is the deterministic DSA indexer top-k. It has two Cake variants: the
default BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 form (`float8_e4m3fn` q / k with a
per-key FP32 `k_scale`). This PR changes only the FP8 form, and only on
sm_100a. Earlier FP8 PRs: #8749 added the FP8 form and #8781 improved
it. #8841 / #8895 / #8933 added an FP8 wide program on sm_103a / sm_100a
/ sm_107a, and #8954 picks the FP8 wide unit by wave count on sm_100a.

This PR changes the FP8 l6 scan program (the 6-query unit) and its
longest-segment-first copy. In both, each fold thread now loads the next
key tile's `K_scale` right after the current tile's scores, so that load
overlaps the fold instead of stalling it. Both programs are renamed, and
their registry entries follow the new names. Dispatch is unchanged, so
every call picks the same program kind as before. Calls that run the l6
unit gain 0.8% to 1.7%: s3_cold16k at 1.008x, plus L3, M5, X8, X9 and
X10 below. After #8954, P1, glm2k_16k, s1_8k_on_64k and s2_4x2k_packed
run the wide unit on sm_100a. They run the same program as before, so
their ratio is parity within noise, not a speedup.

**NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4 (13.4.92), PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.** Each time is the CUPTI GPU interval over every kernel
the call launches, with cold L2, eager launch, 3 warm-up iterations and
20 repetitions. Cake arms time a prepared runner (scan, merge, finalize)
that writes into caller-owned outputs and workspace. Each run's value is
the median over three arm orders (A then B, B then A, interleaved). Each
row was measured on two GPUs of one node in separate processes, and the
table gives the median of the two runs. "Previous Cake FP8" is the FP8
form on FlashInfer main before this PR, loaded as a second package in
the same process. "vs previous" = previous time / this PR time (above 1
= faster). A/A twins of both packages bound the noise: a row counts as a
speedup only when every run and every order exceeds 1 + the row's
largest deviation of A/A from 1. Rows marked "wide (unchanged)" run the
same program as before this PR, and their ratio is parity within noise.
"DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k" is the non-Cake reference measured the
same way as in #8954 / #8895. It runs DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits`
(branch `nv_dev`, commit `b64107f2`) with FP32 per-key K scales and FP32
logits, then FlashInfer `top_k_ragged_transform(deterministic=True,
tie_break=LARGE)` over each row's visible keys. "vs DeepGEMM" = DeepGEMM
time / this PR time. All arms return bit-identical scores and ids on
every row. All rows use top-k 2048, key ratio 1 and causal masking (each
segment's queries are its last positions). P1 is a recorded packed
training call. s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries over 18432 / 43008 /
67584 / 100352 keys.

### [3b349c5](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3b349c5b73df1533ca7b111c3a551f198465a1d8)

- **时间**: 2026-11-06T16:50:16Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): SM107a lead-prefetch route for more BLOCK_N 256 single-run layouts (#8979)

`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm` is Cake's prepared contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM.
On sm_100a and sm_103a it ships three variants: FP32-scale programs,
block-scaled programs with packed UE8M0 scales, and a fused gate_up +
SwiGLU + FP8 quant form. On sm_107a it ships only the block-scaled UE8M0
variant. This PR changes only the sm_107a host route rule and does not
change kernel code. It follows #8972, which shipped the current sm_107a
programs. The host sends some layouts to the BLOCK_N 256 single-run
program. In two more cases, those layouts now take the existing
lead-prefetch program instead: K at most 256 with at most 10 routed rows
per group, and K above 256 with at least 160 routed rows per group. The
lead-prefetch program is the same program, except that it reads each
tile's leading row index from a shared-memory table filled at kernel
entry. The previous lead-prefetch cases are unchanged. Output bits are
identical to the BLOCK_N 256 single-run program. The baseline is the
previous Cake route for these shapes: the BLOCK_N 256 single-run program
without the table.

### [7b93789](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7b93789dd6d2ef440f9c2c46c217f9b231b02f21)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T16:46:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): split SM107 FP8 128-head decode calls of 14-15 query rows into three pieces (#8978)

Cake's DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA attention for FlashInfer (`cake_dsv4`) on
FlashInfer main routes 32 call forms to 28 distinct programs on each of
sm_100a and sm_103a, covering BF16 and FP8 KV caches and 8 to 128 query
heads. It also has 9 FP8 programs for sm_107a. This PR adds no program
and changes no kernel. It changes only the host rule that sets how many
pieces each query row is split into on the sm_107a split-KV path that
#8950 added (FP8 KV cache, 128 heads, 1152 sparse keys per query or nine
128-key tiles, PDL on, 1 to 17 query rows). On main, the rule takes the
first of 9, 5, 3 and 2 pieces per row whose total pieces (rows x pieces)
are at most 40, so 14 to 17 rows run 2 pieces per row. In this PR each
piece count has its own cap, chosen by measurement: 9, 5 and 2 pieces
keep the cap of 40, and 3 pieces may go up to 45. As a result, 14 and 15
rows now run 3 pieces per row (42 and 45 pieces), and all other row
counts are unchanged. The baseline is the previous Cake version on
FlashInfer main (commit `34e455db`, which contains #8950). Against it,
for every key group except all 128-384, calls at 14 rows are 1.10x to
1.14x faster (0.93 to 1.17 us saved per call) and calls at 15 rows are
1.11x to 1.13x faster (0.91 to 1.13 us saved). The largest gain is the
mixed-keys batch at 14 rows (1.14x). Calls whose launch is unchanged
(13, 16 and 17 rows, and 4-token requests at 12 and 16 rows) give
bitwise-identical outputs to main and measure about 1.00x. When every
query in a 14- or 15-row batch attends at most 384 keys (three tiles),
each row fits one piece under both rules but the merge kernel still
runs. These calls are slightly slower than main: 7.79 to 7.83 us at 14
rows (0.995x, about 0.04 us slower) and 7.88 to 8.01 us at 15 rows
(0.98x, about 0.12 us slower). The host cannot detect this case because
request lengths live on the GPU, the same reason as in #8950.

Measured on an NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs) with the CUDA 13.4
runtime, in microseconds per call. Each call is one of 8 back-to-back
calls captured in one CUDA graph, with L2 flushed before each replay.
Each value is the median over 24 rounds (6 processes x 4 rounds), with
main (`34e455db`) and this PR timed in the same process in alternating
order, and speedup = main latency / this PR's latency.

- **Layer**: "c4 (32K context)" is the DeepSeek-V4 c4 layer at 32K-token
context, with 128 sliding-window keys plus 1024 top-k keys of the
4x-compressed cache per query. "c128 (128K context)" is the c128 layer
at 128K-token context, with 128 sliding-window keys plus 1024 keys of
the 128x-compressed cache.
- **Keys per query**: "all 1152" means every query attends all 1152
keys. "mixed" means every other query attends all 1152 keys and the
others attend 128-384. "all 128-640" means every query attends 128 to
640 keys (at most one piece under main's 2-piece split). "all 128-384"
means every query attends 128 to 384 keys (at most one piece under both
the 2- and 3-piece splits).
- **Query tokens per request**: 1 (decode) or 4 (multi-token).
- **Query rows T**: query rows in the call.
- **PDL**: programmatic dependent launch, on for every row.
- **Pieces per row (main → this PR)**: "2 → 3" means main runs 2 pieces
per row and this PR runs 3. A single number means unchanged.

### [a03c6c6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a03c6c668ef3fa68ef7899765602423330b91206)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T15:31:16Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det_train): fuse the first radix-select sweep in the sampled calls of the BF16 sm_103a l6 programs (#8974)

Cake ships two variants of its deterministic DSA indexer top-k
(`dsa_indexer_det_topk`) in FlashInfer: the BF16 form, which is the
default, and the opt-in FP8 (e4m3) form. This PR changes only the BF16
form. Within it, only the sm_103a scan programs of the l6 kind change:
the program that mid-size calls use and its longest-segment-first copy.
The FP8 form and the sm_100a and sm_107a programs are unchanged; the
family ships on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

In calls with the sampled threshold, the first radix-select pass now
also counts the second byte of the selected top-byte bucket, so most
calls skip one pass over the candidates. Calls with sampling off run as
before. Output bits are unchanged.

The baseline is the previous Cake version, FlashInfer main `34e476cb`.
Speedup is main time divided by this PR time, so values above 1 mean
faster. On GB300, prepared S1 with sampling goes from 0.3905 to 0.3864
ms (1.011x). With sampling, W4_8k goes from 0.0637 to 0.0625 ms (1.019x)
and G1024x8k_s2 goes from 0.2110 to 0.2067 ms (1.021x). Eager S1 goes
from 0.3923 to 0.3883 ms (1.010x). With sampling, the sweep rows range
from 1.005x (W16_8k) to 1.027x (G256x8k_s1, G1024x8k_s4).

### [3b38a32](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3b38a32596f143b43214a407f048079d150bfaf5)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T15:18:40Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_vsa_sm120): charge a split part more once K and V pass half the L2 (#8973)

`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="vsa_sm120_blk64")` on SM120 /
SM121 has 4 Cake variants: the BF16 and FP16 builds of two persistent
kernels, `vsa_sm120_blk64` (two 128-thread CTAs per SM) and
`vsa_sm120_blk64_pair` (one CTA of two 4-warp groups per SM). Both
kernels run one host plan, and the host planner picks the kernel per
shape. The kernels cover head dim 128, 64 x 64 blocks, GQA and optional
LSE. This PR changes only the host planner (Python). The kernels, the
API and the numerics contract are unchanged. When the work items
outnumber the virtual CTAs, the planner charges each split part an extra
cost of 2. That extra is now 4 once the K and V of all KV heads exceed
2048 blocks of 64 tokens (64 MB in 16 bits, half of the RTX PRO 6000's
L2). Past that size the blocks come from memory, so splitting a row to
fill the virtual CTAs gains less. The change applies to the uniform plan
and to the base plan of the packing stage. The packing itself is
unchanged. The plan changes on 5 of the 100 measured shapes. Each of
them now splits its rows less or not at all, and one of them also
switches from `vsa_sm120_blk64` to `vsa_sm120_blk64_pair`. The other 95
shapes run the same plan and the same kernels as main, and their outputs
are unchanged. The baseline is FlashInfer main at `7a0a609f`, which runs
the previous Cake version of these kernels and planner (from #8799,
#8829, #8898 and #8940). Speedup = main / this PR, so a value above 1
means this PR is faster. Across all 100 shapes, the geomean speedup is
1.006 with nvcc 13.0 (66 of 100 at or above 1.0, slowest 0.992) and
1.006 with nvcc 13.4 (58 of 100 at or above 1.0, slowest 0.989). On the
22 delivery shapes it is 1.000 with both nvcc 13.0 and nvcc 13.4. On the
5 shapes whose plan changes, the speedup is 1.05x-1.16x.

Measured on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120, 188
SMs, driver 595.84.01), with the kernels JIT-built by CUDA 13.0 and by
CUDA 13.4. `wrapper.run` latency is timed with CUPTI and a cold L2. Each
value is the median over 3 interleaved rounds x 3 input placements. The
Kernel column names the kernel that this PR's planner picks for each
shape ("blk64" or "pair", with "+ packed" when the plan packs short KV
lists).

The 95 shapes whose plan does not change run the same plan and the same
kernels in main and in this PR, so their spread is run-to-run noise.

SM100 / SM103 Blackwell (sm_100a, sm_103a); this SM120 family ships for
sm_120a and sm_121a.

### [da118eb](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/da118ebfdd5b54dfad95d09bffbba3b739ba27c2)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T14:59:06Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_dense_gemm): rename both packages to det and nondet (#8928) (#8926)

This PR implements the dense GEMM rows of #8928 for both modes in one
family PR. Under #8928, every Cake training kernel name states its mode
(`det` or `nondet`). Each module lives at the top level as
`flashinfer.cake_<op>_<mode>_train`, and its backend lives under
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/<module>/`. No entry point takes
`deterministic=`.

This PR was first scoped as "explicit `deterministic=False`, no det
aliases or routing". It now does the #8928 rename instead.

### Module location

This PR adds two top-level modules:

- `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train` (deterministic), with its
backend at `flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_dense_gemm_det_train/`
- `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train` (non-deterministic), with
its backend at
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train/`

Each backend directory moved as a whole: `build.json`, `cake_build.py`,
`cake_ffi_checks.h`, the generated `csrc/` sources, `cake_jit.py`,
`cake_backend.py` and the README.

Each top-level module imports its backend on the first attribute access
and returns the backend's own objects, so a call adds no Python layer.
`import flashinfer` imports neither backend.

### Behavior

The family targets SM100, SM103 and SM107 (`sm_100a`, `sm_103a`,
`sm_107a`) and has two kernels:

- K1: the BF16 dense projection GEMM. This covers forward `y[T,N] =
X[T,K] @ W[N,K].T`, dgrad, and wgrad `dW[N,K] = G[T,N].T @ X[T,K]`.
- K2: the FP32 router-gate GEMM, computed through split-BF16x3 emulation
(forward, dgrad, wgrad).

Torch deterministic mode means
`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`.

| Module | Torch deterministic mode off | Torch deterministic mode on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train` | Deterministic. The same
inputs, hardware and plan give bitwise the same outputs on every run. |
Deterministic. No entry point raises or warns. |
| `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train` | Non-deterministic. Split-K
reductions add partials in the order they finish, so results are not
bitwise reproducible across runs. | Some launches can give different
results from run to run: the K1 split-K program at three or more splits,
and any K2 stream-K partition that gives an element more than two
partials. These launches raise PyTorch's `RuntimeError` right before
they launch. With `warn_only=True` they emit a `UserWarning` and then
launch. Fixed-order launches do not alert. This module never falls back
to the det package. |

The torch setting never changes which program runs. The nondet module's
operations, view contract, dtypes and accuracy budgets are the same as
the det module's.

This PR does not change any kernel, program, planner rule or build. The
plans are byte-identical before and after the rename on `sm_100a`,
`sm_103a` and `sm_107a`. This was checked over every rule-table window
edge and over SM counts 148, 152, 208, 212 and 216. Generated kernel,
library and namespace names inside the backends do not change.

### Breaking changes

- The `deterministic=` keyword is removed. Passing it now raises
`TypeError`, like any unknown keyword.
- The old modules and names are removed with no aliases. Importing an
old module raises `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- The nondet plan and prepare functions no longer take `**kwargs`. They
now take explicit keyword-only knobs: the det planner's public knobs
plus `splits` and `chains`.

What `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm` meant depends on
the release:

- In v0.7.3 it was the deterministic package.
- In v0.7.4rc1 it was the numerical-mode package. The default
`deterministic=True` ran the deterministic programs, and
`deterministic=False` ran the non-deterministic ones.

In v0.7.4rc1, `flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm` was
the deterministic package.

Choose the new module based on the behavior you used, not on the old
path:

- Move to `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train` if you called
`dense_projection_gemm` in v0.7.3, relied on its default in v0.7.4rc1,
or called `dense_projection_det_gemm`.
- Move to `flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train` if you passed
`deterministic=False`.

knobs: the det planner's public knobs plus `splits`, `chains` |
| det former aliases (`GemmPlan`, `PreparedGemm`, `PreparedRouterGemm`,
`RouterPlan`, the 13 mode-less function names, `split_fp32_to_bf16x3_`),
det `cake_jit.load_cake_dense_projection_gemm_module`, the nondet

The second row maps the old package to the nondet module because it
follows the backend directory. A caller that used this package in
v0.7.3, or relied on its default in v0.7.4rc1, should move to
`flashinfer.cake_dense_gemm_det_train` instead. See Breaking changes.

### Backend directories and standalone build

| Old backend directory | New backend directory |
| --- | --- |
| `flashinfer/experimental/dense_projection_det_gemm/` |
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_dense_gemm_det_train/` |
| `flashinfer/experimental/dense_projection_gemm/` |
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train/` (in v0.7.3
the old directory was the deterministic package; see Breaking changes) |

For vendoring as in #6553, the det backend directory builds and runs on
its own.

The nondet backend directory has one declared dependency: the det
backend directory. It runs the det backend's fixed-order programs. Its
`build.json` declares the dependency as `common.requires.packages:
["cake_dense_gemm_det_train"]`, using sibling directory names. A
vendoring build ships the two directories next to each other.

The nondet package imports the det package lazily, as its sibling.
Inside a parent package, the sibling is
`<parent>.cake_dense_gemm_det_train`. When vendored at the top level, it
is `cake_dense_gemm_det_train`. Importing the nondet package never
imports the det package. If the det package is missing, the first use
raises `ImportError` naming it. If the det package is held under another
name, `use_deterministic_backend()` binds it.

Only the package chooses the mode. There is no `deterministic=` argument
and no environment variable.

The `PACKAGES` rows in `tests/test_helpers/cake_package.py` are updated.
`tests/experimental/test_cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train_standalone.py`
loads the nondet directory as a top-level package with `flashinfer`
blocked, with and without the det directory beside it.

### Old-name allowlist

A repository-wide grep for the old names passes with exactly this
allowlist.

| ID | Where | What | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A01 | `csrc/**` | any | Generated CUDA sources: library stems, kernel
namespaces, file names and templates are build identities kept
byte-for-byte. |
| A02 | the two backend `build.json` files | old public names (not old
paths) | Generated names kept; the `package` field names the new
package. |
| A03 | the two backend `cake_jit.py` files |
`dense_projection_det_gemm`, `dense_projection_gemm`,
`router_fp32_det_gemm`, `router_fp32_gemm` | Module, kernel and
generator identities (the `cake::<stem>::` namespaces and generator
module fragments). |
| A05 | det backend, det tests and bench | `instance_symbol` | Kept
internal helper of the det backend. |
| A06 | nondet backend, nondet tests and bench |
`load_cake_dense_projection_gemm_module` | Kept internal helper of the
nondet backend. |
| A07 | `docs/training_backend_names.md` | any | Migration table rows of
the #8928 naming document. |
| A08 | the two `*_names.py` tests | any | Removed-name tests spell the
old names to assert that they fail. |
| A09 | `flashinfer/experimental/cake_nvfp4_per_token/cake_backend.py` |
`GemmPlan` | Another family's own type, not a dense name. |
| A10 |
`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_dense_gemm_det_train/cake_backend.py`
| `dense_projection_det_gemm` | Kept generator module name that the det
backend's tile-keyed workspace lookup matches (a build identity). |

### Tests, benchmarks and docs

Tests, benchmarks and docs now use the new names:

- `tests/experimental/test_cake_dense_gemm_det_train.py`
- `tests/experimental/test_cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train.py`
- the `*_names.py` test for each of the two modules
- `benchmarks/bench_cake_dense_gemm_det_train.py`
- `benchmarks/bench_cake_dense_gemm_nondet_train.py`
- each backend README

The two names tests check three things. Every public facade name carries
its mode token. Every entry point rejects `deterministic=` with
`TypeError`. The old modules and names fail to import.

### [40d6871](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/40d6871ae5aa017026ef3ba5113a22e2a2bb0803)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T14:57:22Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): SM107a UE8M0 scale-word reuse for BLOCK_N 128 block-scaled programs (#8972)

`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm` is Cake's prepared contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM.
On sm_100a and sm_103a it ships three variants: FP32-scale programs,
block-scaled programs with packed UE8M0 scales, and a fused gate_up +
SwiGLU + FP8 quant form. On sm_107a it ships only the block-scaled UE8M0
variant, and this PR changes only that variant. The two sm_107a BLOCK_N
128 block-scaled programs, used by the single-run route and the
per-32-row-run route, previously loaded the packed UE8M0 scale word once
per K block. Because one word holds the scales of 4 K blocks, they now
load each word once per 4 K blocks and prefetch the next word one group
ahead. As a result, the MMA warp no longer waits on a scale load for
every K block. Output bits are identical to the previous programs, and
the host routes are unchanged. The other three sm_107a programs are
rebuilt under new names with unchanged code. The baseline is the
previous Cake program on the same route.

### [d52713e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/d52713ec8f27227c9db29ce1d4034705052d3747)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T14:43:53Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16): sm_107a CuTe-DSL fused programs read the peer tables from shared memory (#8971)

`cake_mxfp8_megamoe_ep16` is the fused MoE kernel with BF16 activations
and MXFP8 weights for 16-way expert parallelism (EP16). It has a CUDA
backend and a CuTe-DSL backend. Each backend has three programs per
architecture: the fused kernel, the fused kernel with the return-all-CTA
config, and the top-k reduce. This PR changes only the two sm_107a
CuTe-DSL fused programs (CTA-0 and return-all-CTA).

Compared with the CuTe-DSL backend on current `main` (the previous Cake
version), EP16 on VR200 runs 1.010–1.013× faster in both launch modes.

**Table.** NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 (VR200, sm_107a, 212 SMs per GPU), 16
GPUs (4 nodes × 4 GPUs in one NVLink rack, IMEX), driver 620.62, CUDA
13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CuTe-DSL (nvidia-cutlass-dsl) 4.8.1. Latency
is one eager EP16 forward with a cold (flushed) L2, timed with CUDA
events. A round value is the maximum over ranks of the per-rank median
of 40 iterations. Each table value is the median over 32 rounds: 16
rounds load the baseline first, 16 load this PR first, and sessions are
recreated each round. The baseline is the CuTe-DSL backend on current
`main`, and Speedup = baseline / this PR. In "Pre-sleep" mode, a GPU
sleep of 1e6 cycles precedes each launch. In "Back-to-back" mode,
launches run with no sleep. T is tokens per rank. `balanced` routing
spreads routes evenly across experts, and `hotset50` sends half of the
routes to a hot set of experts. p is an exact one-sided Mann-Whitney U
test on the per-round results, with "this PR faster" as the alternative.
With 32 vs 32 rounds, 5.46e-19 is the smallest possible value; it means
this PR was faster in every round.

(one-sided MWU) |

### [34e455d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/34e455dbe659b04281a222e7b1ab4fefa32e1bd0)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T14:18:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mega_moe_v3): faster TP4 EP1 and TP8 EP1 T32 / T128 / T512 / T1024 / T4096 rank programs on sm_103a (#8970)

`flashinfer.experimental.mega_moe_v3` runs the Cake MegaMoE v3 prepared
pipeline in a single kernel launch. It has single-rank routed-FP4,
single-rank routed-FP8 and grouped-GEMM-routes variants, plus a TP/EP
rank variant. The rank variant has 32 programs, covering TP4 EP1, TP8
EP1, TP4 EP4 and TP8 EP8 at 1 to 4096 tokens. This PR changes 10 of the
32 rank programs: TP4 EP1 and TP8 EP1 at 32, 128, 512, 1024 and 4096
tokens. In these programs, the second (down-projection) GEMM now reads a
dense W2 weight image that skips the padded intermediate columns, so it
streams fewer weight bytes. For these 10 routes, the prepared W2 image
is `[num_experts * hidden + 1, dense_k / 2]`, with one slack row,
instead of the padded width. Weight preparation for every other route is
byte-identical to before. The other 22 rank programs are unchanged, and
outputs are bitwise identical to the previous version. The changed
programs are 1.0103x to 1.0217x faster, saving 1.57 to 6.38 us per call.

- **提交信息**: perf(cake_deepgemm): route an SM120 batch-128 64K-context decode step to a faster program (RTX 5090 h32 p64 n4) (#8965)

The SM120 paged FP8 MQA logits kernel picks its program from a route
catalog. Each heads/page/next_n configuration has a default route, and
device routes pick a tuned variant for each shape. FlashInfer main
(9c2158ce) already ships the previous version of this kernel. This PR
moves one RTX 5090 shape, h32/p64/next_n 4 at batch 128 and context
65536, from its default route to a new route,
`sm120:fp8:h32:p64:n4:a4:mpf_bta_ha_k2q_ef_dynv28_p5s1`. The new route
adds one dynamic-schedule program.

1.022× (seed 52021). RTX PRO 6000 routes do not change. No existing
routes or programs are deleted or changed, and every other shape keeps
its current route.

* Batch-size-128 workloads in this configuration now select the
supported execution path instead of receiving no route.

### [4c2b8a7](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/4c2b8a7ed4af902df94e83260c8c12e8d3f71872)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T13:23:20Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet): name the DSA sparse-attention autograd package by its mode (#8928) (#8942)

## Description

Part of #8928. The issue renames every Cake training kernel so that each
public name states its mode (`det` or `nondet`). It removes the
`deterministic=` keyword and adds no aliases, so old names fail at
import. Each kernel family gets one PR with a migration table.

This PR covers the DSA sparse-attention training family. DSA is DeepSeek
Sparse Attention: top-k sparse MLA with absorbed queries and 64 query
heads. It runs on SM100a, SM103a and SM107a. The kernels are single
rank, with no KCP.

### Why `nondet`

This family has only a non-deterministic implementation:

- The forward is fixed-order.
- dq is fixed-order. Each row is written once, so dq is bitwise
reproducible run to run for one pass plan.
- The backward uses unordered atomics to add the dK / dV contributions
of every query row into FP32 accumulators. As a result, the key
gradients are not bitwise reproducible run to run. They differ within
the FP32 reduction spread. This covers `kv_latent` / `k_rope`, `kv` for
NoPE, and the rows added into a caller `dkv_acc`.

The name `flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_det_train` is reserved
for a planned deterministic package. This PR does not add it.

### New facade module

`flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train` replaces
`flashinfer.dsa_sparse_attention`. It is a stable API:

- Its four entries use `@flashinfer_api` instead of
`@flashinfer_experimental_api`. They emit no `ExperimentalWarning`.
- It imports its backend lazily, on the first call or first access.
Importing the module imports no backend.
- It re-exports three backend autograd classes. A module `__getattr__`
resolves them on first access.

| Re-export | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `CakeDSASparseAttentionNondetFunction` | autograd Function of both
rope entries |
| `CakeDSASparseAttentionNondetNopeFunction` | flat NoPE |
| `CakeDSASparseAttentionNondetNopeVarlenFunction` | varlen NoPE |

`__all__` contains:

- The environment-variable name constants `DKV_DIRECT_ENV`,
`CHECK_DST_MAP_ENV` and `BINDING_CACHE_CAPACITY_ENV`. ALL_CAPS constants
keep their names.
- The three classes above.
- The four entries:

| Entry | Input | Scores |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet` | flat | rope + latent |
| `cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_varlen` | packed documents | rope +
latent |
| `cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_nope` | flat | latent only (NoPE) |
| `cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_nope_varlen` | packed documents |
latent only (NoPE) |

### Deterministic mode (rule 8)

No entry takes a `deterministic` keyword. If you pass one, Python raises
its own `TypeError`.

| `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(...)` | Forward | Backward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `True` | Runs. The output matches the output outside the mode. |
Raises a PyTorch-style alert `RuntimeError` ("... does not have a
deterministic implementation, but you set
'torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)' ...") |
| `True, warn_only=True` | Runs | Emits one `UserWarning` per backward
call, then runs this package's backward |

- The backward raises the alert before it allocates its backward buffers
and before its first backward kernel launch. Some deterministic
preparation can run before the alert:
  - copying a `dout` that the TMA descriptor cannot address;
- planning a new binding, which can JIT-load the backward stages and,
without a caller `topk_length`, allocates the binding's `[T]` int32
row-length vector and fills it with `topk` (one fill kernel);
  - validating `dkv_acc` / `dkv_dst_map`.
- A backward with no query rows launches nothing and does not alert.
- Nothing falls back to a deterministic implementation.
- PyTorch has no public Python entry for its alert, so the backend
raises the alert itself. When the backward runs, it reads
`torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()` and
`torch.is_deterministic_algorithms_warn_only_enabled()`.
- The alert sits at the four backward launch points:
  - the bound rope backward;
  - the bound NoPE backward;
  - `DSATrainRunner.backward`;
  - `DSANopeTrainRunner.backward`.

The autograd path, the eager backend `backward` / `backward_nope` and
the prepared runners therefore all alert.

### Migration

| Old | New |
| --- | --- |
| `flashinfer.dsa_sparse_attention` (module) |
`flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train` |
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_train` (backend package,
`flashinfer/experimental/cake_dsa_train/`) |
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train`
(`flashinfer/experimental/cake/cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train/`).
It has the same submodules: `cake_backend`, `cake_jit`, `cake_launch`,
`cake_build`. |
| `dsa_sparse_attention` | `cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet` |
| `dsa_sparse_attention_varlen` |
`cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_varlen` |
| `dsa_sparse_attention_nope` | `cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_nope`
|
| `dsa_sparse_attention_nope_varlen` |
`cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_nope_varlen` |
| backend `DSASparseAttentionFunction` |
`CakeDSASparseAttentionNondetFunction` |
| backend `DSASparseAttentionNopeFunction` |
`CakeDSASparseAttentionNondetNopeFunction` |
| backend `DSASparseAttentionNopeVarlenFunction` |
`CakeDSASparseAttentionNondetNopeVarlenFunction` |

Only names change. Signatures and keyword arguments stay the same. There
are no aliases.

```python
# Before
from flashinfer.dsa_sparse_attention import dsa_sparse_attention
out = dsa_sparse_attention(q_latent, q_rope, kv_latent, k_rope, indices)

# After
from flashinfer.cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet_train import cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet
out = cake_dsa_sparse_attention_nondet(q_latent, q_rope, kv_latent, k_rope, indices)
```

### Unchanged

- Kernels, programs, launch plans and numerics.
- The 33 `csrc` files. They move by pure renames, so they are
byte-identical and the csrc tree hash does not change.
- `cake_build.py`, `cake_jit.py`, `cake_launch.py` and `.gitignore`.
They are byte-identical.
- `build.json`, except for `"package"`.
- Generated names: the library / program stems
`cake_dsa_h64_train_<hex>` / `cake_dsa_h64_nope_train_<hex>`, and
`cake_jit.load_cake_dsa_train_module`.
- The environment variables `FLASHINFER_CAKE_DSA_DKV_DIRECT`,
`FLASHINFER_CAKE_DSA_CHECK_DST_MAP` and
`FLASHINFER_CAKE_DSA_TRAIN_BINDING_CACHE_CAPACITY`. These are tuning
switches and never select the mode.
- The names of internal backend helpers: `forward`, `backward`,
`forward_nope`, `backward_nope`, `prepare_dsa_train`,
`prepare_dsa_nope_train`, `DSATrainRunner`, `DSANopeTrainRunner`,
`BINDING_CACHE`.
- The names of ALL_CAPS constants.

### Other edits

New rule-8 tests in the API test file (GPU):

- **Strict mode, each of the four entries:** the forward output equals
the output outside the mode. `out.backward(dout)` raises, and no
gradient reaches the leaves.
- **`warn_only`, each entry:** the backward issues exactly one alert of
this package, under the expected entry name, and runs. Query gradients
are bitwise equal to those outside the mode. Key gradients are within
rel. L2 < 1e-2 (the FP32 atomic spread).
- **Eager `backward` / `backward_nope` and prepared runners:**
- In strict mode, they alert. A prepared runner's strict-mode backward
leaves every output and FP32 accumulator buffer unwritten (sentinel
check).
- With `warn_only`, each issues exactly one alert under its own entry
name and runs. dq is bitwise equal, and dK/dV (including the NoPE
runner's `dkv`) are within the FP32 spread.
- **CPU:**
- The alert helper follows the torch mode: nothing outside the mode,
`RuntimeError` in strict mode and `UserWarning` with `warn_only`.
  - The alert message names no other package.
  - A backward with zero query rows launches nothing and does not alert.
- **Docstrings:** every entry docstring states the behaviour under
`torch.use_deterministic_algorithms`. The entries are not marked
experimental.

Checks in the names test (CPU only):

- Every `__all__` name except the ALL_CAPS constants contains the mode
word `nondet` as a whole token, after splitting at `_` and CamelCase.
- `inspect.signature(...).bind_partial(deterministic=False)` raises
`TypeError` for:
  - the four facade entries;
  - the backend objects of the same names;
  - `forward` / `backward` of the three autograd Functions.
- The facade re-exports are the backend classes. Old names are absent
from both the facade and the backend.
- The former modules `flashinfer.dsa_sparse_attention`,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_train` and
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_dsa_train.cake_backend` do not import.
- In a fresh interpreter, `import flashinfer` and importing the facade
load no backend module. The first access of a re-exported class loads
it.
- It also runs the shared #8928 check `assert_cake_mode_module`
(`tests/test_helpers/cake_mode_names.py`, #8947) on the facade, with
`flashinfer`, the backend package and `cake_backend` as namespaces.

### Standalone build (#6553)

Asks 3-9 and constraints 1 and 3 of the issue hold for this package:

- The backend moved as a whole directory, together with `build.json`,
`cake_build.py` and `csrc/cake_ffi_checks.h`. Manifest paths are
package-relative.
- The backend is self-contained. It uses only package-relative imports
plus torch and tvm_ffi. The only `flashinfer` import is the shared

function and is the same in every package.
- Only the package name chooses the mode. There is no `deterministic=`
keyword and no mode environment variable.
- The `PACKAGES` row is updated.
- Constraint 2, the shared CI check that imports every `PACKAGES` entry
with `flashinfer` blocked, is a separate shared test with its own owner
and is not in this PR. This PR ran the same kind of check for this
package; see the standalone vendoring check under Validation.

### Overlapping open PRs

These open PRs touch the old paths. Whichever PR lands second updates
its paths.

- #6205 packages the old `cake_dsa_train` JIT sources (`pyproject.toml`

### Remaining old-name hits

All remaining hits are intended:

- The old-name literals in the names test.

### [db445b8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/db445b85db3e35d064ae3eb22a75c6685d3c59af)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T13:20:57Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): pick the FP8 wide unit by wave count on sm_100a (#8954)

The deterministic DSA indexer top-k,
`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk(..., backend="cake")`, has
two Cake variants. The default form is BF16. The opt-in FP8 form uses
e4m3 q / k with a per-key FP32 k_scale. #8749 added the FP8 form and
#8781 improved it. #8841, #8895 and #8933 added an FP8 wide program on
sm_103a, sm_100a and sm_107a, respectively. This PR changes only the FP8
form, and only on sm_100a (measured on NVIDIA B200). It changes which
unit size the FP8 dispatch picks. It does not change any program.

Until now, the FP8 form used the BF16 dispatch rule. That rule takes the
8-query wide unit only at 6 or more wide rounds per CTA, so many calls
ran the 4-query narrow unit or the 6-query l6 unit. The sm_100a FP8
dispatch record now sets a new optional field, `wide_wave_rule`. Only
this record sets it. The rule counts waves of the persistent grid,
ceil(units / grid), for each unit size. It takes the wide unit when the
narrow unit needs at least 1.7x the wide unit's waves. It also takes the
wide unit when the l6 unit needs at least 1.3x the wide unit's waves and
the mean unit has at least 84 key tiles. Otherwise it keeps the unit the
BF16 rule picks. Calls that move to the wide unit need a larger FP8
workspace, and `dsa_indexer_det_topk_workspace_size(...,
dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)` follows the new plan.

In a 31-call sweep, every call whose unit changed was faster, and every
other call was at parity. Of the five shapes, s1_8k_on_64k and
s2_4x2k_packed were already wide, and s3_cold16k stays l6. These three
run the same program as before, so their ratio against the previous Cake
FP8 form is parity, not a speedup. P1 and glm2k_16k move from the l6
unit to the wide unit. P1 runs 1.15x faster than the previous Cake FP8
form and 1.42x faster than DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k. glm2k_16k runs
1.12x and 1.31x faster.

**NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.** The
method is the same as in #8895. All rows use top-k 2048, key ratio 1 and
causal queries (each segment's queries are its last positions). P1 is a
recorded packed training call. s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries over
18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352 keys. Previous Cake FP8 is the FP8 form
on main before this PR, loaded as a second package in the same process.
DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k runs DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` (branch
`nv_dev`, commit `b64107f2`) with FP32 per-key K scales and FP32 logits.
It then runs FlashInfer `top_k_ragged_transform(deterministic=True,
tie_break=LARGE)` over each row's visible keys (the ragged arm, which
reads the row-padded logits in place). Each time is the CUPTI GPU
interval over every kernel the call launches, with cold L2 and eager
launch. Cake arms time a prepared runner into caller-owned outputs and
workspace. Each run's value is the median over three arm orders (A then
B, B then A, interleaved). Every row was measured on two GPUs of one
node in separate processes, and the table shows the median of the two
runs. "vs previous" = previous time / this PR time. "vs DeepGEMM" =
DeepGEMM time / this PR time. A value above 1 means this PR is faster.
All arms return bit-identical scores and ids on every row.

| Shape | Queries T | Keys Tkv | Segments | Previous Cake FP8 (ms) |
This PR (ms) | vs previous | DeepGEMM + FlashInfer top-k (ms) | vs
DeepGEMM |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| P1 | 16231 | 268757 | 8 | 3.547 | 3.087 | 1.15x | 4.391 | 1.42x |
| glm2k_16k | 2048 | 16384 | 1 | 0.329 | 0.293 | 1.12x | 0.382 | 1.31x |
| s1_8k_on_64k | 8192 | 73728 | 1 | 3.088 | 3.061 | 1.01x | 4.237 |
1.38x |
| s2_4x2k_packed | 8192 | 229376 | 4 | 2.644 | 2.647 | 1.00x | 3.770 |
1.42x |
| s3_cold16k | 16384 | 16384 | 1 | 1.250 | 1.252 | 1.00x | 1.895 | 1.51x
|

Other measured B200 calls also gain against the previous Cake FP8 form:
1024 queries over 16384 keys (1.45x), 1792 over 131072 (1.28x), 600 over
49152 (1.28x), 4096 over 65536 (1.10x) and 5120 over 49152 (1.10x).

The other Cake variant, the default BF16 form, is unchanged; both Cake
forms cover sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a, and the FP8 form has a wide
program on all three.

### [3e6ae48](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3e6ae484496dd2bd6575a336a30baa7ca54112be)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T13:16:47Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_kda_det): remove the single-rank names before the det rename (#8908)

Every public name of a deterministic KDA training object now includes
`det`. This PR removes the previous names with no alias and no
compatibility entry.

**This is an API-incompatible change.** Code that imports or calls any
previous name below, including `flashinfer.kda_train` and
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train.*`, fails after this PR with
`ImportError` / `AttributeError`. Callers must move to the det names in
the tables below. The KCP (context-parallel) implementation and its det
entry points are not removed; only the previous spellings are.

## Removed

- `flashinfer/kda_train.py`: an alias-only module that bound the
previous single-rank names and the previous KCP names to the det
objects.
- `flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_train/` (7 files: `__init__.py`,
`cake_backend.py`, `cake_build.py`, `cake_jit.py`, `cake_kcp.py`,
`cake_kcp_jit.py`, `cake_kcp_plan.py`): a compatibility package whose
modules were the det package's module objects.
- `tests/test_helpers/cake_kda_train_reference.py`: callers now use
`tests/test_helpers/cake_kda_det_train_reference.py`.
- These aliases in `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_det_train` (the
package `__init__` and `cake_backend`): `ChunkKDAFunction`, `KdaArena`
(`cake_backend` only), `KdaChunkSaved`, `KdaWorkspace`, `chunk_kda`,
`chunk_kda_fwd`, `chunk_kda_bwd`.
- The `"cake_kda_train"` key in `PACKAGES` in
`tests/test_helpers/cake_package.py`.

### [35b9c10](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/35b9c102395826102bc87b7fda21b6e32af7c044)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T13:04:09Z
- **提交信息**: test(cake_gqa_nondet_train): check the shared #8928 name rules with cake_mode_names (#8962)

## Description

PR #8939 renamed the GQA HD256 training package to
`flashinfer.cake_gqa_nondet_train`. Its names test used a local token
splitter, `_tokens`, to check the mode word. PR #8947 later added the
shared helper `tests/test_helpers/cake_mode_names.py`. Every #8928
family uses it for the shared naming rules. #8947 asked each family to
adopt the helper in a follow-up rather than copy it. This PR makes that
change for the GQA family.

It changes one file,
`tests/experimental/test_cake_gqa_nondet_train_names.py`. It does not
touch library code, kernels, docs or benchmarks. The branch has two
commits on main `02b041cd`. The head is `6f1fc68d`.

Changes:

- **Removed:** the local `_tokens` splitter and
`test_mode_word_is_a_token`. The helper's own self-test in
`tests/cpu/test_cake_mode_names.py` covers token splitting.
- **Added:** `test_the_shared_mode_rules_hold`. It runs the helper's
four shared checks one at a time:

  | Helper call | Input | Assertion |
  |---|---|---|
| `assert_mode_names(public)` | Public names | Public names carry
`nondet` after the op |
| `assert_no_deterministic_keyword(...)` | Every facade `__all__` name
except the aliases in a new `TYPE_ALIASES` tuple | No entry point takes
a `deterministic` keyword |
| `assert_same_object_same_name(public, (flashinfer, package, backend),
forwards=...)` | Namespaces: `flashinfer`, the backend package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gqa_nondet_train`, and its
`cake_backend` module | Each object is bound under only one name across
those namespaces |
| `assert_old_names_fail(old modules, old names, cwd=repo root)` | Old
module paths (including `flashinfer.gqa_train` and
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gqa_train`), removed facade entries and
removed backend names | Old module paths and names fail at import in a
fresh interpreter |

- **Updated:** `test_public_names_carry_the_mode` now calls
`assert_mode_names(package, names=FORWARDED)` instead of the local
splitter. It covers the backend objects that the facade forwards to or
re-exports. Its other checks stay the same: each forwarded name is in
both the backend and package `__all__`, and both names refer to the same
object.
- **Unchanged:** the family's own checks.
  - `deterministic=` raises `TypeError` for every entry.
  - Only the backward's alert reads torch's deterministic mode.
  - The `build.json` package and build identity checks still run.
- `test_no_entry_takes_a_mode_keyword` still checks each entry point's
signature. It covers the 5 facade entries, the 4 forwarded backend
functions, `CakeGQANondetWorkspace` and `CakeGQANondetFunction.forward`.

### Why the test does not call `assert_cake_mode_module`

`assert_cake_mode_module(flashinfer.cake_gqa_nondet_train, ...)` fails
with exactly one error:

```
flashinfer.cake_gqa_nondet_train.CakeGQANondetDkvAccSource: takes a 'deterministic' parameter through **kwargs
```

This is a false positive:

- `CakeGQANondetDkvAccSource` is a `typing.Callable` alias. It is the
type of the `dkv_acc` callable, and the facade re-exports it in
`__all__`.
- `inspect.signature` returns typing's `(*args, **kwargs)` for the
alias. As a result, the helper's keyword check treats it as an entry
point.
- The alias is a type, not an entry point. Calling it raises
`TypeError`.

The second commit calls the four checks separately and leaves the alias
out of the keyword check through `TYPE_ALIASES`. The family's own
`test_no_entry_takes_a_mode_keyword` still checks every real entry
point.

## Related Issues

- Part of #8928.
- Follows #8939 (GQA HD256 rename) and #8947 (shared helper).
- #8951 (standalone import check) has no GQA entry and needs no change.

tests/experimental/test_cake_gqa_nondet_train_names.py` | all hooks
pass, no file rewritten |

--head 6f1fc68d` | 0 new findings |

These are CPU-only tests (`pytest.mark.cpu_only`). No GPU run is needed
because no kernel or library code changes.

## Reviewer Notes

#8947.
- Library behavior is unchanged.
- The helper's owner knows about the false positive for typing aliases.
If the helper later skips typing aliases, this test can go back to
calling `assert_cake_mode_module`.

### [1d39e26](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1d39e26c8caf3c29961e7949ce7a0770c42cfc36)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T13:03:35Z
- **提交信息**: test(cake): skip type aliases in the deterministic-keyword check (#8928) (#8961)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8928

`assert_no_deterministic_keyword` in
`tests/test_helpers/cake_mode_names.py` was added by #8947, and
`assert_cake_mode_module` also runs it. For every public callable, it
requires `inspect.signature(entry).bind_partial(deterministic=False)` to
raise `TypeError`. Subscripted typing generics are callable and report
`(*args, **kwargs)`. As a result, the public type alias
`CakeGQANondetDkvAccSource` exported by
`flashinfer.cake_gqa_nondet_train` fails with:

`flashinfer.cake_gqa_nondet_train.CakeGQANondetDkvAccSource: takes a
'deterministic' parameter through **kwargs`

The alias is a type, not an entry point. Any facade that exports a
`typing` or `collections.abc` alias hits the same error.

The check now skips objects where `typing.get_origin(obj) is not None`,
using a new private `_is_type_alias`. It skips them at the module's top
level and among the public members of a class. If a class is public, it
is still checked even when an alias subscripts it. The module and
function docstrings document this. No library code changes. Families can
now run `assert_cake_mode_module` on a facade that exports a type alias
instead of calling each check separately.

### Tests

New self-tests in `tests/cpu/test_cake_mode_names.py`:

- Aliases at module and class level pass.
- An entry that takes `**options` and sits next to those aliases is the
only failure reported.
- An entry that takes `**options` and has a keyword-only `__signature__`
passes, also through `functools.wraps`. Without that signature it fails.
This is existing behavior that the KCP packages can rely on.

- `tests/cpu/test_cake_mode_names.py`: 50 passed (47 on main) on a
CPU-only cluster node in the CUDA 13.4 development container; pre-commit
passes.
- On main aa033729 with this helper, `assert_no_deterministic_keyword`
passes on `flashinfer.cake_gqa_nondet_train` and on its backend package
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_gqa_nondet_train`. With the alias
skip disabled, it reports exactly the error above (a separate probe, not
part of this PR).

### [ec147f4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ec147f471ac9b749ddcda4f07ad2b896bd615451)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T12:05:27Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm_det): compensate every step in the large-token backward on SM100, SM103 and SM107 (#8835)

The deterministic Cake RMSNorm training package
(`cake_rmsnorm_det_train`) covers BF16 and FP32 weights, residual and
non-residual inputs, row widths H 256 (contiguous and per-head views),
512, 1536, 2048, 4096, 5120 and 6144, and the forward and backward
passes. This PR changes only the backward pass, only at large token
counts, for BF16 and FP32 weights in these windows: on sm_100a, H 2048
for T in (58880, 65536] and H 5120 for T in (50688, 65536]; on sm_103a,
H 4096 for T in (51200, 65536]; on sm_107a, H 4096 for T in (50176,
65536]. In these windows the compensated (Kahan) dw column sums now
apply the compensation at the end of every chunk step instead of once
per block of 8 steps. With the previous version, the largest per-element
dw error at these sizes reached up to 1.10 times the tolerance bound
(|err| <= 1e-4 + 1e-4 |ref|) on a few elements near zero. With this PR
it is at most 0.79 times the bound. dw stays fixed-order and bitwise
reproducible from run to run, and the forward pass, dx and all launch
shapes outside these windows are unchanged. The fix trades speed for
accuracy: on the changed rows this PR runs at 0.876-0.979x the speed of
the previous Cake version, but it is still faster than torch.compile on
30 of the 32 rows.

Previous Cake / Cake latency ratios on the changed rows (below 1 means
this PR is slower):
- **B200 (sm_100a) backward:** 0.876-0.906x on all 14 changed rows, at
most 41.671 us slower. Against torch.compile it is 0.974-1.648x: Cake is
faster on 12 of the 14 rows. It is on par at H 2048 BF16 T 61504
(140.647 us vs 140.592 us) and slower at H 2048 BF16 T 65536 (149.245 us
vs 145.325 us).
- **GB300 (sm_103a) backward:** 0.907-0.925x on all 8 changed rows, at
most 25.639 us slower. Against torch.compile it is 1.007-1.159x: Cake is
faster on all 8 rows.
- **R200 (sm_107a) backward:** 0.962-0.979x on all 10 changed rows, at
most 5.161 us slower. Against torch.compile it is 1.151-2.061x: Cake is
faster on all 10 rows.

**NVIDIA B200 (148 SMs), sm_100a, backward.** CUDA 13.4 (kernels built
with nvcc 13.4), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Latency is CUPTI
kernel-active time per call with a cold L2. Previous Cake is the
previously shipped Cake package. Both Cake versions run through the
package's public backward entry point in the same processes, in
counterbalanced order. Each Cake value is the fastest valid process: the
lowest per-process median among processes where a repeated timing of the
new call lands within 1%. torch.compile is
`torch.compile(dynamic=False)` of the FP32 RMSNorm formula and its
backward, fastest process.

### [33491c8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/33491c8c678a0bd68501b6408e0b2d7b95214cb3)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T12:05:07Z
- **提交信息**: test(cake_package): check that every Cake package imports with flashinfer blocked (#8951)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8928
Requirement:
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8928#issuecomment-6680200530
(every backend is self-contained)

This PR adds one test file,
`tests/cpu/test_cake_packages_standalone.py`, and changes nothing else.
A build that vendors a Cake package (#6553) copies the package directory
into its own tree and imports it under its own name, without flashinfer.
This test is the only check that imports every Cake package with
flashinfer blocked, so the #8928 renames keep that layout working.

### What it checks

For each distinct import path in `PACKAGES` of
`tests/test_helpers/cake_package.py`, read when the test runs, a fresh
interpreter does the following:

1. Blocks flashinfer with `sys.modules["flashinfer"] = None` and a
meta-path finder that raises `ImportError` for `flashinfer` and
`flashinfer.*`.
2. Removes the working directory from `sys.path`, along with every entry
at or above a loaded directory. It keeps the other entries, so torch and
tvm_ffi still import.
3. Loads the package directory where it is, without a copy, as the
top-level package `vendored_<directory>`. A relative import that climbs
out of the directory therefore fails.
4. Imports every `.py` module of the directory one by one, including
modules in subdirectories. If `__init__.py` fails, its other modules are
still checked.
5. Fails on any import error. It also fails if a flashinfer module
leaked: any `flashinfer.*` entry left in `sys.modules`, or a
`flashinfer` entry other than the `None` sentinel.

A `PACKAGES` row fails if its directory or `__init__.py` does not exist.
The child interpreters run with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` empty and `-B`,
and each has a 600 s timeout. The prebuilt/JIT loader `cake_build.py`
imports `flashinfer.jit` only inside a function (`_jit_toolchain`), so
it passes. The file also tests itself on temporary packages: 13 cases
for the child interpreter and 5 for sibling validation. That way a pass
still means something once the allowlist is empty.

Limits:
- Imports inside functions are not checked, because the test only
imports modules.
- An editable install also maps `b12x`, `build_backend` and
`build_utils` to the checkout. The test does not block these names, so a
package must not import them.

### Declared siblings

A KCP or dense nondet package that needs a single-rank package declares
it as a sibling:
- **Where siblings come from:** `build.json` `common.requires.packages`
(sibling directory names) when that key is present. Otherwise, the
`requires` field of the package's row in
`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py`.
- **Layout:** the package and its siblings load under one synthetic
parent, `vendored_<directory>.<directory>` beside
`vendored_<directory>.<sibling>`. This matches the layout of
`check_cake_build_manifests.py --vendored-gate`, so `from ..<sibling>
import x` resolves. Undeclared siblings cannot be imported.
- **Requirements:** each declared sibling must be a `PACKAGES` row with
the same parent package and an existing directory. Otherwise the package
fails.

### Burn-down `ALLOWLIST`

These four packages fail on main today (the `cake_dsa_indexer` alias row
left with its removal in #8936):

| import path | modules that fail today | reason |
|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_det_train_kcp` | `cake_kcp`,
`cake_kcp_jit` | they import the single-rank package across directories
(`from ..cake_kda_det_train import`), undeclared |
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train` | `__init__`, `cake_backend`,
`cake_build`, `cake_jit`, `cake_kcp`, `cake_kcp_jit`, `cake_kcp_plan` |
compatibility alias: `__init__.py` star-imports
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_det_train`, and each module replaces
itself with a det package's module, imported by its flashinfer path |
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train_kcp` | `cake_kcp`,
`cake_kcp_jit` | they import the single-rank package across directories
(`from ..cake.cake_kda_train import`), undeclared |
| `flashinfer.experimental.cake_stepfun_moe` | `__init__` |
`__init__.py` decorates its entry points with flashinfer's
`flashinfer_experimental_api` (`from ...api_logging import`) |

The allowlist is strict. An allowlisted package is marked xfail only
when exactly its listed modules fail. The test fails if a listed module
now imports or no longer exists, or if an unlisted module fails. A
leaked flashinfer module always fails the test, whether or not the
package is allowlisted. So the PR that fixes a package deletes its
modules from the entry in the same change, and deletes the entry once it
is empty. `test_allowlist_names_packages` fails if an entry's path is
not in `PACKAGES`, if an entry is duplicated or empty, or if `PACKAGES`
is empty.

How each row goes away:
- **The two KDA KCP rows:** the KDA rename PRs declare the single-rank
sibling (`common.requires.packages` in `build.json`, plus the README)
and resolve it from their parent package.
- **The alias row** (`cake_kda_train`): the alias is removed.
- **`cake_stepfun_moe`:** it imports flashinfer's `api_logging`. Its
owner decides how to vendor it.

### For the rename PRs

Each family updates only its own `PACKAGES` rows. The test reads the
table at run time, so no family copies this check. CI runs this file in
the unit-test run over `tests/`. The file lives in `tests/cpu` because
that run does not recurse into `tests/experimental`.

The `experimental-tests` block of a PR body accepts only
`tests/experimental/`. A PR that changes `PACKAGES`, a package directory
or a sibling declaration should therefore ask for a targeted run:
`@flashinfer-bot run tests/cpu/test_cake_packages_standalone.py`

### Tests

- Cluster CPU node, CUDA 13.4 development container, main 2e989556: 57
passed, 5 xfailed (exactly the five `ALLOWLIST` rows);
`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py`: 0 findings for 44 packages.
- Same check on the RMSNorm rename (#8910) merged into main: 57 passed,
5 xfailed; both renamed RMSNorm packages
(`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_rmsnorm_det_train`,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_rmsnorm_nondet_train`) import with
flashinfer blocked.
- Same check merged into main 555dd84e (after the conv1d, GDN and MoE
renames): 57 passed, 5 xfailed (same five `ALLOWLIST` rows).
- Current head merged into main 98fd797c (after the DSA indexer rename
#8936): 57 passed, 4 xfailed (exactly the four `ALLOWLIST` rows above);
`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py`: 0 findings for 44 packages.
- Same check merged into main 02b041cd (after #8901, #8939 and #8922):
57 passed, 4 xfailed (same four `ALLOWLIST` rows);
`scripts/check_cake_build_manifests.py`: 0 findings for 44 packages.
- pre-commit: passes.

### [7a0a609](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7a0a609f33f41fa6b67532b060583ea299594b2a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T11:59:26Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): tune SM107 FP8 64-head decode routing for the four-stage sibling (#8955)

The Cake backend of `trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` has 50
programs: BF16 and FP8 programs for 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads
(several bodies per head count, picked per shape by the host route) and
an NVFP4-KV decode family. On sm_107a it ships seven FP8 programs for
the DeepSeek-V4 decode route. This PR changes which of two of them a
64-head FP8 decode row runs: the persistent H128 uniform-gather body, or
the 64-head M64 multi-tile program with its four-stage K/V sibling. Only
the host route changes, so no program changes and each program's output
bits stay the same. On sm_107a, in a process that can launch the
four-stage sibling, more 64-head FP8 decode rows (max_q_len < 257) now
leave the persistent body for the M64 body. Sparse widths 385-1152 move
at fewer rows than before, and sparse widths 257-352 from 24 rows,
353-383 from 44 rows and width 640 from 32 rows move below the 48-row
floor of the uniform route. This follows #8885, which moved the first
set of these rows.

The baseline is the previous Cake version: FlashInfer main's route,
which already includes #8885 and runs these rows on the persistent body.
Across the 611-shape verification grid, with the 8-call protocol
described below, the new rule moves 180 cells on R200 (216 SMs), with
speedup 1.013-1.109 (median 1.051), and 232 cells on VR200 (212 SMs),
with speedup 1.004-1.126 (median 1.054). No moved cell is below 1.000 on
either GPU. Timed as a single call after an L2 flush, the same cells
give 1.000-1.111 (median 1.047) on R200 and 1.010-1.141 (median 1.063)
on VR200. A repeat run of the final rule on a second VR200 GPU (476
shapes, 253 moved cells) gave 0.998-1.131 (median 1.058) with the 8-call
protocol and 1.007-1.140 (median 1.061) as a single call; its one cell
below 1.000 (0.998) is within run-to-run noise. Shapes the rule does not
move run the same program on the same route as FlashInfer main. The
table lists 24 of the moved shapes.

NVIDIA R200 with 216 SMs and NVIDIA VR200 with 212 SMs, sm_107a, CUDA
13.4. Each time is per call, from eight back-to-back calls with PDL in
one CUDA graph, each call on its own input set (cold KV per call), with
one L2 flush per graph launch; median of three rounds with rotated

layer with sparse width W = 128 SWA tokens + top-k; rows = batch x
q_len. Speedup = previous / this PR.

### [07fa301](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/07fa301307eac5c99f59044d26f3792499f4357f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T11:45:16Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsv4): split SM107 FP8 128-head decode calls of up to 17 query rows across SMs (#8950)

Cake's DeepSeek-V4 sparse MLA attention for FlashInfer (`cake_dsv4`)
ships 30 programs for sm_100a and 30 for sm_103a on FlashInfer main,
covering BF16 and FP8 KV caches and 8 to 128 query heads, plus 7 FP8
programs for sm_107a: 128-head persistent programs, 64-head M64 programs
and a low-head prefill program. This PR adds 2 sm_107a programs: a
split-KV form of the FP8 128-head persistent uniform-gather program, and
a kernel that merges its pieces. They handle sm_107a calls with an FP8
KV cache, 128 heads, 1152 sparse keys per query (nine 128-key tiles), 1
to 17 query rows and PDL enabled. Each query row in these calls runs as
2 to 9 pieces on separate SMs, where the previous Cake version on
FlashInfer main (5a94f96e) runs it as one two-CTA cluster. Against that
baseline, these calls are 1.03x to 1.50x faster when queries attend all
or mixed key counts, with the largest gain at 1 to 3 rows (about 3.3 us
per call). When every request in the batch is short, these calls are
slower: 0.79x to 0.82x of main, or 1.1 to 1.8 us per call. The merge
kernel still runs in that case, and the host cannot detect it because
request lengths live on the GPU. All other calls launch exactly as on
main and give bitwise-identical outputs (1.00x in the table).

Latency on NVIDIA R200 (sm_107a, 216 SMs) with the CUDA 13.4 runtime, in
microseconds per call. Each call is one of 8 back-to-back calls captured
in one CUDA graph, with L2 flushed before each replay. Values are the
median over 8 rounds, with main (5a94f96e) and this PR timed in the same
process in alternating order. Speedup is main latency divided by this
PR's latency.

- Layer: "c4 (32K context)" is the DeepSeek-V4 c4 layer at 32K-token
context, with 128 sliding-window keys plus 1024 top-k keys of the
4x-compressed cache per query. "c128 (128K context)" is the c128 layer
at 128K-token context, with 128 sliding-window keys plus 1024 keys of
the 128x-compressed cache.
- Keys per query: "all 1152" means every query attends all 1152 keys.
"mixed" means every other query attends all 1152 keys and the others
attend 128-384. "all short" means every query attends at most the keys
of one piece.
- Query tokens per request: 1 (decode) or 4 (multi-token).
- Query rows T: query rows in the call.
- PDL: programmatic dependent launch on or off.
- Pieces per row: the number of pieces s each query row runs as (9 for
1-4 rows, 5 for 5-8, 3 for 9-13, 2 for 14-17). "not split" means the
launch is unchanged from main.
