### [74c8d6b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/74c8d6bd0943165f8ec85c898908f3cebcef875a)

- **作者**: Ruoqian Guo
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T06:42:46Z
- **提交信息**: perf(moe_ep): faster SM90 MXFP4/NVFP4 pull MegaMoE (N72/N80 token tiles, measured defaults, K128 pipelining) (#7961)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

This PR makes the SM90 pull-style CuTe-DSL MegaMoE faster for packed FP4
weights (MXFP4 and NVFP4) with FP8 activations, mainly after autotuning.
It builds on #6999 (SM90 NVFP4 x FP8 MegaMoE) and #7542 (the NVFP4 scale
ring).

**Why it is faster.**

- **N72 and N80 token tiles.** With N64 swap-AB tiles, an expert with
65-80 rows needs a second, almost empty tile that still loads and
converts all of the expert's FP4 weights. Packed FP4 now also accepts
N72 and N80 tiles (M256). Defaults take the width needing the fewest
tiles for the balanced rows per expert; ties keep N64. The activation-SF
pool is padded to a multiple of the tile width.
- **K128 pipelining.** For K128 tiles with N64, N72 or N80, each K step
now waits for and loads the next stage's packed weights while the
current WGMMAs run, instead of after them. K128 FC2 also gets K256's
paired BF16 stores.
- **Dispatch pull.** A dispatch warp can keep up to four rows in flight
(two or three in the measured tactics) in idle pull-buffer slots and
rotate the rows it takes on each pass, which shortens the NVLink pull at
large token counts.
- **Measured defaults.** Untuned MXFP4 uses per-bucket tactics measured
on the two shapes below (other shapes keep the heuristic); NVFP4
reference defaults without the scale ring take the same N64/N72/N80
rule.
- With `epi_warps` token-back, the two epilogue warpgroups of a packed
FP4 kernel share one code copy.

**Behavior changes.**

- Untuned MXFP4 tactics change for the two measured shapes, including
the compact pull buffer from 129 tokens per rank (the 256 bucket) on the
K256 shape. Untuned NVFP4 tactics of the reference shape change where
N72 or N80 needs fewer tiles.
- `compact_pull_buffer`, `dispatch_pull_batch` and
`dispatch_pull_rotate` are MXFP4/NVFP4 tactic fields set through
`knobs=`; for MXFP4, explicit config or shim values override a cached or
default tactic, as `token_back_mode` does. `compact_pull_buffer` of the
MXFP4 backend config and of `get_symm_buffer_for_hopper_mxfp4_mega_moe`
now defaults to `None` (follow the tactic): an explicit `False`, the old
default, forces the full buffer, and `knobs="auto"` ignores it.
- MXFP4 and NVFP4 tuning caches re-tune. Autotuning skips dispatch-side
token-back; an explicit `token_back_mode` and the published-exact
profile's untuned defaults above 512 tokens still use it, as before.
- Configs now reject the NVFP4 scale ring off non-pingpong N64/K256
tiles (a compile failure before) and pull rotation with dispatch-side
token-back.
- FP8 (per-tensor and blockwise) and BF16 compile to the same cubins as
main.
- `bench_moe_ep_sm90_nvfp4.py` also runs EP2 and takes `--capacity`
(buffer capacity above the live tokens).

### Performance

H200 SXM, SM clocks locked at 1830 MHz, block-permutation routing. Each
tree was tuned into its own cache, which
`benchmarks/bench_moe_ep_sm90_nvfp4.py` then read (10 warmup and 50
timed iterations in 3 rounds, 300 µs padding, per-rank median, maximum
over ranks). Every bucket ran its cached winner (checked from the
recorded tactic). Both trees ran this PR's script (main's accepts only
EP4) in alternating fresh processes (main, PR, PR, main, main, PR).
Ratios are medians of the three paired PR/main ratios (range in
brackets), µs values are medians over processes, and Tile is the token
tile N, main → PR.

**H7168/I3072/E384/top-6, EP4, NVFP4, tuned on both sides**

**MXFP4 against FP8 on the shape of #6465.** #6465 added M256/K128 MXFP4
tuning candidates for H2560/I640/E512/top-10/EP2. On main, which
includes #6465, tuned MXFP4 is still 2-18% slower than tuned FP8
per-tensor on this shape; with this PR it is 5-13% faster. Each row
alternates the FP8 and MXFP4 layers of `bench_moe_ep_sm90_mega.py` in
one process with a local harness (three fresh processes, three rounds
each, same padding and iterations); the ratio is the median of the nine
paired rounds. FP8 cubins are identical on both trees; its two columns
come from separate runs.

µs | MX/FP8 PR |

Untuned (empty cache, same method): PR/main is 0.53-1.00 for NVFP4 and
0.60-0.99 for MXFP4 on the EP4 shape (the 13 buckets plus 1152, 1280,
2304, 2560, 4608 and 5120 tokens), and 0.97 for NVFP4 and 0.66-0.75 for
MXFP4 on the EP2 shape (1024-16384 tokens).

```bash
# MXFP4: tune each token count T into a per-tree cache (EP2: --nproc_per_node=2 and the EP2 shape).
FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE=knobs.json torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 -m flashinfer.moe_ep.tune --dtype sm90_mxfp4 \
  --routing-profile block_permutation_v1 --hidden 7168 --intermediate 3072 --num-experts 384 --topk 6 --max-tokens T
# FP8 per-tensor (EP2 table): no routing profile (MXFP4 only), and the clamp of the FP8 benchmark.
FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE=knobs_ep2.json torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 -m flashinfer.moe_ep.tune --dtype sm90_fp8_e4m3 \
  --fp8-scale-mode per_tensor --gate-up-clamp 10 --hidden 2560 --intermediate 640 --num-experts 512 --topk 10 --max-tokens T
# NVFP4 has no tuning CLI: a layer built with Sm90_Fp8_Nvfp4_Bf16_PullCutedsl_MegaMoeConfig(..., knobs="auto") and
# FleetParams(..., max_tokens_per_rank=T, tuning_live_tokens=T) tunes on its first compute_staged call and records
# the winner in the same cache.
# Replay: NVFP4/MXFP4 tables.
FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE=knobs.json torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 benchmarks/bench_moe_ep_sm90_nvfp4.py \
  --tokens 8 16 32 64 128 256 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384 32768
FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE=knobs_ep2.json torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 benchmarks/bench_moe_ep_sm90_nvfp4.py \
  --hidden 2560 --intermediate 640 --experts 512 --top-k 10 --tokens 1024 2048 4096 8192 16384
# MXFP4 against FP8, one process each (the table alternated both in one process).
B=benchmarks/moe_ep/backends/mega/kernel/sm90/bench_moe_ep_sm90_mega.py
S="--hidden 2560 --intermediate 640 --num-experts 512 --top-k 10 --tokens 1024,2048,4096,8192,16384"
FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE=knobs_ep2.json torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 $B $S --scale-mode per_tensor --no-sparse-data
FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE=knobs_ep2.json torchrun --nproc_per_node=2 $B $S \
  --backend sm90_fp8_mxfp4_bf16_pull_cutedsl --mxfp4-tactic-source cache_or_heuristic
```

### [2c78ff6](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2c78ff66846d48b77ee48f5cf4ae13ac4ccabe3a)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T06:34:45Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mok_bf16): per-expert x-replay release, expert-major weight-gradient claims and in-place dy pre-weighting in the sm_107a MXFP8 backward (#7821) (#8919)

`cake_mok_bf16` is FlashInfer's MoK mixture-of-experts training kernel
family. It covers forward, full-forward checkpoint recompute and
backward, and has four variants: BF16 or MXFP8 routed experts, each with
plain or clamped SwiGLU. This PR speeds up the MXFP8 backward kernel on
sm_107a (for #7821). The change covers all four of its builds: plain or
clamped SwiGLU, each with BF16 or FP32 weight-gradient outputs.

When there is more than one macrobatch, the communication CTAs no longer
wait for the whole macrobatch before replaying the next macrobatch's
tokens (x). Each 128-row task is now replayed as soon as its owning
expert has retired its weight-gradient tiles. Weight-gradient tiles are
claimed expert by expert, so experts retire in row order. The x replay
also now runs ahead of the router-weight preload.

The weighted dy dispatch used to scale every dy element twice: once in
the column-major MXFP8 quantizer, with a per-column weight load, and
once in the row-major one. It now scales the 128 dy rows once, in place
in shared memory, with 128-bit vector loads and stores, and both
quantizers read the scaled values. Every quantized byte is the same as
before.

The per-expert retire counters grow the backward's `buffers_done`
workspace from `macros` to `macros * (experts + 1)` int32 counters. At 8
macrobatches and 36 local experts, that is 1152 more bytes. Outputs are
bitwise identical to before. The forward and recompute code and the
sm_100a and sm_103a kernels are unchanged.

**Kernel phases** (ms, before → after, speedup)
| Workload | Forward | Backward |
|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform routing | 3.879 → 3.895 (0.996x) | 6.766 → 6.625
(1.021x) |
| T=32768, uniform routing | 5.165 → 5.178 (0.997x) | 8.728 → 8.465
(1.031x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 1.25x | 6.200 → 6.205 (0.999x) | 10.644 →
10.228 (1.041x) |
| T=27116, hot-expert routing 2x | 10.932 → 11.084 (0.986x) | 22.339 →
21.215 (1.053x) |

**End to end** (ms, before → after, speedup)
| Workload | MoE microbatch | Training update, 5 layers |
|---|---|---|
| T=27116, uniform | 14.091 → 13.964 (1.009x) | 141.613 → 140.552
(1.008x) |
| T=32768, uniform | 17.778 → 17.553 (1.013x) | 177.403 → 174.959
(1.014x) |
| T=27116, hot 1.25x | 20.632 → 20.226 (1.020x) | 204.988 → 201.467
(1.017x) |
| T=27116, hot 2x | 37.065 → 36.124 (1.026x) | 372.384 → 363.390
(1.025x) |

*8 NVIDIA VR NVL72 GPUs (sm_107a, 212 SMs, two 4-GPU trays in one NVLink
domain), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. EP8, H=4096, I=2048, 288
experts, top-8, one shared expert, clamped SwiGLU (limit 10), FP32
weight gradients, MXFP8 routed experts, macrobatch 262144. "Before" is
FlashInfer main, with the same MoK sources as this PR's base, and
"after" is this PR. Both use recompute replay mode, with
`recompute_forward_context` for the checkpointed forward. Each value is
the mean of 2 runs per side, interleaved on the same nodes in the order
before, after, after, before. The two before runs differ by at most 0.16
% per microbatch. The forward kernel SASS is identical on both sides,
and SM clocks agree within 4 MHz. The forward differences (up to 1.4 %
at hot 2x) therefore do not come from forward code; they grow with the
backward speedup. The microbatch and training-update times include them.
Peak memory per rank grows by 512 bytes in the three T=27116 rows and is
unchanged at T=32768. Outputs, input gradients, routing-score gradients
and weight gradients are bitwise identical to before on all 8 ranks,
with FP32 weight-gradient accumulators seeded identically.*

The family also ships the BF16 routed-expert variants and the MXFP8
forward and recompute kernels, and every variant runs on sm_100a,
sm_103a and sm_107a.

loss, policy loss, log-probability with no temperature, a scalar
temperature or a per-token FP32 `[T]` temperature, support
log-probability and support-KL, on BF16 hidden states and weights. The
backend has a deterministic form and a non-deterministic (ND) form.
`deterministic=False` on the public `flashinfer.chunked_lm_head` entries
(`chunked_lm_head_loss`, `chunked_lm_head_logprob`,
`chunked_lm_head_support_logprob`, `chunked_lm_head_support_kl`) selects
the ND form, implemented in
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`.

This PR changes the ND log-probability backward, with or without
temperature, on sm_100a and sm_103a when a call of two or more chunks
skips rows with zero dlogp. When the trailing chunks hold no live row,
the weight-gradient (dW) accumulate of the last live chunk now writes
the BF16 dW, so the backward runs no separate cast-only pass over dW.
The forward, the loss and support modes, the plans without the skip,
runners prepared with explicit live-row counts and sm_107a are
unchanged; the sm_107a tables are in #8902.

The tables below give absolute ms for B200 and GB300, 195 cells each.
Prev is FlashInfer main's ND planner, which includes #8796, timed on
this PR's build with the cast-at-the-last-live-chunk forms hidden.
Against prev, this PR's ND plan (new) is faster in 45 cells on B200
(1.0146x-1.1067x) and 67 on GB300 (1.0142x-1.1166x), and slower in none.
Every faster cell is a bwd, f+b or ckpt cell at z 0.166 or 0.5. The
largest gain on each GPU is p09 bwd (B200 16.806 -> 15.186 ms, GB300
13.543 -> 12.129 ms). The rest are parity or inconclusive (lowest point
estimate: B200 s01 bwd 0.9870x, GB300 h07 and h10 bwd, both 0.9963x).
Against deterministic Cake (det), new is faster in 124 cells on each GPU
(B200 1.0690x-1.9942x, GB300 1.0731x-1.9402x) and slower in none.

SOTA is the fastest non-Cake arm timed in each cell. On the 105
log-probability (LP) cells, it is Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1 (CCE,
torch.compile path), faster than PyTorch chunked + torch.compile (PT) in
all 105. New is faster than CCE in 42 cells on each GPU (B200
1.0649x-1.3377x, GB300 1.0953x-1.3251x). It is slower than CCE in 55 on
B200 (0.6844x-0.9823x) and 53 on GB300 (0.6900x-0.9839x), all at z 0 or
0.166. Prev is also slower than CCE in each of those cells by point
estimate. The lowest ratios are p26 bwd on B200 (new 119.070 vs CCE
81.497 ms) and p01 bwd on GB300 (new 14.304 vs CCE 9.870 ms). On B200,
five more LP cells (ckpt, z 0.166) are inconclusive with point estimates
below the noise band (0.9688x-0.9886x); GB300 has none. On the 90
temperature cells (LP+tT, LP+t0.7), PT is the only non-Cake arm timed.
New is faster than PT in all 90 (B200 1.0463x-2.0682x, GB300
1.0555x-2.0734x).

latency / new latency on the same steps (> 1: new faster), its verdict
mark and its CI95. Operations: fwd = forward; bwd = backward; f+b =
forward + backward; ckpt = checkpointed 2x forward + backward.

### [1017bc8](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/1017bc8b0f8d4c4f055dd4575f87ac7fd8cfce1b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T06:04:41Z
- **提交信息**: test(cake_gdn): with grad, stop depending on the former no-det names of the deterministic packages (#8916)

## Summary

The deterministic Cake GDN training packages are
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train`,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp` and the facade
`flashinfer.cake_gdn_det_train_kcp`. They still carry their former
names, which lack "det": `flashinfer.gdn_train`,
`flashinfer.experimental.cake_gdn_train`, `chunk_gdn_kcp` / `KcpOptions`
and `chunk_gated_delta_rule` / `ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFunction` /
`gdn_chunk_forward` / `gdn_chunk_backward`. The KDA compatibility
package `flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_train` has the same problem.
The package owners will delete these names in follow-up PRs and won't
keep compatibility aliases.

This PR stops the non-deterministic GDN tests, benchmark and READMEs
from using these former GDN and KDA names. They pass both before and
after the removals. The former conv1d names used in the same files are
migrated separately by the conv1d package owner (#8912). Package
behavior and kernels are unchanged. The only edits to package files are
three provenance docstrings: they keep the historical KDA source path
and add its current det path.

## Changes
- `tests/experimental/test_cake_gdn_train_kcp_api.py`:
- Removes the test that asserted the former names are the deterministic
objects.
- Keeps one absence test over a single list of former spellings. That
list now also covers `cake_backend`, `cake_build` and `cake_l2n`.
- Keeps a test, checked through the det names, that this package's
entries and types are not the deterministic package's.
- `tests/experimental/test_cake_gdn_train.py`: compares against the
deterministic package's det names instead of its former aliases.
- `test_cake_gdn_train_kcp.py` and `test_cake_gdn_train_kcp_build.py`:
KDA references now use `cake_kda_det_train_kcp.cake_kcp_plan`
(`partition_det_kcp`, `build_context_det_kcp`) and
`cake_kda_det_train.cake_build`.
- `benchmarks/bench_cake_gdn_train_kcp.py`: reads `LAST_CALL` and
`graph_cache_clear` for both routes from each package's `cake_kcp`
module, because the deterministic package will stop re-exporting them at
package level.
- The two non-deterministic READMEs refer to the deterministic packages
only by their det names.

## Testing
One commit on main `3757bab`, head `1d5f7bb`. The first revision
`802dc8a` differs from it only in docstrings and the commit message.
Each run used a clean tree at the named head and a tree with the former
names deleted (simulated removal):
- **CPU at `1d5f7bb`** (CUDA 13.4 devel image, Python 3.14.9, torch
2.14.1+cu130): `test_cake_gdn_train_kcp_api.py`,
`test_cake_gdn_train_kcp_build.py` and `test_cake_gdn_train_kcp.py` gave
454 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed on both trees. `pre-commit` (mypy, ruff
check, ruff format, ...) passes.
- **CPU at `802dc8a`**: `test_cake_gdn_train.py` plus the 8
`test_cake_gdn_train_kcp*.py` files gave 577 passed, 352 skipped, 0
failed on both trees. As a control, the old tests fail 3 on the
simulated-removal tree.
- **GPU at `802dc8a`** (B200, sm_100a): 0 failed on both trees.
  - Non-deterministic API tests: 162 passed.
  - Train names/exports/deterministic tests: 29 passed.
  - Build tests: 37 passed.
- `test_plan_parity_with_kda_on_rows` skips in every environment because
it needs `GDN_ROWS_DIR`. That skip predates this PR and is unchanged.

## Follow-ups
- The deterministic package owners remove the former names.
- The conv1d package owner migrates the former conv1d names in these
files.
- A later PR aligns the `deterministic=` behavior of the
non-deterministic facade with the shared mode rules.

### [0c49b23](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/0c49b232c07221b8194c20bbc528885fd192cb8b)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T05:49:30Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_gemm): cluster DSMEM split-K for the thin FP32 weight gradient on 152-SM sm_100a parts (#8844)

The dense projection GEMM family ships as a deterministic package,
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_det_gemm`, and a
non-deterministic package,
`flashinfer.experimental.dense_projection_gemm`. The family covers K1
BF16 projections with BF16 or FP32 output and an FP32 router GEMM, and
each has forward, input-gradient and weight-gradient programs. This PR
changes one variant: the FP32-output K1 weight gradient dW = G^T X for
the thin rows d_in 4096/5120 → d_out 32/48/64/128 with
`deterministic=False` on 152-SM GB200 (sm_100a). It now runs a cluster
split-K program, with 2 or 3 CTAs per cluster, whose partial sums are
added through distributed shared memory. It uses this program in these T
windows: 4096 → 32: 1024-2048 and 6144-32768; 4096 → 48: 1024-2048,
4096-8192 and 16384-32768; 4096 → 64: 1024-32768; 4096 → 128: 4096-8192;
5120 → 32: 1024-32768; 5120 → 48: 1024-24576; 5120 → 64: 1024-2048 and
4096-24576; 5120 → 128: 1024-6144. Over the 61 rows below, the
new/baseline speedup ranges are:

- **Op:** 1.044-2.079x (geomean 1.289) vs deterministic Cake,
0.778-1.288x (1.080) vs cuBLAS / cuBLASLt and 1.029-1.462x (1.159) vs
the current `deterministic=False` route.
- **Training step:** 1.012-1.243x (1.089), 0.530-1.130x (0.870) and
1.007-1.134x (1.043) against the same three baselines.
- **Checkpointed step:** 1.009-1.154x (1.061), 0.450-1.088x (0.788) and
1.005-1.100x (1.031).

cuBLAS / cuBLASLt is faster than the new route on 20 of 61 op rows
(every row with T ≤ 3072, plus T 4096 on 4096 → 128 and 5120 → 128). It
is also faster on 34 of 61 training-step rows (every T ≤ 4096, T 6144 on
all shapes except 5120 → 32, and T 8192 on 4096 → 32 and 4096 → 128). In
the checkpointed step it is faster on 42 of 61 rows (every T ≤ 8192,
plus T 24576 on 4096 → 32 and 5120 → 32). All timings are CUDA-graph
replay.

NVIDIA GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs), driver 580.126.20 (CUDA 13.4 driver
API), CUDA 13.0 runtime (PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130), kernels JIT-compiled
with nvcc 13.4.92, cuBLAS / cuBLASLt 13.8.0. Timing: CUPTI GPU span of
the call in CUDA graph replay, cold L2 (flushed before every iteration).
Cake values: median of 8 runs on 2 nodes (4 GPUs per node, one run per
GPU: all shapes in one process in forward or reverse order, or one
process per shape in forward or reverse order); each run is the median
of 15 groups x 20 iterations. cuBLAS / cuBLASLt: the faster of
torch.mm(..., out_dtype=torch.float32) and the fastest of the first 8
cuBLASLt heuristic algorithms that meet the same FP32 accuracy budget,
one process per shape on each node, median of the 2 nodes. Ratios > 1
mean the new route is faster; they use the unrounded medians.

### [fb45571](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/fb455719e0511de3a6cd828c736030960bd042df)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T05:48:53Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_alpha_moe): NVFP4 fused batch kernel reduces two output blocks per bulk add on sm_100a (#8903)

The AlphaMoE Cake kernels in FlashInfer come in three sets: NVFP4 MoE,
W8A8 MoE and the fused router. This PR changes one NVFP4 kernel on
sm_100a: the fused batch kernel of the word-scale path. That kernel now
places two adjacent 128-column down-projection output blocks side by
side, using one 1024-byte row per routed token and a ring of two pair
buffers. After the second block it issues one FP32 bulk reduce per row,
so it issues half as many reduces and each one is twice as long. Every
output element gets the same FP32 adds at the same addresses. Only the
arrival order of the top_k adds can change, which can already happen
with the existing unordered bulk reduces. Of the 10 NVFP4 shapes below,
only M=128, N=256, K=7168, block_m=16 runs this kernel. On that shape,
this PR is faster on B200 than the previous version (the Cake AlphaMoE
NVFP4 kernel from FlashInfer #8869, now on main): 1.026x with memset and
1.032x with read. The other 9 shapes run the same machine code on both
sides. Their ratios of 0.999x to 1.001x fall inside the same-node noise
band, which was measured by running the previous code against itself.
Speedup = previous / this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster.

#### B200 (sm_100a)

NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a), driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.3 (PyTorch 2.13, nvcc
13.3). Kernel time per MoE call in us (sum of the MoE kernels of one
call, CUPTI); "memset" clears L2 with a memset of a large buffer and
"read" flushes L2 by reading a large buffer; previous = the Cake NVFP4
kernel from FlashInfer #8869 on main. The M=8/N=256, M=128/N=256,
M=8/N=1024 and M=128/N=1024 rows are the mean of two node medians; the
other 6 rows are one node median. Each node median covers 16 values (8
GPUs x 2 repetitions, paired interleaved).

**memset**

routes and the fused router) keep the same machine code, and the family

running the same machine code as before in this PR.

### [755e972](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/755e9726fb48a4daccb9c2471c6bd9099c602724)

- **时间**: 2026-11-06T05:47:52Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_causal_conv1d_det): det names only, remove the pre-det-rename aliases (#8912)

The deterministic Cake causal conv1d packages now expose only names that
contain `det`. This PR removes the compatibility names kept by #8055. No
alias or compatibility module remains. Callers use the det names that
already exist on main.

This PR moves these call sites to the det names: the KDA and GDN
context-parallel tests, benchmarks, docstrings and READMEs; the
selectable-mode facade docstrings (the
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_causal_conv1d_train` and
`flashinfer.cake_causal_conv1d_train_kcp` entry points keep their
names); `docs/api/mamba.rst`; the test helper's compatibility key; and
the alias test, now replaced by
`tests/norm/test_cake_causal_conv1d_det_train_names.py`, which checks
that the old names are gone.

Kernels, programs and numerics are unchanged.

Tests: on B200 at 076e60aa: test collection 1677 items / 0 errors; the
det conv / KCP / KDA / GDN GPU suites in four groups (485 passed; 285
passed, 14 skipped; 647 passed, 1 skipped; 36 passed) and the 4-GPU dist
group (59 passed, 26 skipped: those rows need 8 or 16 GPUs); the GDN det
and selectable-mode 4-rank conv rows give the same per-test results on
this branch and on main (3 passed, 4 skipped as 8-rank rows, each);
benchmark `--help` 7/7; pre-commit clean.

### [1398884](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/139888400ff008a4136ce6b35e2f7320bb0c0f40)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T05:32:39Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_fp8_rowwise_gemm_allreduce): SM90 fused FP8 GEMM + all-reduce for TP2/4/8 (#8905)

`flashinfer.comm.fp8_rowwise_gemm_allreduce` with `backend="cake"` runs
a row-wise scaled FP8 (e4m3) GEMM and the all-reduce over 2, 4 or 8
ranks on one node in one fused kernel per call, and returns a BF16
output on every rank. It supports one data type combination: FP8 e4m3
inputs with per-row and per-column scales, and BF16 output. This PR adds
sm_90a (H100, Hopper) support for 2, 4 and 8 ranks. All three world
sizes use the peer-to-peer NVLink pull carrier, because NVLink multicast
(NVLS) is not used on sm_90a. One new generated program serves all three
world sizes. A second generated program is selected only at 8 ranks,
when the preallocated capacity is exactly 4096 rows. The existing
sm_100a and sm_103a files are unchanged. On sm_90a the fused kernel is
slower than the PyTorch baseline on most shapes at every world size. The
geomean is 0.957x at 2 ranks, 0.944x at 4 ranks and 0.739x at 8 ranks.
At 8 ranks every shape is slower.

### 2 ranks

Cake has no previous version on sm_90a, so the baseline for all three
world sizes is `torch._scaled_mm` row-wise FP8 GEMM (cuBLASLt, BF16
output) followed by `torch.distributed.all_reduce` in BF16 (NCCL default
algorithm). It runs on one node of 8 NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 GPUs (sm_90a,
Hopper) with CUDA 13.0 and driver 535.216.03. The timed value is the
CUPTI GPU time of one call (median over iterations of the slowest rank).
The L2 cache is flushed and all ranks are synchronized before each call.
Cake and the baseline alternate in the same session (A/B/B/A order).
Each shape has one recorded value. Speedup = baseline / this PR (> 1
means this PR is faster). Geomean 0.957x, 16 of 48 shapes at or above
1.0x, range 0.604x to 1.151x. All 16 of those shapes have M ≥ 8192, and
no shape with M = 4096 reaches 1.0x. One shape shows 1.000x in the table
but is 0.99951x, so it counts as below 1.0x.

### [071dd13](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/071dd138efb146730e01231059a0d033db2dc305)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T05:29:44Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda_det): gate-gradient accuracy of the GLM intra stage (diagonal TF32 rounding) (#8909)

Follow-up to #7817.

## Summary

This PR updates the deterministic Cake package for KDA (Kimi Delta
Attention) chunked training. The package contains the forward and
backward passes. The family has these variants:

- Gate form: `g` (precomputed log gate) or `raw` (the kernel computes
the gate from `A_log` / `dt_bias`).
- Q/K L2 norm: `off`, or `fused` into the kernel.
- Backward path: `saved` (uses the saved forward set) or `replay`
(checkpoint replay, `saved=None`).

The data types are bf16 for q/k/v/beta and fp32 for the gate. The head
dimension is 128.

This PR changes two things:

- **Gate-gradient accuracy fix.** In the backward GLM intra stage, both
members of each diagonal pair term of the gate gradient now round on the
same TF32 operands. dq, dk and dbeta do not change.
- **Rolled loops.** The larger kernels now stay inside the instruction
cache.

On the fast-decay rows, the fix brings the gate-gradient error (the dg,
dA_log and dt_bias gradients) down to about the FLA 0.6.0 `chunk_kda`
level or lower. On main, this error was up to about 50x the FLA level.

Most rows are a little slower. This is the cost of the accuracy fix. The
slowest backward row on every GPU is `4doc:raw:off:saved`: +2.35 % on
GB300, +2.17 % on GB200, +3.92 % on R200 212-SM and +3.42 % on R200
216-SM. On R200, the `raw` + `fused` L2 norm path is faster.

Row key: `rows:gate:l2n:path`.

- `1doc`: 1 sequence of 16384 tokens, 64 heads.
- `4doc`: 4 sequences of 8192/4096/3072/1024 tokens, 64 heads.
- `R2`: 16384 tokens in 3 unequal sequences, 4 heads.
- `m2`: 2 sequences of 2048/1500 tokens, 4 heads.

`bwd` is the backward pass only. `fwd+bwd` is the forward and backward
passes together.

Each time is the median of 15 samples. One sample is the CUDA-event time
of 20 back-to-back calls, divided by 20. The runs used a warm L2 and
eager mode. "before main" is FlashInfer main at 79cf0557, which has the
previous Cake deterministic version. "after head" is this PR. An
after/before value above 1.00 means this PR is slower.

The non-deterministic KDA training package and the context-parallel
(KCP) deterministic package ship separately. This family ships on
sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a.

### [8f62815](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8f628157101f7b6c02723b66cedb7ad9378e56ed)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T05:21:17Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_kda_train_kcp): CUDA 12.9 floor for the sm_100a PTX ISA 8.8 entries (#8911)

Follow-up to https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8896,
which fixed the sm_100a CUDA floor in the deterministic context-parallel
KDA training package. This PR makes the same fix in the experimental
non-deterministic package, `flashinfer/experimental/cake_kda_train_kcp`.
Only `min_cuda` values change. Kernel sources and the sm_103a / sm_107a
floors (12.9 / 13.4) are unchanged, so outputs and gradients are bitwise
identical to main.

- **sm_100a CUDA floor:** Kernels using the 256-bit `st.global.v8.b32`
store need PTX ISA 8.8. CUDA 12.8 emits 8.7, so ptxas rejects them. Four
sm_100a entries change `min_cuda` from "12.8" to "12.9", which matches
their deterministic twins. Two are in `build.json` (forward output stage
and output backward). The other two are test-only full-width tape walks
in `build.test.json`. No other entry's units use a PTX ISA 8.8
instruction. The build test
`test_an_entry_whose_units_use_ptx_isa_8_8_needs_cuda_12_9` from #8896
now also covers this package. It fails on main's manifests and passes
with this change.
- **Walk-form rules:** This package doesn't need the provider fix from
#8896. All of its `WALK_FORM_RULES` are strings, so `_walk_form_of`
never passes `arch=` to the rule. A provider whose `walk_form` takes
only `knob` already works.

### [abbe776](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/abbe776c8c9f7be408e2f24f2f9450d0dae41c10)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T05:02:06Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_lm_head_loss): two-slice counted dX and a 1946-row zero-gradient floor on sm_107a (#8902)

Cake's chunked LM-head + loss training backend covers cross-entropy
loss, policy loss, log-probability with no temperature, a scalar
temperature or a per-token FP32 `[T]` temperature, support
log-probability and support-KL, on BF16 hidden states and weights. The
backend has a deterministic form and a non-deterministic (ND) form.
`deterministic=False` on the public `flashinfer.chunked_lm_head` entries
(`chunked_lm_head_loss`, `chunked_lm_head_logprob`,
`chunked_lm_head_support_logprob`, `chunked_lm_head_support_kl`) selects
the ND form, implemented in
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_lm_head_loss`.

On sm_107a, this PR starts the zero-gradient (zero dlogp) row skip of
the ND log-probability backward, with or without temperature, at 1946
valid rows instead of the generic 4097 (`ZERO_DLOGP_MIN_ROWS_BY_ARCH`).
Under that skip, a dX chunk that the slice rule gives one K slice now
uses two (the two-slice rule, `DX_COUNTED_MIN_SLICES_BY_ARCH`), as on
sm_100a and sm_103a, which are unchanged.

The tables below give absolute ms for R200 (sm_107a) 212-SM and 216-SM
boards separately, 195 cells each. Against the previous ND plan (prev),
this PR's ND plan (new) is faster in 21 cells on 212-SM
(1.0260x-1.2225x) and 30 on 216-SM (1.0187x-1.2562x). All faster cells
have z > 0 and T 16172 or 16231 (216-SM also T 32463). The largest ratio
on each is h09 bwd (212-SM 1.2225x, 17.742 -> 14.513 ms; 216-SM 1.2562x,
19.592 -> 15.597 ms). No cell is slower than prev. Against deterministic
Cake (det), new is faster in 132 cells on 212-SM (1.0185x-2.1309x) and
140 on 216-SM (1.0136x-1.9662x). It is slower than det only in h13 fwd
and h14 fwd on 212-SM (C 8192; new 8.168 vs det 8.052 ms, new 8.218 vs
det 8.088 ms). Prev is also slower than det there by point estimate.

SOTA is the fastest non-Cake arm timed in each cell. On the 90
temperature cells (LP+tT, LP+t0.7), SOTA is PyTorch chunked +
torch.compile (PT), the only non-Cake arm timed there. New is faster
than PT in all 90 (212-SM 1.0673x-2.2278x, 216-SM 1.0470x-2.0007x). On
the 105 log-probability (LP) cells, SOTA is Cut Cross-Entropy 25.1.1
(CCE, torch.compile path). New is faster than CCE in 53 LP cells on
212-SM (1.0248x-1.5008x) and 60 on 216-SM (1.0188x-1.4751x). It is
slower than CCE in 34 on 212-SM (0.7077x-0.9684x) and 35 on 216-SM
(0.7302x-0.9738x), all at z 0 or 0.166. Prev is also slower than CCE in
all of them by point estimate. The lowest ratio against CCE is p01 bwd
(new vs CCE: 212-SM 8.667 vs 6.134 ms, 216-SM 8.491 vs 6.201 ms).

### [7481099](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7481099d98f22d2801da55fd77f3368ec35575e6)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T04:59:40Z
- **提交信息**: refactor(cake_mhc_det): remove the mHC training names without det (#8900)

Every public function and class name in the deterministic Cake mHC
training package now includes `det`. This PR removes the names that
FlashInfer 0.7.3 used for the same deterministic objects. It adds no
alias module, no top-level alias and no deprecation shim.

### Renamed / removed

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `flashinfer.cake_mhc_train` (module) | `flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train`
|
| `flashinfer.cake_mhc_train_backend` (package) |
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train_backend` |
| `flashinfer.cake_mhc_train_head_backend` (package) |
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train_head_backend` |
| `flashinfer.cake_mhc_train_<name>` |
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_det_train_<name>` |
| `flashinfer.CakeMHCTrain{Prepare,Finish,Head}Function` |
`flashinfer.CakeMHCDetTrain{Prepare,Finish,Head}Function` |
| `is_cake_mhc_train_supported` (removed modules) |
`is_cake_mhc_det_train_supported` |
| `is_cake_mhc_train_head_supported` (removed modules) |
`is_cake_mhc_det_train_head_supported` |

`<name>` is one of these 12 functions: `forward_prepare`,
`forward_stats`, `forward_finish`, `backward_prepare`,
`backward_finish`, `prepare`, `finish`, `head`, `head_forward`,
`head_backward`, `forward_workspace_bytes`, `backward_workspace_bytes`.
With the three autograd classes, this PR removes 15 top-level names. All
new names already exist on `main`.

### Breaking change

FlashInfer 0.7.3 shipped the deterministic package under
`flashinfer.cake_mhc_train`. The `det` names did not exist in 0.7.3.
After this PR, code that imports the old names gets `ImportError` or
`AttributeError`. To migrate, replace `cake_mhc_train` with
`cake_mhc_det_train`. Replace `CakeMHCTrain` with `CakeMHCDetTrain`.

### Not changed

This PR does not change kernels, routing, numerics or the deterministic
package's behavior. The names without `det` now belong only to the
experimental selectable-mode module
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train`. That module's
non-deterministic package is
`flashinfer.experimental.cake.cake_mhc_train_backend`.

Generic constants and route helpers keep their names because the module
path qualifies them. These are `ARCHES`,
`SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES`, `TENSOR_ALIGNMENT_BYTES`,
`WORKSPACE_ALIGNMENT_BYTES`, `route_key` and `route_modules`.

A follow-up PR will align the experimental module's `deterministic=`
keyword and its `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` behavior with
the other Cake training families.

### Docs and tests

A note at the top of the training section in `docs/api/mhc.rst` now
states the naming rule. The page no longer has the removed module's text
or autosummary. The `det` facade and selector module docstrings state
the same rule.

`tests/cpu/mhc/test_cake_mhc_det_train_names.py` replaces
`tests/cpu/mhc/test_cake_mhc_det_train_aliases.py`. It checks that:
- the removed modules cannot be imported;
- no top-level name without `det` remains;
- the `det` modules export only `det` names and the generic names above;
- no `det` entry point takes a `deterministic` keyword.

The experimental API and rules tests no longer refer to the removed
module.

The API-diff report for this PR lists 15 removed top-level exports and 3
removed public modules. This is intended.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai
-->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **API Changes**
* Removed the legacy non-`det` mHC training names and compatibility
modules; these names are no longer available as aliases.
* Deterministic training APIs remain available under their `det`-named
names.
* Selectable-mode training APIs are available through the experimental
package. The model head has no counterpart in that namespace.
* **Documentation**
* Clarified the naming distinction between deterministic and
selectable-mode training APIs.

### [ba14d1e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/ba14d1e28bfa89473f3ed25ce450b0e9f7a74091)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T04:35:19Z
- **提交信息**: cake_mla_value_gate: load the request lengths through L1 (#8904)

`cake_mla_value_gate` has one variant (BF16 inputs and output, FP32
sigmoid, H × 512 → H × 128 per row), and this PR updates that variant:
its two per-row request-length loads (`valid_lengths`) are now ordinary
global loads that may be cached in L1 instead of L2-only loads. The
baseline is the previous Cake version of the kernel, which FlashInfer
main has shipped since #8867. Using the criterion in the table captions,
2 of 96 rows are faster on GB300, 3 on B200 and 3 on B300, at
1.051×–1.065×; they are at B = 48 standalone with warm L2 and at B = 64
behind a PDL predecessor with cold L2 and pitch 3648 gate rows. Every
other row is at parity, none is slower, and the median speedup is 1.000×
in each L2 / launch mode on every GPU except warm-L2 standalone on B300
(1.007×). Every row with a ratio below 1 differs by less than 128 ns
(the lowest, 0.941× on B300, is 126 ns) and is within measurement noise,
with warm-L2 standalone the noisiest mode.

**NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4 toolkit, driver 580.159.03.** Both
kernel versions and the inputs are in one process on one GPU and are
measured interleaved under CUDA graph replay. Each time is the median
over 8 groups of the per-group CUPTI time of the kernel, in µs.
Standalone = the kernel's time when launched alone; behind PDL
predecessor = the time the kernel adds after a predecessor kernel that
triggers programmatic dependent launch (exposed time). Warm L2 = inputs
resident in L2; cold L2 = inputs evicted between calls. H = 12 heads
(Kimi-K3 TP8 decode), one query row per request, all rows valid. Pitch
3648 = gate logits as a strided row slice (row pitch 3648 elements, as
in SGLang); contiguous = gate rows of 1536 elements. Speedup = previous

### [9885584](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/98855843366bc2ae3cebbb6de1170b50359c9521)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T04:15:40Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_rmsnorm): blocked FP32 dw sums for the large-T GB300 backward windows (#8899)

Related issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/8066

`flashinfer.cake_rmsnorm_train` is RMSNorm for training. The forward
returns y (BF16) and rstd (FP32), and the backward returns dx (BF16) and
dw (FP32). The two modes, `deterministic=True` and
`deterministic=False`, share the forward and differ only in the
backward. Both modes support:

- [T, H] rows with BF16 or FP32 weight
- a fused residual add (H6144)
- per-head views [T,24,256] (strided) and [T,4,256] (contiguous), with a
shared w[256]

This PR follows #8577, #8626, #8655, #8704, #8810, #8827, #8848 and
#8849. It changes only the `deterministic=False` backward on sm_103a
(GB300). The change covers H1536, H2048 and H6144, with BF16 or FP32
weight, plain rows, in the windows listed below. FlashInfer main runs a
TwoSum single in all of these windows, the same program that stays above
T 131072. With this PR, the backward in each window runs one of two
program kinds:

- kb: a single kernel with blocked FP32 dw sums, the kernel kind that
#8655 ships on GB300
- det: the same programs as `deterministic=True`

The windows are:

- H1536, BF16 weight: kb on T 46593 to 53184 and on T 76353 to 131072;
det on T 53185 to 76352
- H1536, FP32 weight: kb on T 37889 to 40448 and on T 76353 to 131072;
det on T 40449 to 76352
- H2048, both weight dtypes: det on T 61953 to 68160 (the programs that
#8810 routes on T 58497 to 61952); kb on T 68161 to 131072
- H6144, BF16 weight: det on T 49153 to 57344; kb on T 57345 to 131072
- H6144, FP32 weight: det on T 49153 to 83392; kb on T 83393 to 131072

In every ratio below, a value under 1 means the baseline is faster than
new. The ranges cover all rows of the table, except that the SOTA ranges
leave out the rows marked !.

- **Against main.** main is the TwoSum single this PR replaces. new is
faster on every bwd and 2xfwd+bwd row where main was timed (20 shapes,
run A). bwd is 1.0279 to 1.2870 and 2xfwd+bwd is 1.0128 to 1.1468. These
ratios are det-anchored (see Measurement).
- **Against det on the 20 det shapes.** new runs det's programs there,
and the table repeats det's time, so det/new is 1.0000.
- **Against det on the 27 kb shapes.** det is faster than new on 25 of
27 bwd rows (det/new 0.9426 to 0.9989). new is faster on the other 2:
H6144 with BF16 weight at T 98304 and 131072 (1.0060 and 1.0115). On
2xfwd+bwd, det/new is 0.9699 to 1.0058, and det is faster on 24 of 27
rows. On 23 bwd rows and 18 2xfwd+bwd rows (marked -), det is faster
than new in all 4 sessions, each time by more than the row's A/A floor
in that session. new is faster in the same sense on 3 rows (marked +):
bwd of H6144 with BF16 weight at T 98304 and 131072, and 2xfwd+bwd at T
131072.
- **Against the strongest in-budget non-Cake SOTA.** On the 43 shapes
that have an in-budget SOTA, bwd is 0.9896 to 1.5171 and 2xfwd+bwd is
0.9964 to 1.3069. SOTA is faster than new on 1 bwd row (QA, H1536 T
131072 with FP32 weight) and on 1 2xfwd+bwd row (TC, H2048 T 114688 with
BF16 weight).
- On 4 shapes, no non-Cake candidate meets the dw budget (marked !):
H6144 T 131072 with BF16 weight, and H6144 T 114688, 122880 and 131072
with FP32 weight.
- On these shapes, the fastest candidate that has these outputs is QA.
Its worst dw element is 1.543 to 2.976 times the budget. It is faster
than new: bwd 0.9210 to 0.9630 and 2xfwd+bwd 0.9666 to 0.9829.
- **Forward.** This PR does not change the forward, and the fwd values
are as measured. main/new is 0.9961 to 1.0018. det/new on kb shapes is
0.9956 to 1.0030. SOTA/new is 0.9893 to 1.1306 and is below 1 on 7 rows:
every H6144 row with BF16 weight, and H2048 T 131072 with BF16 weight.

**Measurement**

- **Latency:** the median of the CUPTI span of one CUDA-graph replay
with L2 flushed (cold L2). Each run uses the 4 GPUs of one GB300 node,
one session per GPU. Each session times 201 replays per implementation
and op, split over 3 interleaved rounds, and the median pools the 4
sessions. Each implementation's own setup, reduction, cast and copy
kernels are inside the span. In each session, det, new and every
non-Cake candidate run in one process, and the implementation order
rotates. Over the table's rows, the largest |1 - A/A| in a session is
0.0066 to 0.0341 across the 12 sessions of the three runs. In the 4
sessions of main's process, it is 0.0080 to 0.0277.
- **Context:** on small rows, Cake gains somewhat more than the other
non-compile libraries from sharing the process with torch.compile. On
GB300, SOTA/new vs the non-compile candidates is up to about 1.10x
higher in the one-process measurement than in a process without
torch.compile; on large rows the difference is <= 1.02x. Every row here
is a large row (T >= 37889). Ratios vs det are unaffected.
- **Runs:** A, B and C ran on three different GB300 nodes. Each row
comes from one run (column run): from A where A measured the shape,
otherwise from B or C. A and one other run both measured 8 shapes. On
those shapes, the other run's det/new differs from A's by at most
0.0017, and its SOTA/new by at most 0.0084.
- **Builds:** det and new were timed on an earlier build of this branch.
On kb rows, that build runs the same kb program as this PR's head. It
also ran kb in the det windows, so on det rows new us is det's time (see
Key). Its det programs in these windows are the same as on FlashInfer
main at this PR's base, and this PR does not change them. main, and the
det it is anchored to, were timed on an earlier FlashInfer main build.
In these windows, that build's main and det programs are the same as on
FlashInfer main at this PR's base.
- **det and new:** det = deterministic Cake (`deterministic=True`),
which this PR does not change. new = this PR's non-deterministic Cake
(`deterministic=False`).
- **SOTA:** the fastest non-Cake candidate in the run that has these
outputs and meets the accuracy budget. The budget is dx atol = rtol =
1e-2 and dw per element atol 1e-4 + rtol 1e-4 vs FP64, taking the worst
of 5 seeds. new meets the dw budget in every changed window. On the 8
rows marked !, no candidate meets the budget (see Key).
- Candidates: QuACK 0.6.5 (heuristic config and per-shape autotuned),
torch.compile (torch 2.14.1+cu130; max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and
default mode) of the explicit FP32-statistics reference, Liger-Kernel
0.8.5, and Transformer Engine 2.20.2 (run as the FP32 problem).
- On BF16-weight rows, library APIs that return dw in BF16 do not have
these outputs, so they are never chosen as SOTA.
- **main:** this backend on FlashInfer main before this PR. Its
`deterministic=False` backward runs the TwoSum single in these windows.
  - main was timed only in run A, in its own process together with det.
- main/new = (main / det of that process) / (new / det of new's
process).
- main us is main's latency in that process. main/new is det-anchored,
so it can differ slightly from main us / new us. n/a means main was not
timed at that shape.
- **Speedup:** baseline latency / new latency (> 1: new is faster; < 1:
the baseline is faster).

Key:

- **kb / det at the end of the workload:** the program new runs at that
T. kb = the single kernel with blocked FP32 dw sums. det = the programs
of `deterministic=True`. On det rows, new us is det's measurement from
the same run, so det/new is 1.0000 by construction.
- **op 2xfwd+bwd:** checkpointed step (forward, forward recompute,
backward).
- **+ / - after det/new:** in each of the 4 sessions of that run,
det/new differs from 1 by more than the row's A/A floor in that session,
and all 4 sessions agree that new (+) or det (-) is faster. Each session
also times a second copy of det and of new. A row's A/A floor in a
session is the larger |1 - A/A| of its det and new copies. Unmarked rows
do not meet that test.
- **! after the SOTA impl and after SOTA/new:** no non-Cake candidate
meets the dw budget. The table shows the fastest candidate that has
these outputs, with its worst dw element as a multiple of the budget in
parentheses, and computes SOTA/new against it.
- **SOTA names:**
  - Q = QuACK, heuristic config
  - QA = QuACK, per-shape autotuned
  - TC = torch.compile, inductor mode max-autotune-no-cudagraphs
  - TCd = torch.compile, inductor default mode

on sm_100a, sm_103a and sm_107a. This PR does not change the forward,
`deterministic=True`, the sm_100a or sm_107a routes, or any GB300 window
other than the ones above.

### [34e476c](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/34e476cbf9fe3dacd7bb3fbc4186c89b9eead1ea)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T04:07:00Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_vsa_sm120): overlap softmax with P*V and move mbarrier retries off the block loop (#8898)

`BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="vsa_sm120_blk64")` on SM120 /
SM121 has 4 Cake variants: the BF16 and FP16 builds of two persistent
kernels, `vsa_sm120_blk64` (two 128-thread CTAs per SM) and
`vsa_sm120_blk64_pair` (one CTA of two 4-warp groups per SM). Both
kernels run one host plan, and the host planner picks the kernel per
shape; the kernels cover head dim 128, 64 x 64 blocks, GQA and optional
LSE. This PR regenerates all 4 variants. In `vsa_sm120_blk64`, the P·V
MMAs of one key group now run between the softmax steps of the next
group, and in both kernels the compiler now keeps the mbarrier wait
retry loops out of the block loop, with the API, host plan and outputs
unchanged (bitwise equal to main). The baseline is FlashInfer main,
which runs the previous Cake version of these kernels (from #8799 and
#8829); speedup = main / this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is
faster. Across all 100 shapes, the geomean speedup is 1.023 with nvcc
13.0 (100 of 100 at or above 1.0, slowest 1.002) and 1.011 with nvcc
13.4 (82 of 100 at or above 1.0, slowest 0.988); on the 22 delivery
shapes it is 1.029 and 1.006.

Measured on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120,
driver 595.84.01) with the kernels JIT-built by CUDA 13.0 (nvcc 13.0.88)
and CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92); `wrapper.run` latency is timed with CUPTI
and a cold L2, and each value is the median over 3 interleaved rounds x
3 input placements.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
* Invalid negative work counts now stop processing instead of continuing
through attention calculations.
* Attention calculations now apply normalization consistently as score
groups are processed, improving output consistency across workloads.
* Valid nonnegative work counts continue through the existing processing
path.

### [38bfc1b](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/38bfc1b1074055ee82f97fe538a3a5ffc06fcf0f)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T03:59:01Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dsa_indexer_det): an FP8 wide scan program on sm_100a (#8895)

The deterministic DSA indexer top-k,
`flashinfer.dsa_indexer.dsa_indexer_det_topk(..., backend="cake")`, has
two Cake variants: the default BF16 form and the opt-in FP8 form, which
#8749 added and #8781 improved. #8841 added an FP8 wide program on
sm_103a. This PR changes only the FP8 form, and only on sm_100a
(measured on NVIDIA B200). On sm_100a, the FP8 form had no 8-query wide
program. As a result, calls planned as an unsplit wide unit ran the
6-query l6 program. On sm_100a they now run a new FP8 wide program (and
its longest-segment-first twin). sm_103a keeps the wide program from
#8841. sm_107a keeps its FP8 dispatch, because this PR registers no FP8
wide program there. Of the five shapes, two are planned as wide on B200:
s1_8k_on_64k and s2_4x2k_packed. s1_8k_on_64k runs 1.18x faster than the
previous Cake FP8 form and 1.39x faster than DeepGEMM + FlashInfer
top-k. s2_4x2k_packed runs 1.10x and 1.44x faster. The other three rows
keep their program, so their 1.00x against the previous Cake FP8 form is
parity, not a speedup.

**NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.** All
rows use top-k 2048, key ratio 1 and causal queries (each segment's
queries are its last positions). P1 is a recorded packed training call.
s2_4x2k_packed is 4 x 2048 queries over 18432 / 43008 / 67584 / 100352
keys. This PR is measured at the PR head. Previous Cake FP8 is the FP8
form on main before this PR (the #8841 dispatch, which runs wide units
with l6 on sm_100a), reproduced in the same process. DeepGEMM +
FlashInfer top-k runs DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` (branch `nv_dev`,
commit `b64107f2`) with FP32 per-key K scales and FP32 logits.
FlashInfer `top_k_ragged_transform(deterministic=True, tie_break=LARGE)`
then runs over each row's visible keys. Two DeepGEMM arms were measured
on every row, and the table reports the faster one (the ragged top-k arm
on every row, which reads the row-padded logits in place). Each time is
the CUPTI GPU interval over every kernel that the call launches, with
cold L2 and eager launch. Cake arms time a prepared runner into
caller-owned outputs and workspace. Each value is the median over three
arm orders (A then B, B then A, interleaved). s1_8k_on_64k and
s2_4x2k_packed were each measured on two GPUs, and each value is the
median of the two (spread: s1_8k_on_64k this PR 3.011 to 3.078 ms,
previous 3.586 to 3.598 ms; s2_4x2k_packed this PR 2.619 to 2.626 ms,
previous 2.873 to 2.883 ms). The other rows were measured on one GPU.
"vs previous" = previous time / this PR time. "vs DeepGEMM" = DeepGEMM
time / this PR time. A value above 1 means this PR is faster. All arms
return bit-identical scores and ids on every row.

### [3757bab](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/3757bab377c4ea3055f76e67ffafbfd632164a59)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T03:14:21Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mla): hide the V-shift hand-offs of the NVFP4 MLA paged decode wide route behind loads (#8884)

The experimental Cake dense NVFP4 MLA paged decode,
`flashinfer.mla.cake_mla_nvfp4_paged_decode(...)`, serves the Kimi-K3 /
DeepSeek-V3 geometry (512 latent + 64 rope channels per key). It reads
an NVFP4 query and the NVFP4 paged latent cache. Its package has seven
programs:

- three narrow swapped-AB schedules at 16, 32 and 48 packed (token,
head) rows (`main_rt16`, `main_rt32`, `main_rt48`), for requests with at
most 48 packed rows
- the two-CTA wide schedule `main_wide`, for larger requests (H96 /
H128, and MTP with q_len x heads > 48)
- a BF16-to-NVFP4 query quantizer
- two split-KV merge programs (a warp reducer and a CTA reducer)

This PR changes only the device code of `main_wide`. Its program name
(`..._32a47bbfa05aebbc97c5`), binding, launch and shared memory stay the
same. The per-token V-scale shift from #8837 added two hand-offs to
every KV tile, and the new code overlaps them with loads already in
flight. Outputs are bitwise identical to main.

The baseline is the previous Cake version of `main_wide` on FlashInfer
main. On the seven `main_wide` rows, old/new is 1.0026–1.0142 on GB300
(new is 0.3–1.4 % faster) and 1.0119–1.0298 on GB200 (new is 1.2–3.0 %
faster). Rows that use unchanged programs read 0.9946–1.0007 on GB300
and 0.9872–1.0073 on GB200. That range is measurement noise between
identical programs, and the two smallest GB300 wide-row gains (1.0026,
1.0028) fall inside it.

**How latency was measured.** Each value is the latency in µs of one
complete call: attention plus the split-KV merge when the plan has one.
`complete_call_h12_b8_q1_kv131072` takes a BF16 query, so its call also
includes the query quantizer.

- Calls run as CUDA graph replays with a cold L2 before every call.
- Each value is the median of the steady samples. A steady sample is a
timed call whose previous call ran the same version.
- Each row gets a 400-call warm-up, then 4 groups x 400 timed calls,
giving 400 steady samples per version.
- Old is FlashInfer main at 4d0c28d8, the previous Cake version of
`main_wide` with the same program name. New is this PR. Both ran in the
same process on the same inputs.
- old/new > 1 means new is faster. Ratios come from the unrounded
medians.
- GPUs: NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a, 152 SMs, driver 580.159.03) and NVIDIA
GB200 (sm_100a, 152 SMs, driver 580.126.20).
- Kernels were compiled with CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4) and run under PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.
- The shapes are the 22 rows from #6242. In each label, h is heads, b is
batch, q is query tokens per request, and kv is the KV length of the
longest request in the batch. Page size is 64.
`long_split_h12_kv65536_lse` also writes the LSE.

### [617a70f](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/617a70f6445b6a28b14e1579e9e53ffde7640c10)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T03:01:38Z
- **提交信息**: fix(cake_gdn_det): launch the fwd_ho_vh2 stage on fwd_ho's grid where its record is the fwd_ho program (#8887)

#8805 added the `fwd_ho_vh2` stage to
`flashinfer/experimental/cake_gdn_det_train`. The stage splits the fused
forward scan and output by value halves. It uses two CTAs per segment
and value head, so its grid is twice the size of the plain `fwd_ho`
grid. It is on by default only on sm_107a (`FWD_HO_VH2_ARCHS =
("sm_107a",)`). The package ships no separate value-half kernel for
sm_100a or sm_103a, so on those architectures the `fwd_ho_vh2` record is
the plain `fwd_ho` program.

`test_the_value_half_split_gives_the_fwd_ho_bits` forces the stage on
the device's architecture. On sm_100a/sm_103a, the chain then launched
the plain `fwd_ho` program on the doubled grid. The extra CTAs read past
the end of the segment walk and caused `CUDA error: an illegal memory
access`. The error is sticky, so about 87 later tests in the same
process also failed. On B200 the suite gave 151 passed and 88 failed.
Default calls never take this path on sm_100a/sm_103a, and on sm_107a
the record is the real value-half kernel.

This PR adds a helper, `fwd_ho_vh2_splits(arch)`, that reports whether
an architecture's `fwd_ho_vh2` record is a different program from
`fwd_ho`. The grid is doubled only when it is. On sm_100a/sm_103a, a
forced `fwd_ho_vh2` stage now runs the `fwd_ho` program on its own grid
and produces the same bits. A CPU assertion covers the helper: it
returns False on sm_100a and sm_103a and True on sm_107a. On B200
(sm_100a) the full test file now gives 239 passed, 0 failed and 6
skipped, compared with 151 passed and 88 failed on main. Default
launches don't change on any architecture, and neither does performance.

### [7acea03](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/7acea035ace23b49535948d97682d6961714f823)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:54:12Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_dense_projection_det_gemm): drop the 3-split router weight-gradient rule at H 6144 (#8886)

This PR changes the Cake `dense_projection_det_gemm` package in
`flashinfer.experimental`, the deterministic dense projection GEMM. The
package has BF16-operand forward, dgrad and wgrad programs and an FP32
router GEMM. The router GEMM has three layouts: forward (`kk`, 4 split-K
partitions by default), input gradient (`kn`, 1) and weight gradient
(`nn_t`, 6). Each router launch splits the second operand into BF16x3,
runs the program and sums the split-K partials. If the caller passes no
`splits`, the router weight gradient gets its split-K count from
`ROUTER_SPLIT_RULES`. Before this PR, that table had 8 entries. They
cover 256 experts (N = 256) and T 16129 to 16384 on `sm_100a` and
`sm_103a` at 148 and 152 SMs. Hidden size 5120 used 9 splits, and hidden
size 6144 used 3 splits. This PR removes the 4 hidden-size-6144 entries,
so those shapes go back to the default of 6 splits. The 4
hidden-size-5120 entries keep 9 splits. Nothing else in planning
changes, and no kernel source or compiled library changes. The 3-split
value was picked on an idle GPU, where it is 1.2 to 2.9 % faster than 6
splits. In training, a kernel on another stream often holds some SMs,
for example a communication kernel. In that case 3 splits loses. In one
measured cell it was 1.38x slower than 6 splits. With this PR, the
idle-GPU rows are 1.2 to 2.8 % slower. We accept that cost because the
change removes the large loss under SM sharing.

**Speedup of this PR over the previous Cake version on main.** Values
are previous / this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster. The
previous version used 3 splits at hidden size 6144. The timed launch is
the whole router weight-gradient call: the BF16x3 split, the program and
the sum of partials. Isolated means an idle GPU with cold L2, taking the
median over passes. Co-run means another stream holds 8, 16 or 32 SMs.
Co-run values are the geometric mean over eager and CUDA graph launches
and three launch orders. Both sides are paired in every pass and run.
All runs use CUDA 13.4 and FP32 output. The GPUs are GB200 (`sm_100a`,
152 SMs), GB300 (`sm_103a`, 152 SMs), B200 (`sm_100a`, 148 SMs) and B300
(`sm_103a`, 148 SMs). The layer is 6144→256 with T 16129, 16231 and
16384, which gives 12 rows. Isolated, this PR scores 0.972-0.988x, so it
is 1.2-2.8 % slower. With 8 SMs held, it scores 0.973-1.209x. That is
1.18-1.21x faster on the 148-SM parts and 2-3 % slower on the 152-SM
parts. With 16 SMs held it scores 1.067-1.165x, and with 32 SMs held it
scores 1.061-1.095x.

### [90eb5cf](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/90eb5cf131e9785cf38a004e605d683501d6d990)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:51:03Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_mhc_det): with grad, L2 hints for fn partial sums and launch tuning on sm_100a / sm_107a (#8870)

FlashInfer's Cake deterministic mHC backend holds the four-stream mHC
kernels with grad. It has forward prepare / recompute and gradient
routes at hidden sizes 4096, 5120 and 7168, group-row forms above 14927
tokens, the dual-layout fn split and the mapping-pass forms. On sm_100a,
the gradient route's slab kernel writes per-slab fn-gradient partial
sums, and a reduction kernel then reads them. Main writes these partial
sums with the default L2 policy, and on these shapes most of them come
back from DRAM. This PR adds `_dpl` forms for 4096 ≤ T ≤ 8192: two slab
forms and three reduction forms. The slab kernel stores the partial sums
with EVICT_LAST, and the reduction kernel loads them with EVICT_FIRST.
In ncu on B200, the reduction kernel's DRAM read falls from 18.02 MB to
0.70 MB at T = 4096 and from 21.35 MB to 1.26 MB at T = 8192. Its time
falls from 9.25 µs to 7.42 µs at T = 4096 and from 9.60 µs to 7.62 µs at
T = 8192. Also on sm_100a, the existing `_xn` mapping-pass forms now run
for 6144 < T ≤ 7168 as well as 64 < T ≤ 6144. On sm_107a, on the
activation-checkpoint route for 3584 ≤ T ≤ 4096, the gradient-route slab
kernel now launches without programmatic dependent launch after the
preceding kernel. Main launches it early with programmatic dependent
launch. sm_103a is unchanged. Outputs and gradients are bitwise
identical to main and deterministic run to run, and the public API is
unchanged. The baseline, "previous", is the current Cake version of the
same kernels in FlashInfer main.

**NVIDIA B200, sm_100a, 148 SMs; CUDA 13.4 toolkit, PyTorch
2.14.1+cu130.** Times are CUPTI active GPU time (the union of kernel
intervals) in microseconds. L2 is flushed with a memset before every
timed call. "Forward" is forward prepare + finish. "Checkpoint" is the
activation-checkpoint recompute followed by the gradient route. Every
shape uses 4 streams, hidden 4096 and T tokens. Each session interleaves
three arms in 6 ABC/CBA groups of 32 iterations: previous, this PR, and
a second previous run as a control. Each value is the mean of two

### [413990a](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/413990ad0cc34f15d3ec3d312466f54aef4ef573)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:44:58Z
- **提交信息**: build: write flashinfer/_build_meta.py atomically (#8883)

Since #7897 overlaps the AOT provider builds within one job, the `AOT
Build Import` jobs fail intermittently in the provider wheel build:

```
  File "/workspace/flashinfer/version.py", line 21, in <module>
    __version__: str = _build_meta.__version__
AttributeError: module 'flashinfer._build_meta' has no attribute '__version__'
```

Each concurrent build imports `build_backend.py` at start-up, and
`_create_build_metadata()` truncates and rewrites
`flashinfer/_build_meta.py` on every import in a git checkout. A build
that imports `flashinfer` at that moment reads an empty module.
Examples: runs 42137289813 (attempts 1 and 2) and 42140527393 (attempts
1 and 2), and the same error on other PRs since 2026-11-06 00:11 UTC.

This PR skips the rewrite when the content is unchanged, and otherwise
writes a temporary file and `os.replace()`s it, so readers see either
the old or the new file. It is the same kind of fix that #7897 applied
to `_create_data_dir()`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai
-->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

* Build metadata is left unchanged when it already matches, reducing
unnecessary file updates. When updates are needed, they are applied more
safely to reduce the chance of incomplete metadata.

### [97f812e](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/97f812ed3b1c284ff6f4c9e2c1eff0a513993dca)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:36:28Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_alpha_moe): NVFP4 fused batch kernel keeps its activation scale in registers on sm_100a (#8869)

The AlphaMoE Cake kernels in FlashInfer come in three sets: NVFP4 MoE,
W8A8 MoE and the fused router. This PR changes one NVFP4 kernel on
sm_100a: the fused batch kernel of the word-scale path. That kernel now
computes each 16-lane group's scale in registers, so its quant loop
reads no shared memory. It also decodes the E4M3 scale without branches
and builds the 16 packed words in one pass before storing them. The
per-element math is unchanged. Of the 10 NVFP4 shapes below, only M=128,
N=256, K=7168, block_m=16 runs this kernel. On that shape, this PR is
faster on B200 than the previous version (the Cake AlphaMoE NVFP4 kernel
on FlashInfer main): 1.006x with memset and 1.010x with read. Speedup =
previous / this PR, so a value above 1 means this PR is faster.

#### B200 (sm_100a)

NVIDIA B200 (sm_100a), driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.3 (PyTorch 2.13, nvcc
13.3). Kernel time per call in us (sum of the MoE kernels of one call);
"memset" clears L2 with a memset of a large buffer and "read" flushes L2
by reading a large buffer; previous = the Cake NVFP4 kernel on
FlashInfer main. The M=8/N=256, M=128/N=256, M=8/N=1024 and M=128/N=1024
rows are the mean of two node medians; the other 6 rows are one node
median. Each node median covers 16 values (8 GPUs x 2 repetitions,
paired interleaved).

### [9b0149d](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/9b0149d70a47b1a9348607a3703139f2c59bed25)

- **作者**: adsridhar
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:33:26Z
- **提交信息**: feat(sm100): add opt-in ExpCast for avoiding exponential in S->P for FP8 PV (#6481)

# Opt-in ExpCast for blockscaled attention

## 📌 Description

Adds `p_exp_mode="expcast"`, based on VC Attention, to directly encode
log-domain softmax scores as E4M3 probabilities (fixed `beta=-0.35`).
The S→P path reuses the Prims-TS `expcast_e4m3_quad_relu` helper for
E4M3
encoding and FP16 partial sums, and `f16x2_sum4` for FP32 reduction.
Normalization sums the decoded FP8 weights consumed by PV.
Supports NVFP4/MXFP8 QK, E4M3 FP8 PV, D=128, MHA and GQA. ExpCast is
JIT-only;
`exp2` remains the default. Existing scheduling and resource allocation
retained.

## Benchmark

Device: NVIDIA B200. Batch size: 1. MHA Hq/Hkv=32/32 and GQA=32/8,
D=128, BF16 output, LSE disabled, seed=0, threshold 2^-8 / P offset +8.
Each sweep has 216 cases: nine shapes, both masks, both QK modes, three
kernels
and both schedulers. Source JIT; 5 warmups / 30 measured iterations;
CUDA Graph,
CUPTI preferred/CUDA-graph event fallback. Compilation, quantization and
reference
are excluded. The updated runner explicitly uses warm-cache timing for
both
backends (`cold_l2_cache=False`, no L2 flush or tensor rotation) and
records the
actual `timing_backend` (`cupti` or `cuda_graph`) and `cold_l2_cache` in
each CSV row.

### Speedup summary

| Head configuration | Nonpersistent median speedup | Persistent median
speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MHA 32/32 | 1.170× | 1.188× |
| GQA 32/8 | 1.171× | 1.185× |

Speedups are medians of exp2/expcast latency ratios across nine shapes,
both
masks and both QK modes (36 pairs per scheduler). 

### Accuracy

Accuracy uses untimed FP16 QK/PV/output exp2 attention with FP32
accumulation,
on dequantized Q/K and decoded V cast to FP16. This excludes original
input
quantization error. Δ RMSE is the increase over matched blockscaled
exp2's
relative RMSE against that reference, in percentage points (pp).

| Head configuration | Exp2 RMSE | ExpCast RMSE | Δ RMSE (pp) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MHA 32/32 | 2.076–2.620% | 2.479–3.133% | 0.403–0.514 |
| GQA 32/8 | 2.097–2.632% | 2.509–3.148% | 0.412–0.516 |

the summaries above cover the full sweeps.
Times are ms; speedup = exp2 / expcast; TFLOP/s counts QK+PV GEMMs with
causal masking.

## Reproduce

Set `Q_HEADS=32`, `KV_HEADS=32` (MHA) or `8` (GQA), and `OUTPUT` to a
separate
result file in the runner, then run in the activated CUDA/CuTe-DSL
environment:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python benchmarks/bench_blockscaled_expcast.py
```

The CSVs include NVFP4/MXFP8 blockscaled QK with exp2 and ExpCast, plus
a
regular BF16-QK exp2 baseline. All three use E4M3 FP8 PV. Results cover
MHA/GQA,
both masks and both schedulers, with timing and accuracy metrics against
the
FP16 reference.

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6296.
No linked issue.

### [6ae7f55](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/6ae7f55392527f3bbe5381af05804d377597c085)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:26:32Z
- **提交信息**: feat(cake_mla_value_gate): add an experimental fused MLA value projection + sigmoid gate (#8867)

This adds `cake_mla_value_gate`, an experimental FlashInfer primitive
for MLA decode. In one kernel it computes the value projection of the
merged BF16 latent `[B, H, 512]` with `W_UV` `[H, 512, 128]` (FP32
accumulation, explicit BF16 rounding), an FP32 sigmoid of the BF16 gate
logits, the multiply, and zeroing of rows with `valid_lengths <= 0`. It
writes a caller-owned BF16 `[B, H*128]` output that matches SGLang's
fused `MlaValue` consumer bit for bit. The first baseline is the
strongest FlashInfer composition: `bmm_bf16` on the strided latent view
(fastest per row among the auto, cudnn and tgv backends, autotuned or
not), then a `torch.compile`d FP32 sigmoid gate with valid-row zeroing.
The second is SGLang's fused `MlaValue` kernel
(sgl-project/sglang#48510), the consumer this primitive is proposed for
in #8795. On GB300 the new kernel is faster than the FlashInfer
composition on all 96 rows, at 1.29x-3.10x with per-mode medians of
1.82x (warm standalone), 2.28x (warm, behind PDL), 1.81x (cold
standalone) and 2.70x (cold, behind PDL). It is also faster than
`MlaValue` on all 96 rows, at 1.06x-1.53x with medians of 1.15x, 1.20x,
1.10x and 1.51x. On B200 it is faster than the FlashInfer composition on
all 96 rows, at 1.27x-3.02x with medians of 1.82x, 2.23x, 1.80x and
2.61x. Against `MlaValue` on B200 it ranges from 1.05x to 1.59x with
medians of 1.14x, 1.19x, 1.09x and 1.49x. It is faster on 95 rows and
within measurement noise on one (cold L2 standalone, contiguous, B = 1:
1.05x). On B300, the target GPU of sgl-project/sglang#48510, it is
faster than the FlashInfer composition on all 96 rows, at 1.28x-2.85x
with medians of 1.85x, 2.30x, 1.82x and 2.72x, and faster than
`MlaValue` on all 96 rows, at 1.06x-1.53x with medians of 1.15x, 1.20x,
1.10x and 1.50x.

NVIDIA GB300 (sm_103a), CUDA 13.4 toolkit, driver 580.159.03, H = 12
heads (Kimi-K3 TP8 decode), one query row per request, all rows valid;
median CUPTI time in µs of one complete call under CUDA graph replay,
with both baselines run in the same process on the same GPU with the
same inputs and output semantics; "behind PDL predecessor" = time the
call adds after a predecessor kernel that triggers programmatic
dependent launch; "pitch 3648" = gate logits as a strided row slice (row
pitch 3648 elements, as in SGLang), "contiguous" = gate rows of 1536
elements; speedup = baseline time / Cake time (> 1 means Cake is
faster).

### [a40d5c1](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/a40d5c1a93ecaeb90b360e7d6e7ba018d0ffd8d9)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:22:25Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_grouped_fp8_gemm): SM107a lead-prefetch BLOCK_N 256 for padding-heavy short-K layouts (#8881)

`cake_grouped_fp8_gemm` is Cake's prepared contiguous grouped FP8 GEMM.
On sm_100a and sm_103a it ships three variants: FP32-scale (promotion)
programs, block-scaled programs with packed UE8M0 scales, and a fused
gate_up + SwiGLU + FP8 quant form. On sm_107a it ships only the
block-scaled UE8M0 variant, and this PR changes only that variant. The
PR adds one sm_107a program: a BLOCK_N 256 single-run block-scaled UE8M0
program with a lead-prefetch table. On kernel entry, each CTA fills a
shared-memory table with the leading row index of each tile in its tile
walk. The tile loop then reads this table instead of global memory.
Walks longer than 224 tiles fall back to the global read. The host
routes to this program only on sm_107a, and only for alignment-128
layouts with at most 2 K blocks (K <= 256) whose valid M blocks are at
most 4/5 of the M blocks (padding-heavy layouts). Output bits are
identical to the previous program. The baseline is the previous Cake
route for these shapes: the BLOCK_N 256 program without the table.

Shapes whose route changes (alignment 128, G = 512 experts, top-k 10):

| Shape | M, N, K | valid rows | GPU (SMs) | before µs (hot) | this PR
µs (hot) | speedup hot (noise) | before µs (cooled) | this PR µs
(cooled) | speedup cooled (noise) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

12.93 | 1.7655 (0.14%) | 22.98 | 12.93 | 1.7683 (0.24%) |
| q397b_down_t1_a128 | 65152, 4096, 256 | 10 | R200 (212) | 22.62 |
12.90 | 1.7630 (0.00%) | 22.56 | 12.83 | 1.7624 (0.25%) |
| q397b_down_t8_a128 | 65152, 4096, 256 | 80 | R200 (216) | 30.24 |
22.98 | 1.3092 (0.14%) | 30.24 | 22.96 | 1.3115 (0.21%) |

22.26 | 1.3342 (0.15%) | 29.66 | 22.24 | 1.3324 (0.14%) |

42.18 | 1.1082 (0.08%) | 46.53 | 42.18 | 1.1078 (0.11%) |

GPU product NVIDIA R200, architecture sm_107a, CUDA 13.4. Before =
BLOCK_N 256 without the table, this PR = BLOCK_N 256 with the
lead-prefetch table. Each value is the median over operand seeds 21, 22
and 23, with L2 flushed and before/after runs paired and interleaved, in
hot and cooled windows. Speedup is the inverse of the reported
after/before ratio; above 1 is faster.

Every other shape of the 63-shape list keeps its route and program on
sm_107a, and sm_100a and sm_103a are unchanged.

### [27da1d4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/27da1d46824d3f26d647da979e76144469220fb8)

- **作者**: Brian K. Ryu
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T02:18:31Z
- **提交信息**: feat(batch_invariant): `mm_fp4(batch_invariant=True)`, the NVFP4 and MXFP4 GEMM classes (#8537)

<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re
needed. -->

Fifth PR of the batch-invariant GEMM series. `flashinfer.mm_fp4(a, b,
a_descale, b_descale, alpha, backend="auto", use_nvfp4=...,
batch_invariant=True)` runs a batch-invariant NVFP4 or MXFP4 GEMM in
place of the backends, with the mode's guarantee: an output row's bits
depend on the input values, their block scales, `alpha` and the weight
shape alone, not on the batch size, the row's position, the
configuration the dispatcher or the autotuner picks, the chunk count's
implementation or the SM count.

### Performance
**Untuned / autotuned speedup over the best FlashInfer backend (geomean
per regime; the class of the part)**

| part | format | class | decode (M <= 16) | mid (32 .. 1024) | prefill
(>= 1536) | all | cells >= 0.95 (untuned) | over `backend="auto"` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rubin NVL8 (SM107) | NVFP4 | `gemm.nvfp4.kfold128` (the split weight:
`gemm.nvfp4.kchunk2`) | 0.91 / 0.93 | 1.00 / 1.02 | 1.02 / 1.09 | 0.99 /
1.03 | 73 % | 0.95 / 0.99 |
| Rubin NVL8 (SM107) | MXFP4 | `gemm.mxfp4.kfold128` | 0.95 / 0.99 |
0.99 / 1.01 | 1.10 / 1.16 | 1.03 / 1.06 | 83 % | - |
| B200 (SM100) | NVFP4 | `gemm.nvfp4.kfold` | 0.87 / 0.89 | 0.90 / 0.91
| 0.89 / 0.95 | 0.89 / 0.92 | 33 % | 0.94 / 0.98 |
| B200 (SM100) | MXFP4 | `gemm.mxfp4.kfold` | 0.89 / 0.94 | 0.93 / 0.96
| 0.92 / 0.99 | 0.92 / 0.97 | 46 % | 1.00 / 1.05 |

**Which baseline wins the cell** (decode / mid / prefill cells, of 60 /
96 / 108). Rubin NVFP4: CuTe-DSL 60 / 84 / 85, cuDNN 0 / 12 / 23; Rubin
MXFP4: CuTe-DSL 58 / 96 / 108, the low-latency kernel 2 / 0 / 0 (cuDNN
and CUTLASS do not run MXFP4 there). B200 NVFP4: CuTe-DSL 60 / 69 / 21,
cuDNN 0 / 26 / 85, CUTLASS 0 / 1 / 2; B200 MXFP4: CuTe-DSL 60 / 93 / 85,
cuDNN 0 / 3 / 23. TRT-LLM wins no cell on either part.

Regimes: (1) decode (0.87-0.95) is where the CuTe-DSL kernels win every
cell, as for the other classes; the swapped decode records close most of
the gap (the NVFP4 spaces have no 64-wide token tile, so M = 33 .. 64
runs the dense tiles there). (2) Prefill on Rubin is above the backends
for both formats (1.02 / 1.09 and 1.10 / 1.16); on the B200 the untuned
picks trail the CuTe-DSL kernel and cuDNN by 8-11 % and the autotuner
recovers to 0.95 (NVFP4) and 0.99 (MXFP4), the same B200 prefill picture
as the fp8 and MXFP8 classes (the heuristic prefers a 1-CTA 256-wide
tile where the 2-CTA 192- / 256-wide ones are measured faster at the
large weights). (3) The split weight (512, 16384) is the worst column
(0.37-0.53 untuned against the CuTe-DSL split-K kernel and cuDNN;
autotuned 0.62-1.02): the chunk rule is a function of the weight shape
alone (R2 forbids an M-dependent split), so this weight runs with few
CTAs at small M and with a fixed two-chunk split at large M.

### [8af51e4](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/8af51e46aaecb6d0002f096f13f8f2465133dcb0)

- **作者**: eigen
- **时间**: 2026-11-06T01:59:10Z
- **提交信息**: perf(cake_kda_det_kcp): fused forward walk with the chunk output and 8 x 4 affine merge builds, bitwise identical (#8875)

`flashinfer.experimental.cake_kda_det_train_kcp` holds the deterministic
context-parallel (KCP) training kernels of KDA (Kimi Delta Attention).
This PR adds one new kernel, a fused forward state walk that also writes
the chunk output, and new builds of the affine merge. Outputs and
gradients are bitwise identical to main. The baseline in every table is
main, the previous Cake version of these kernels. Kernel ranges are
isolated kernel times.

- **Fused forward state walk with chunk output** (new): in the forward
pass it replaces the pair that main runs today, the forward state walk
that writes tapes and the output stage that reads them. It ships in two
builds: full-width (one CTA per head over the 128 value columns) and
two-CTA (two CTAs per head, 64 columns each). A per-architecture
head-count rule picks the build. sm_100a and sm_103a use the two-CTA
build up to 32 heads and the full-width build above. sm_107a uses a fit
rule up to 48 heads and the full-width build above. At 64 heads the
full-width build runs on all three and is 1.964-2.115x faster than the
pair on GB300, 1.965-2.119x on GB200 and 1.732-1.984x on R200. The
backward pass is unchanged.
- **Affine merge** (state merge across ranks): on sm_100a and sm_103a,
new 8 x 4 builds over 32 and 64 columns replace the 32-column 4 x 8 and
64-column 8 x 8 builds (T 21-40 and T > 56). On sm_107a the merge bands
change: the 16-column build runs at T = 24 and T >= 64, and the
32-column 8 x 4 build runs at T 32-48. 1.014-1.077x on GB300,
1.009-1.074x on GB200, 1.057-1.318x on R200.

End to end, the CP4 training step is 1.028-1.032x faster for fwd+bwd and
1.045-1.049x faster when checkpointed across GB300, GB200 and R200; the
forward alone is 1.077-1.092x faster, and the backward stays at
1.000-1.001x.

**End-to-end training step**: CP4 (4 ranks), 16384 tokens per rank, 64
heads (Q, K and V), per-document zigzag, Q/K L2 norm in the kernel.
Values are ms as main → this PR, with speedup = main / this PR. Both
sides were timed on the same node. CUDA 13.4, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.
